title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: During the overnight CustomerSync batch window (scheduled 01:00–04:00 PST), the Integration Gateway in us-west-2 began returning repeated 504 Gateway Timeout errors and API call durations exceeding 30 seconds when calling the downstream CRM API endpoint at api.customersync.corplabs.com. This was first reported by Priya Nair (Application Support lead, Portland office) after the Reporting Dashboard failed to refresh overnight customer records. Gateway logs on host INTGW-WEST-01.corplabs.internal showed a token refresh job failure (job ID: tknrot-20251201-0130) in the same time window, indicating the sync process was blocked by downstream authentication issues rather than a general platform outage. Approximately 14,200 customer records were delayed, impacting dependent reporting and sync workflows used by the finance reconciliation team.
root_cause: An expired downstream API token was left in use after the automated token rotation job failed. The Integration Gateway could no longer complete authenticated calls, which manifested as repeated timeout behavior during batch sync processing and delayed customer data updates.
resolution_steps: Validated the downstream API authentication path for service account svc-custsync-prod and manually rotated the expired API token on the Integration Gateway (INTGW-WEST-01.corplabs.internal) via the admin console to restore successful authenticated requests to api.customersync.corplabs.com. Rotation performed by Melissa Williams (mwilliams) at 21:02 UTC.

Restarted the gateway worker process on INTGW-WEST-01.corplabs.internal (PID 28417) to clear any stale authentication cache and ensure the new token was actively used by batch sync jobs. Post-restart, confirmed HTTP 200 responses with avg latency of 280ms on downstream calls.

Applied temporary retry and exponential backoff tuning on the Integration Gateway (max_retries: 5, initial_backoff: 2s, backoff_multiplier: 2.0) to reduce immediate job failures while authentication was being stabilized. Configuration change deployed by Derek Hollis (dhollis, Platform Engineering, Seattle office).

Corrected the failed automated token rotation job (tknrot-20251201-0130) by updating the rotation script's credential store path and added pre-expiry validation checks so future rotations confirm token acceptance at least 24 hours before the previous credential expires. Fix committed by dhollis and reviewed by Priya Nair.

Added alerting and dashboard visibility for token rotation failures via the Monitoring System (alert rule: TOKEN_ROTATION_FAIL, notify: appsupport-oncall@corplabs.com, pnair@corplabs.com) and post-change monitoring confirmed API success rates returned to 99.97% and sync latency returned to normal levels (p95: 1.2s) within 30 minutes of remediation.
agent_questions: Hi Priya — we found repeated 504 timeouts during the overnight CustomerSync batch on INTGW-WEST-01.corplabs.internal and a failed token refresh event (job tknrot-20251201-0130) in the same window. The service account svc-custsync-prod was returning AUTH_EXPIRED on downstream calls starting around 01:32 UTC. Can you confirm whether any token rotation or downstream API credential change occurred before the sync delays started? Also, was anyone else on your team — perhaps Raj Menon or the on-call engineer — aware of a scheduled credential update?

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts
description: CustomerDataSync scheduled sync jobs through the Integration Gateway began failing during the 02:00 UTC processing window on 2025-12-02. The affected integration, managed by backend engineer Priya Nair (EMP-40291), could not complete authenticated calls to the external CRM API endpoint from gateway worker pods running on host WORKSTATION-GWPOD-PN in the us-east-1 EKS environment. Monitoring dashboards showed repeated 401 Unauthorized token_expired responses for service account svc-custsync followed by 504 Gateway Timeout errors as retries accumulated. This blocked timely customer data synchronization and increased backlog in the gateway worker queue, with over 1,200 pending sync jobs reported by 02:30 UTC. The issue was initially flagged by Monitoring System alert ALERT-SYNC-7744 and escalated to the integration operations team at ext 4085.
root_cause: The Integration Gateway service account token expired, causing 401 Unauthorized token_expired responses from the external API. The gateway continued retrying failed authentication attempts until jobs exhausted retries and surfaced as 504 timeouts, which created a processing backlog for scheduled syncs.
resolution_steps: Validated that the external CRM API itself was healthy via Monitoring System synthetic probes and direct latency checks from 10.42.17.88, and confirmed the primary failure pattern was authentication-related 401 token_expired responses for service account svc-custsync rather than a downstream service outage.

Rotated the expired Integration Gateway service account token for svc-custsync via Vault (new token issued 2025-12-02T02:48:00Z) and updated the active secret used by the gateway worker pods igw-worker-01 through igw-worker-04 for outbound API authentication.

Restarted the Integration Gateway worker pods (igw-worker-01 through igw-worker-04) on node 10.42.17.88 so they would load the new svc-custsync token and clear stuck retry state from previously failed sync attempts. Restart completed by 02:52 UTC.

Verified successful authenticated API calls after the token update by reviewing gateway response logs, and monitored backlog processing with Marcus Ellison until the 1,450+ delayed sync jobs drained normally by approximately 03:40 UTC.

Added token-expiry alerting in Monitoring System to notify the backend-syncers group (priya.nair@corplabs.com, mellison@corplabs.com) 14 days before TTL expiration, scheduled automatic token rotation at 60-day intervals for svc-custsync, then adjusted retry and backoff behavior (max retries reduced to 3, exponential backoff ceiling set to 30s) to reduce cascading timeout conditions if authentication fails again.
agent_questions: We are seeing 401 Unauthorized and 504 timeout errors during the scheduled sync window on the Integration Gateway pods in us-east-1. Reviewing logs from gateway node igw-worker-04 (10.42.17.88) confirms the failures are tied to service account svc-custsync. Priya, please confirm whether there was any recent token or secret rotation change for the Integration Gateway service account, and whether the credentials stored in Vault path secret/integrations/custsync were updated in the last 90 days.

title: API integration timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: Overnight scheduled data synchronization jobs between the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east.corplabs.internal) and the downstream Inventory API service intermittently failed from approximately 02:00 to 03:30 UTC on 2025-12-02 in us-east-1. The gateway received repeated 504 Gateway Timeout and ETIMEDOUT responses on the /api/v2/inventory/sync endpoint, which delayed application data updates and increased integration job failures. Reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Chicago operations center — internal operations needed the scheduled sync process to complete normally so downstream application records would be current by the start of business.
root_cause: Elevated latency on the downstream service caused API responses to exceed the Integration Gateway timeout window, resulting in intermittent 504 Gateway Timeout errors and failed scheduled sync jobs.
resolution_steps: Correlated the failed sync window (02:00–03:30 UTC) with Integration Gateway latency metrics on igw-prod-east (node 10.42.18.55), Jaeger API traces for the /api/v2/inventory/sync endpoint, and downstream Inventory API endpoint health to confirm the timeout condition was external to the scheduler itself. Analysis performed by Priya Nair (pnair).

Escalated the incident to the downstream Inventory API service owners — Rafael Ortega (rortega@corplabs.com, phone 312-555-0147) at the Austin office — with captured request traces, timeout evidence (47 failed jobs, p99 latency 45s), and the affected overnight time window for remediation.

Applied a temporary increase to the Integration Gateway timeout threshold from 30s to 90s on the igw-prod-east configuration (ConfigMap igw-timeout-override) so requests could complete during the period of elevated downstream latency. Change approved by team lead Jenna Whitfield (jwhitfield, EMP-30295).

Adjusted retry and backoff settings on the Integration Gateway — increased max retries from 3 to 5 and exponential backoff base from 1s to 2s — to reduce immediate job failure rates and improve recovery for intermittent downstream slow responses. Configuration deployed to igw-prod-east pods via Helm update.

Re-ran and validated the 47 previously affected synchronization jobs (sync-inv-20251202-0200 through sync-inv-20251202-0330) after downstream latency stabilized at approximately 06:15 UTC, confirming successful completion and normal data propagation to the order-fulfillment application. Validated by Marcus Delgado from the Chicago operations center.

Removed the temporary timeout increase (reverted igw-prod-east ConfigMap to 30s default) after stability was confirmed at 09:00 UTC and kept Monitoring System alerting in place to verify that 504 and timeout rates returned to baseline. Post-incident review scheduled with Rafael Ortega's team for 2025-12-04.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing failed sync jobs
description: Customers were trying to run scheduled data synchronization through the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east-01), but starting around 2025-12-02 03:10 UTC the gateway began returning repeated 504 Gateway Timeout errors on downstream API calls to the Order Fulfillment API Service. Two scheduled sync jobs (sync-job-4417 and sync-job-4418, owned by svc-integrations) failed, data delivery to the Application was delayed by over 3 hours, and monitoring reported elevated latency and timeout alerts in us-east-1. Confirmed authenticated API requests from igw-prod-east-01 (10.42.17.88) completed successfully after the secret update, with response times returning to baseline ~200ms, and removed reliance on the temporary timeout increase as the primary mitigation.

Re-ran queued sync jobs (sync-job-4417 and sync-job-4418) and verified previously failed synchronization jobs completed successfully without further 504 errors. Marcus Delgado confirmed data delivery to the Application was restored and consistent.

Updated the token rotation policy to enforce automated renewal 14 days before expiry via Vault auto-rotate and reviewed secret management ownership for the integration path, assigning Raj Venkatesh as the designated secret owner for the igw-prod-east-01 integration credentials.

Adjusted retry and backoff behavior on igw-prod-east-01 from linear (5s fixed interval, 10 retries) to exponential backoff (initial 2s, max 60s, 5 retries) so future transient downstream issues are less likely to surface as repeated gateway timeouts. Configuration change reviewed by Priya Nair.

title: Integration Gateway - scheduled job timeouts

title: Integration Gateway timeouts causing delayed data sync to downstream service
description: Nightly batch data synchronization from DataSyncApp (service account svc-datasync) through the Integration Gateway to the downstream InventoryAPI service began failing between 03:20 and 03:50 UTC on 2025-12-03. The API Service running on pod datasyncapp-worker-7b in namespace appsync-prod (us-east-1) received repeated HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout responses, and at least one scheduled sync job (sync-20251203-batch4) failed, delaying data availability for downstream consumers in the Chicago fulfillment group. Investigation by Marcus Ellison showed the gateway was still referencing a deprecated retry/backoff policy (v1.2) while downstream latency was elevated, causing retries to amplify timeout behavior rather than allowing the batch to complete. Reported initially by Priya Nagarajan via the Application Support on-call channel.
root_cause: Elevated downstream service latency caused upstream request timeouts, and the impact was amplified because the Integration Gateway was still using a stale deprecated retry/backoff policy that extended retry behavior beyond the effective integration window.
resolution_steps: Replaced the deprecated Integration Gateway retry policy v1.2 (rtpol-0012-deprecated) with the supported v1.3 production configuration on gw-east-prod-01.corplabs.internal in the appsync-prod namespace, applied by Marcus Ellison.

Updated gateway retry behavior to exponential backoff with jitter (base 2s, max 16s, jitter factor 0.5) and reduced the cumulative retry window from 180s to 60s to avoid amplifying downstream latency spikes against InventoryAPI.
Maintained the temporary timeout increase (30s → 45s) only during recovery validation of sync-20251203-batch4-retry, then aligned runtime settings with the corrected retry policy v1.3 defaults.

Coordinated with the downstream InventoryAPI team lead Daniel Okafor (E-40291) to review and mitigate the latency condition observed during the 03:20–03:50 UTC failure window; downstream team confirmed a database connection pool exhaustion event on their side.

Validated successful end-to-end batch sync completion across the next two scheduled runs (sync-20251204-batch4 and sync-20251205-batch4) and monitored gateway 504 and latency metrics on the Monitoring System for 24 hours — zero 504s observed post-fix.

Documented the policy correction in runbook RB-APPSYNC-017 and added guidance to verify retry-policy version references (current: v1.3) during future timeout incidents. Notification sent to appsupport-oncall@corplabs.com and Priya Nagarajan for awareness.
agent_questions: Reviewing the nightly sync failure window now. Can you confirm whether the issue is isolated to timeout responses from the Integration Gateway, or if you also see authentication or rate-limit errors? I'm pulling logs from gw-east-prod-01.corplabs.internal for the 03:00–04:00 UTC window. Also, Priya, can you verify which service account identity DataSyncApp is using — is it svc-datasync or was it recently rotated?

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: Customer-facing integration jobs between the Application and the downstream partner API (PartnerSync endpoint at partner-api.extdata.io) intermittently failed over the last 90 minutes during peak traffic. The Integration Gateway node igw-prod-07 in us-east-1 returned repeated HTTP 504 timeout responses on outbound partner API calls originating from service account svc-integrations, which caused inbound API Service requests to queue on the api-ingest-pool cluster, retries to accumulate, and data synchronization for the nightly billing feed to be delayed rather than completed in the expected 06:00–07:30 UTC window. Reported by Marcus Ellison (emp ID EMP-40821) from the Denver office.
root_cause: Most likely cause was intermittent latency and capacity degradation on the downstream partner API during peak traffic, causing outbound calls from the Integration Gateway to exceed the original timeout threshold and return HTTP 504 responses. Token rotation was not identified as causal because authentication monitoring showed no token expiry, authentication failure, or rate-limit pattern.
resolution_steps: Validated that the integration token for service account svc-integrations remained accepted by the downstream API at partner-api.extdata.io and confirmed no authentication expiry or auth-failure pattern was present in Monitoring System auth event logs.

Increased the Integration Gateway outbound call timeout threshold on igw-prod-07 from 30s to 60s to better match observed downstream response latency during peak traffic windows (p99 8.2s with tail spikes beyond 30s).

Applied an exponential retry backoff policy (initial interval 2s, max 32s, jitter enabled) to the svc-integrations job configuration to reduce retry amplification and request queue buildup on api-ingest-pool while the downstream API was slow to respond.

Restarted affected Integration Gateway pods (igw-prod-07, igw-prod-08) via kubectl rollout to clear 1,842 queued work items and restore normal processing after the timeout policy update. Confirmed queue depth returned to baseline (~120) within 10 minutes.

Escalated the incident to the downstream service owner at extdata.io (contact: Raj Mehta, rmehta@extdata.io) with collected HTTP 504 examples, latency traces, and Monitoring System evidence for capacity and latency investigation, while continuing post-change monitoring via the Monitoring System alerting channel for recurrence.
agent_questions: We are seeing repeated HTTP 504 responses on outbound partner API calls from Integration Gateway pod igw-prod-07. Reviewing traces for service account svc-integrations shows the failures cluster between 06:12 and 07:36 UTC. Please confirm whether the sync delays line up with peak job volume on the nightly billing feed and whether any partner-side maintenance or slowdown was reported. I've also asked Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) on the platform team to pull the Monitoring System dashboards for the affected window.

title: API timeouts causing nightly sync failures
description: Nightly data synchronization for the Reporting Application began failing around 03:10 UTC on 2025-12-03 when POST requests to /v1/sync started returning 504 Gateway Timeout. Impacted components include the Integration Gateway and API Service running in the EKS environment in us-east-1. The issue was initially reported by Daniel Okoye (emp ID E-40291) from the Chicago office after the morning reporting dashboards showed stale data.
root_cause: Expired API token used by the Integration Gateway caused authentication failures during token refresh, which led to repeated retries, elevated latency, and eventual 504 timeouts on /v1/sync during the nightly reporting sync window.
resolution_steps: Rotated the expired API token for service account svc-reporting-sync used by the Integration Gateway and updated the Kubernetes secret (reporting-sync-token) in the igw-prod namespace with the replacement credential, performed by Marcus Reeves.

Restarted affected Integration Gateway pods (igw-worker-7c4d9, igw-worker-8a2f3) so all running instances loaded the new token from the updated Kubernetes secret and cleared stale authentication state.

Validated successful authentication handshakes between the Integration Gateway (client IP 10.42.17.88) and API Service on apisvc-prod-east.corplabs.internal, and confirmed sync requests on POST /v1/sync were returning HTTP 200 responses instead of 504 errors. Verification performed by Daniel Okoye and Liang Chen.

Reviewed and updated token rotation controls for svc-reporting-sync to enforce automated renewal 72 hours before expiration via the Vault secrets engine, and added PagerDuty alerting for upcoming token expiry conditions targeting the on-call rotation for Platform Engineering (current on-call: Marcus Reeves, m.reeves@corplabs.com).

Adjusted gateway retry and exponential backoff behavior on the Integration Gateway (max retries reduced from 10 to 3, initial backoff set to 500ms with 2x multiplier, max backoff capped at 4s) to reduce cascading timeout impact during downstream latency spikes and authentication failures. Configuration change reviewed by Priya Nambiar and deployed via Helm chart update.
agent_questions: Hi Daniel — please confirm whether the failed nightly syncs all target POST /v1/sync and whether you are seeing authentication-related errors (specifically token_expired) in the Integration Gateway logs for service account svc-reporting-sync near the start of the 504s. Also, can you verify the client IP 10.42.17.88 is the expected source for the sync jobs? You can reach me at l.chen@corplabs.com if you need to share log bundles offline.

title: Intermittent API timeouts on Integration Gateway causing delayed data sync
description: Users in the Finance and Operations group were trying to sync data through the Integration Gateway (gw-integ-prod-east.corplabs.internal) to the API Service endpoint, but intermittent 504 Gateway Timeout responses and elevated request latency caused delayed synchronization and failed integration jobs. The issue was reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) and affects the Linux-hosted integration path in us-east-1, where jobs were timing out after 30 seconds and backlog had to be cleared manually. The affected client workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (IP 10.42.17.88) was used for initial troubleshooting. A gateway restart did not provide sustained improvement, and token validity plus downstream API health initially remained unconfirmed. Ticket escalated internally by Derek Owens (EMP-40291).
root_cause: Primary cause was downstream API latency periodically exceeding the Integration Gateway request timeout window, which produced intermittent 504 errors and delayed sync processing. Token expiration could not be confirmed from the original intake, but available evidence favored timeout sensitivity to elevated downstream response times rather than an authentication failure.
resolution_steps: Validated the integration path against gateway monitoring on gw-integ-prod-east.corplabs.internal and confirmed that request latency spikes were breaching the original 30 second timeout window during affected sync periods (18:45–19:10 UTC on 2025-12-03), as reported by Maria Chen and Priya Nair.

Increased the Integration Gateway request timeout from the prior 30 second setting to 60 seconds on gw-integ-prod-east.corplabs.internal so transient downstream latency no longer caused immediate 504 failures for normal sync traffic. Change applied by Raj Patel (rpatel).

Updated retry behavior for service account svc-integ-sync to use controlled exponential backoff (initial 2s, max 32s, jitter enabled) so repeated calls during latency spikes would not rapidly exhaust retries or compound queue congestion on the us-east-1 integration path.

Cleared and reprocessed the pending retry backlog (approximately 47 queued jobs) after the timeout and retry configuration changes were applied to restore delayed synchronization jobs. Confirmed completion with Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com).

Continued post-change monitoring of gateway latency and 504 volume on gw-integ-prod-east.corplabs.internal via the Monitoring System and confirmed reduced failure frequency over the following 4-hour observation window, with guidance to escalate to downstream service owners if sustained latency again exceeds the adjusted 60-second timeout threshold. Derek Owens (EMP-40291) assigned as point of contact for any recurrence.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please confirm whether the API client token associated with service account svc-integ-sync was recently rotated or expired, and provide any gateway request IDs tied to the 504 errors along with the latest latency graphs from the Monitoring System dashboard. Also, can you verify whether the issue is isolated to your workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC or if other team members in the Arlington office are also affected? Please loop in Derek Owens (dowens@corplabs.com) if he has additional context from the Operations side.

title: Integration Gateway API calls timing out causing integration job failures
description: Integration jobs for the reporting application (managed by the Data Integration team under Marcus Delgado) began failing around 09:12 UTC on 2025-12-04 when API calls routed through the Integration Gateway on host INTGW-AKS-PROD-01 started timing out. The issue was first reported by analyst Priya Nair (emp ID DI-40287) who observed delayed real-time data syncs and failed nightly ingestion runs from her workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN (IP 10.42.18.93). Application and gateway logs showed repeated 504 Gateway Timeout errors, and the Monitoring System dashboard indicated rising downstream latency and elevated error responses from the external analytics API endpoint. The outage affected the API integration path used by the reporting application and blocked normal data synchronization for the Austin office until the downstream rate-limit condition was mitigated.
observed_errors: integration job error: timeout waiting for response
root_cause: The downstream API enforced rate limits against the integration client, producing sustained 429 Too Many Requests responses. Gateway retries accumulated under elevated latency, exhausted the effective timeout window, and resulted in 504 Gateway Timeout errors that caused integration job failures and delayed data syncs.
resolution_steps: Reviewed Integration Gateway traces on INTGW-AKS-PROD-01 and Monitoring System dashboards to confirm the timeout pattern was driven by repeated downstream 429 responses (1,247 occurrences) and increasing response latency (p99 >28s) rather than an internal gateway failure. Analysis performed by Raymond Chen (rchen) with input from Priya Nair.

Applied temporary exponential backoff (initial delay 2s, max 60s, jitter enabled) and adjusted the Integration Gateway retry policy on INTGW-AKS-PROD-01 to cap retries at 3 attempts, reducing immediate retry storms while preserving successful completion for delayed downstream responses.

Coordinated with the downstream analytics API owner (contact: Tomás Rivera, trivera@partnerapi.net) to increase the request quota for integration client ID intg-rpt-prod-east from 200 req/min to 500 req/min after confirming sustained rate-limit enforcement against the Austin integration path.

Replayed the failed ingestion job RPT-INGEST-0412 and real-time synchronization jobs after the quota increase was confirmed at 11:02 UTC, and verified that all requests completed successfully without recurring gateway 504 errors. Priya Nair (pnair) confirmed data sync restored on her workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN.

Updated the Integration Gateway retry and backoff policy for the reporting integration path on INTGW-AKS-PROD-01 and added Monitoring System alerting thresholds for 429 spike detection (>20 per 5-min window) and downstream latency growth (p95 >5s) to detect recurrence earlier. Alert recipients set to mdelgado@corplabs.com and rchen@corplabs.com.
agent_questions: Hi Priya — please confirm whether the downstream responses you're seeing show HTTP 429 or other 5xx status codes. Also, can you share the last successful job timing from the Data Ingestion Pipeline so we can determine whether this is a latency degradation or a rate-limit issue? You can pull the trace IDs from the Integration Gateway logs on INTGW-AKS-PROD-01 or forward them to me at r.chen@corplabs.com. — Raymond Chen

title: Intermittent API timeouts from Integration Gateway with conflicting token/latency evidence
description: Scheduled internal batch jobs using the Integration Gateway (gateway cluster igw-prod-east-01) began failing intermittently after a recent deploy (build 4.7.2-rc3, deployed 2025-12-04T03:45Z), causing delayed data synchronization and missed downstream deliveries over an approximately 3-hour window starting around 04:00 UTC. The issue was reported by Marcus Ellison (mellison@corplabs.com) from the Atlanta data operations team, who noticed that several overnight ETL batches tied to service account svc-batch-integ failed to complete. Gateway monitoring showed repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses aligned with elevated downstream service latency on the Order Fulfillment API endpoint (/api/v2/orders/sync). Some client traces from host WORKSTATION-BATCH-ME also showed 401 Unauthorized responses, indicating a secondary token validity issue that complicated diagnosis.
root_cause: Primary cause was elevated downstream service latency causing the Integration Gateway to exceed its timeout window and return intermittent 504 responses after the deploy. A secondary expired or stale API token condition was also present on some client calls, producing intermittent 401 errors, but this was not the dominant driver of the batch failure spike.
resolution_steps: Validated the failure window (04:00–07:00 UTC) against Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east-01) and downstream Order Fulfillment API latency metrics in the Monitoring System to confirm the timeout pattern was primarily latency-driven (p99 >12s vs. 5s gateway timeout) rather than a full authentication outage.

Rotated the integration API token for service account svc-batch-integ to remove the intermittent expired or stale credential condition seen in client traces from 10.42.18.77 (WORKSTATION-BATCH-ME), and updated the credential in the gateway's secret store.

Increased Integration Gateway retry count from 2 to 4 and adjusted exponential backoff settings (initial delay from 500ms to 1500ms, max delay from 3s to 10s) on igw-prod-east-01 so transient downstream latency spikes would not immediately fail scheduled batch requests.

Cleared the gateway request queue (approximately 180 backed-up requests) and restarted the affected gateway pod igw-worker-7b4c to remove backed-up requests created during the latency spike. Darren Cho from the platform team confirmed pod health post-restart.

Escalated the downstream latency condition to the Downstream Service Team (contact: Raj Patel, rpatel@corplabs.com) with aligned gateway logs from igw-prod-east-01 and Monitoring System performance evidence for service-side remediation, while keeping monitoring alerts in place to verify timeout reduction after the gateway changes. Follow-up review scheduled for 2025-12-05.
agent_questions: We are seeing both 504 timeout spikes at the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east-01) and some 401 responses in client traces originating from 10.42.18.77. Can you confirm whether failures started after the 4.7.2-rc3 deploy at 03:45 UTC and whether all batches are affected or only a subset of integrations? We'd also like to know if the service account svc-batch-integ credentials were refreshed as part of the deployment. — Priya Nair, Application Support

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: Nightly integration jobs from the Integration Gateway (pod ig-prod-worker-07 on cluster k8s-east-prod) to the downstream API Service were delayed between 23:50–00:15 UTC on 2025-12-04 in us-east-1. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Dallas application support team after the overnight data synchronization workflow failed to complete on schedule. Monitoring System dashboards showed repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses and 401 token_expired errors originating from service account svc-ig-sync, causing queued sync jobs to fail and data ingestion to lag by over 25 minutes. The blocked task was the overnight data synchronization workflow feeding the Ingestion Worker pipeline, with impact to downstream application data freshness for the finance and analytics consumers until authentication and retry behavior were corrected.
root_cause: Expired API credential on the Integration Gateway caused token refresh failures, leading to 401 token_expired responses and subsequent downstream call timeouts during the nightly sync window.
resolution_steps: Rotated the expired API token for service account svc-ig-sync configured on the Integration Gateway pod ig-prod-worker-07 and confirmed the gateway could successfully authenticate to the downstream API Service at https://api.corplabs.internal/v2/ingest. Rotation performed by Rachel Nguyen (rng0042) at approximately 00:18 UTC.

Validated that token refresh operations for svc-ig-sync completed successfully after the credential update by reviewing gateway logs on ig-prod-worker-07 and confirming that new API requests no longer returned 401 token_expired errors.

Cleared and reprocessed 14 affected integration queue items so delayed nightly sync jobs could resume with valid authentication; Marcus Delgado (E-50821) confirmed data freshness was restored for downstream finance and analytics consumers by 00:32 UTC.

Updated the token_refresh_policy for svc-ig-sync to enforce automated renewal checks 7 days before credential expiry and configured a Monitoring System alert to notify the Dallas application support team (appsupp-dallas@corplabs.com) before credential expiration to prevent recurrence.

Adjusted the integration retry and backoff configuration on ig-prod-worker-07 from a fixed 5s interval to exponential backoff (initial 2s, max 120s, jitter enabled) to better tolerate transient downstream latency without exhausting jobs during the nightly sync window.

Monitored logs and Monitoring System metrics for 24 hours after remediation to confirm normal API latency on the /v2/ingest endpoint, successful sync completion for all scheduled jobs, and no further 401 or 504 spikes. Rachel Nguyen signed off on the 24-hour observation at 2025-12-05T13:00:00Z.

title: Nightly integration timeouts via Integration Gateway (03:00 UTC)
description: Nightly batch data sync jobs sent through the Integration Gateway to the downstream partner (Acme Data Services) are failing around 03:00 UTC in us-east-1. The gateway returns 504 Gateway Timeout for POST /sync during the scheduled run window, and monitoring shows a matching latency spike at the same time. This is delaying the partner data synchronization workflow for batch-sync-users. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Dallas integration operations team. Current telemetry is incomplete because request correlation IDs and token rotation history were not available in the original evidence. The affected API client ID is intg-client-batch-7741, and the integration service account username is svc_batchsync. Requests originate from host WORKSTATION-INTGOPS-MD (10.42.18.97).
root_cause: Downstream API latency during the 03:00 UTC batch window exceeded the Integration Gateway timeout window, producing 504 Gateway Timeout responses for POST /sync. Token expiry was considered but not supported by available evidence because gateway and API log review found no authentication failures or 401 errors.
resolution_steps: Correlated the nightly failure window (03:00–03:12 UTC on 2025-12-04) with Monitoring System data (alert group intg-latency-critical) and confirmed that elevated downstream latency (p95 of 45s) aligned with the Integration Gateway 504 responses for POST /sync around 03:00 UTC on gateway node gw-east-01. Analysis performed by Kevin Ortiz (kortiz) using source IP 10.42.18.97 request logs.

Reviewed Integration Gateway (gw-east-01) and API Service logs for authentication failures and token-related errors for service account svc_batchsync / client ID intg-client-batch-7741; no 401 responses or explicit token rejection events were present, reducing likelihood of expired credentials as the primary cause. Confirmed by Priya Nair (pnair).

Classified the incident as downstream latency (Acme Data Services partner endpoint) exceeding the 15-second gateway timeout window rather than an authentication failure and prepared evidence package for service owner escalation. Rachel Simmons (rsimmons, EMP-41503) approved the classification.

Escalated the recurring 03:00 UTC latency condition to the downstream service owners/vendor (Acme Data Services, vendor ticket ref: ACME-INC-2291) for remediation of the partner-side performance issue during the batch sync window. Escalation contact: Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) designated as corplabs liaison.

Recommended increasing retry/backoff tolerance (from 2 retries with 5s backoff to 4 retries with exponential backoff up to 60s) or adjusting the gateway timeout window from 15s to 45s for the nightly sync path as an operational mitigation until the downstream latency issue is corrected. Change request to be submitted by Kevin Ortiz (kortiz) pending approval from the Dallas integration operations team.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please provide the API client ID (confirmed intg-client-batch-7741), last token rotation date for svc_batchsync, and a sample request ID or precise failure timestamp so we can correlate gateway events with monitoring traces and rule out credential issues. Also looping in Priya Nair (pnair) from the API platform team to assist with downstream trace analysis. You can reach her at pnair@corplabs.com. — Kevin Ortiz, Integration Support (EMP-60738)

title: Intermittent API timeouts from Integration Gateway causing delayed data sync
description: Application support engineer Priya Nair (emp ID: E-40291) reported delayed synchronization between the CRM Application and the third-party Salesforce Data API beginning around 2025-12-05 09:00 UTC. Intermittent 504 Gateway Timeout responses were returned by the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east.corplabs.internal), causing some scheduled API integration jobs to fail or complete late. Monitoring System dashboards showed correlated spikes in outbound latency from the gateway to the downstream API endpoint https://api.partnersync.io/v2/data. A gateway pod restart on node igw-worker-04 and temporary timeout increase from 30s to 90s did not remove the issue, and available logs on the gateway did not show clear token expiry errors or enough detail to distinguish between rate limiting and downstream latency. Ticket raised from the Arlington office.
root_cause: Primary cause was downstream API latency causing Integration Gateway requests to exceed the configured timeout window, with incomplete gateway access logging and missing token rotation context initially delaying confirmation. Token expiry was not supported by available evidence, and the existing retry/backoff behavior was insufficient to absorb intermittent latency spikes without causing job failures.
resolution_steps: Collected and correlated Integration Gateway timeout events from igw-prod-east.corplabs.internal with Monitoring System data for the incident window (2025-12-05 09:00–11:00 UTC) to confirm that 504 responses aligned with outbound latency spikes to the downstream API at https://api.partnersync.io/v2/data rather than gateway pod health issues on igw-worker-04.

Validated available authentication evidence for service account svc-apisync and reviewed token age and rotation details with Tomás Rivera to rule out an obvious expired or recently changed API credential as the trigger for the timeouts.

Adjusted the integration retry and backoff behavior in the apijobs-prod namespace configuration (max retries increased from 3 to 5, exponential backoff base raised from 2s to 5s) to better tolerate intermittent slow downstream responses and reduce immediate scheduled job failures during latency spikes.

Kept the increased request timeout (90s, up from the default 30s) in place as a temporary mitigation only where needed to allow delayed sync jobs (crm-daily-sync, inventory-hourly-push) additional time to complete during downstream slowness.

Escalated the latency pattern and 504 evidence to the downstream API provider PartnerSync for investigation of service responsiveness and any request-throttling conditions affecting the Integration Gateway, coordinated by Janet Cho (jcho@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office.
agent_questions: We confirmed repeated 504 responses from the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east.corplabs.internal) with matching outbound latency spikes visible in Monitoring System between 09:02 and 10:47 UTC. Hi Priya — please provide gateway access logs for the incident window and confirm the API token age or any recent credential rotation for service account svc-apisync so we can rule out auth or throttling issues. Also, can you confirm whether the integration jobs running under namespace apijobs-prod were all affected or only specific sync schedules? — Marcus Delgado, Integration Support

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: Nightly DataSync integration jobs submitted by the application_support team (contact: r.martinez@corplabs.com) were attempting to send customer records through the Integration Gateway (gateway node igw-prod-east-07) to the downstream API service, but starting around 02:10 UTC on 2025-12-05 the gateway began receiving repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses from the API endpoint and requests exceeded the configured 30 second client timeout. This caused job failures across the DataSync worker pool running on host WORKSTATION-DSYNC-RM, queue growth in the integration worker (queue depth exceeded 4,200 pending messages), and delayed customer data synchronization for the Chicago processing region until retries or manual recovery actions completed. Incident was initially reported by Rafael Martinez (EMP-80241) via the on-call pager.
root_cause: Elevated latency on the downstream API service caused Integration Gateway requests to exceed the configured 30 second timeout, resulting in repeated 504 responses, retry accumulation, and delayed sync processing.
resolution_steps: Correlated the nightly job failure window (02:10–03:45 UTC) with downstream API latency metrics from the Monitoring System and confirmed Integration Gateway requests on igw-prod-east-07 from client IP 10.42.17.93 were timing out at the 30 second threshold during sustained 504 responses — 347 failures logged for service account svc-datasync.

Escalated the incident to the downstream service SRE team (contact: Yuki Tanaka, ytanaka@corplabs.com) for capacity and latency investigation under ticket SRE-4521 and provided timing, error-rate, p95 latency charts, and queue backlog evidence from the Monitoring System covering the 02:10–03:45 UTC window.

Applied a temporary mitigation by increasing the Integration Gateway timeout on igw-prod-east-07 from 30 seconds to 45 seconds to reduce immediate job failures while the downstream latency issue was being investigated. Change applied by agent dkumar and confirmed across all 3 gateway replicas in us-east-1.

Updated the gateway retry policy to exponential backoff with jitter (base interval 2s, max interval 60s, jitter factor 0.5) to reduce retry amplification against the slow downstream API and improve recovery behavior. Configuration change documented by dkumar in the Integration Gateway runbook.

Restarted the integration gateway worker on WORKSTATION-DSYNC-RM to clear 4,200+ stalled requests and allow queued sync jobs to resume processing under the temporary timeout and retry settings. Worker restart performed by Rafael Martinez (EMP-80241) with confirmation from agent dkumar.

Expanded monitoring via the Monitoring System to track end-to-end API latency, 504 error rate, and worker queue depth with alerting thresholds (p95 latency > 10s, 504 rate > 5%, queue depth > 500) so future downstream degradation can be detected and escalated earlier. Alert recipients configured for r.martinez@corplabs.com and powens@corplabs.com.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: Overnight integration jobs for DataSyncApp were delayed or failed when the Integration Gateway in Kubernetes (us-east-1) experienced repeated HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout responses while calling the downstream API Service. The issue was first reported by platform engineer Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) at approximately 06:15 UTC after reviewing the nightly batch run from the Arlington data center. Monitoring and traces showed sustained downstream response time increases above the gateway timeout window, which created retries, backlog growth, and delayed customer data synchronization. Affected gateway pods were running on nodes WORKSTATION-GWNODE-MD in the integration namespace. The incident impacted sync jobs servicing accounts managed by the platform-engineering user group.
root_cause: Sustained downstream API Service latency exceeded the Integration Gateway timeout window, causing HTTP 504 responses, retries, and overnight job backlog.
resolution_steps: Validated that the failure pattern aligned with elevated downstream API latency rather than gateway pod instability by reviewing timeout errors, trace latency, and job failure correlation. Agent Priya Nair (pnair) cross-referenced Monitoring System trace spans with DataSyncApp job scheduler logs from the Arlington cluster to confirm that all 847 failed jobs mapped to downstream latency spikes exceeding the 10-second timeout.

Applied a temporary mitigation on the Integration Gateway by increasing the request timeout from 10 seconds to 30 seconds and tuning retry/backoff behavior to reduce immediate job failures during transient latency spikes. Configuration change was committed by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) and deployed via the platform-engineering CI/CD pipeline at 12:08 UTC.

Scaled the Integration Gateway deployment by two pods to reduce queueing pressure and restarted a limited subset of pods to clear transient worker errors while preserving service availability. The additional pods were scheduled on nodes in the Arlington availability zone and confirmed healthy by Priya Nair via the Monitoring System pod readiness dashboard at 12:15 UTC.

Escalated the confirmed downstream latency issue to the API Service owning team for remediation of the slow response condition that was driving 504s. Escalation ticket INC-AIT-0025-ESC was assigned to Jonathan Reeves (jreeves) at the Columbus service center, with Gold SLA priority and a 4-hour response commitment.

Updated alerting and correlation logging so downstream latency spikes, 504 rates, and integration backlog growth can be identified together and acted on earlier. New composite alert rules were configured in the Monitoring System by Marcus Delgado to trigger when p50 downstream latency exceeds 8 seconds concurrently with 504 error rate above 5% over a 5-minute window.

Monitored the environment for 4 hours after mitigation and confirmed a reduction in HTTP 504 occurrences and stabilization of integration job completion. Priya Nair verified via the Monitoring System that p50 latency returned to 1.8 seconds and the DataSyncApp backlog cleared by 16:30 UTC, with zero additional job failures observed from gateway pod IP 10.42.17.93.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed sync
description: Scheduled analytics integration jobs from the Integration Gateway (gateway-prod-analytics.corplabs.internal) to the downstream API service began failing over the last 2 hours with repeated HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout responses. The issue was first reported by Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) from the analytics team in Charlotte. Retries were exhausted and downstream data synchronization for the analytics application was delayed, affecting automated reporting pipelines. Gateway logs on host INTGW-NODE-04 and the Monitoring System showed upstream latency spikes above the normal 3-second timeout window in Kubernetes in us-east-1, impacting automated sync completion rather than a single I action. The integration service account analytics_sync_svc was used for all failing requests originating from pod IP 10.42.17.88.
root_cause: Downstream API service latency intermittently exceeded the Integration Gateway request timeout window, producing HTTP 504 timeouts and exhausting job retries. Token validity was verified by rotation and post-change behavior did not materially improve, ruling out expired credentials as the primary cause. The incident was mitigated by increasing gateway timeout and retry handling and restarting gateway pods, with ownership handed to the downstream service team for capacity and latency remediation.
resolution_steps: Validated the integration authentication path by rotating the API token for the analytics_sync_svc service account and confirming authenticated requests continued to succeed during low-latency windows, which ruled out token expiry as the primary driver of the failures. Rotation performed by Carlos Medina.

Adjusted the Integration Gateway request timeout from 3 seconds to 8 seconds plus retry/backoff policy (exponential base 2s, max 5 retries) on INTGW-NODE-04 so transient downstream latency spikes would not immediately exhaust scheduled integration jobs.

Restarted Integration Gateway pods (including intgw-analytics-7b4d9f at 10.42.17.88) in Kubernetes us-east-1 to clear transient connection state and ensure the updated timeout and retry configuration was active across the running instances.

Correlated gateway 504 errors with Monitoring System data showing downstream API latency spikes (p99 at 7.2s) above the prior 3-second request window and documented downstream service latency as the operational fault domain. Findings reviewed by Tomoko Ishida.

Escalated the incident to the downstream API service team under Raj Patel (rpatel) for service-side latency and capacity investigation while keeping enhanced Monitoring System alerting in place for 24 hours to confirm sync recovery and no further retry exhaustion on the analytics_sync_svc integration path.

title: Nightly API integration jobs timing out for Integration Gateway
description: Nightly data synchronization jobs from the Integration Gateway (namespace: intg-gateway-prod, cluster: eks-prod-east) to the downstream API Service in us-east-1 began failing at 02:00 UTC on 2025-12-05 with repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses. Gateway pod intg-gw-worker-7b4d9 logged requests timing out after 30 seconds against endpoint https://api-internal.corpsync.io/v2/data-ingest. The last known successful full sync completed at 03:10 UTC on 2025-12-04 (job ID sync-nightly-20251204-0300). This is blocking scheduled data delivery for internal integrations relied upon by the Finance and Analytics teams. Reporter: Darren Whitfield (dwhitfield@corpmail.com), Integration Platform team. Available monitoring in Datadog shows elevated API Service latency during the job window, while retained logs do not show clear 401/403 authentication failures, leaving backend latency and API-side throttling as the primary investigated causes.
root_cause: Downstream API Service latency during the nightly processing window caused Integration Gateway requests to exceed the 30-second client timeout, resulting in repeated 504 timeouts and failed sync jobs. Token expiration was investigated but not supported by available evidence because retained logs showed no explicit authentication failures and the configured token was still present.
resolution_steps: Validated that the integration credential for service account svc-intg-sync was present in Vault configuration (secret/intg-gateway/api-token) and found no supporting evidence of token rejection or 401/403 authentication failures during the incident window in logs from pod intg-gw-worker-7b4d9.

Correlated the nightly job failure window (02:00–02:45 UTC) with Datadog APM monitoring data and confirmed a sharp increase in downstream API Service latency on api-svc-node-east-03, with p95 response time rising from ~200ms to ~6s — well above normal baseline — during the affected sync-nightly runs.

Applied a mitigation on the Integration Gateway job path (namespace intg-gateway-prod, pod intg-gw-worker-7b4d9) by increasing the request timeout from 30s to 90s and configuring exponential retry with backoff (max 3 retries, initial delay 5s) so long-running downstream API calls could complete instead of failing at the prior 30-second limit. Change applied by Priya Nair.

Restarted the affected Integration Gateway pod intg-gw-worker-7b4d9 from workstation WORKSTATION-DW-PC12 to clear transient connection state and reran a validation job (sync-validate-20251206-0015) after the timeout adjustment; validation completed successfully in 74 seconds.

Escalated the latency finding to the API Service owner Marcus Tan (mtan@corpmail.com, phone +1-555-839-2104) for backend performance investigation on api-svc-node-east-03 during the nightly batch window and documented the dependency on their service health for permanent correction. Escalation ticket INC-AIT-0028-ESC created and assigned to the Austin platform engineering team.
agent_questions: Hi Darren — please confirm whether any token rotation or deployment change occurred on the intg-gateway-prod namespace before 02:00 UTC, and share a sample failed request timestamp (e.g., from the pod logs on intg-gw-worker-7b4d9) so we can compare gateway errors with backend latency telemetry in Datadog. Also, can you verify whether the service account svc-intg-sync still has valid credentials in Vault? — Priya Nair, Integration Support

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing scheduled job failures
description: The nightly customer synchronization job (job ID: SYNC-CUST-7041) managed by rchandra was failing through the Integration Gateway in us-east-1. Requests from integration client host WORKSTATION-APPSVC-RC (10.42.18.97) to the API Service endpoint began returning 504 Gateway Timeout responses after earlier 401 token validation failures on service account svc_intsync_prod. The scheduled job failed twice within the hour between 05:00 and 06:00 UTC, blocking downstream data sync to the CRM application and delaying customer record updates for the Austin operations team until the integration client authentication issue and gateway retry behavior were corrected.
root_cause: Expired API token for the integration client caused repeated authentication failures, which increased retry activity and gateway latency until scheduled sync requests began returning 504 timeouts.
resolution_steps: Rotated the expired API token for service account svc_intsync_prod (client_id: intgw-cust-sync-0029) used by the integration client on WORKSTATION-APPSVC-RC and updated the credential in the Integration Gateway connection configuration vault, performed by Priya Nair (pnair, E-40821).

Forced a token refresh for svc_intsync_prod and revalidated authenticated requests from 10.42.18.97 to confirm the API Service was accepting calls on path /api/v2/customer-sync without further 401 errors.

Temporarily increased the gateway timeout on the affected integration path /api/v2/customer-sync from 30s to 90s on gw-east-node-04 to reduce immediate job failures while authentication was being restored for svc_intsync_prod.

Updated gateway retry and backoff settings on the integration client from 3 retries/5s fixed interval to 5 retries with exponential backoff (base 10s, max 120s) to prevent rapid retry storms from amplifying upstream latency during future auth-related failures.

Implemented an automated token rotation process for svc_intsync_prod with a 60-day renewal cycle and alerting at 7 days before expiry, and verified that subsequent scheduled sync requests (SYNC-CUST-7041 at 06:00 UTC) completed successfully through the gateway as confirmed by rchandra.

title: Integration Gateway timeouts during data sync — expired API token
description: Scheduled data sync jobs from the application to the downstream API began failing in Kubernetes in us-east-1, triggering monitoring alerts at 2025-12-06 02:14 UTC. The Integration Gateway (host: INTGW-NODE-04) showed repeated request timeouts and 504 Gateway Timeout responses, with accompanying 401 Unauthorized errors. This blocked normal DataSync Service processing for the Chicago data center and caused delayed data synchronization for affected users and dependent systems. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Jennings (emp ID: EMP-40821) via email at mjennings@corplabs.com.
root_cause: The Integration Gateway was using an expired API token while still referencing stale Integration API Policy v1.2, causing authentication failures against the downstream API; repeated retries then manifested as 504 timeout symptoms during scheduled sync processing.
resolution_steps: Rotated the expired API token (client_id: datasync-prod-east) and updated the downstream API credential used by the Integration Gateway. New token issued by Derek Whitfield (dwhitfield) with a 180-day expiry and stored in the secure token vault.

Changed the gateway policy reference from Integration API Policy v1.2 to Integration API Policy v2.0 to align with the current authentication requirements, as confirmed by the platform engineering team in Chicago.

Redeployed the Integration Gateway configuration in Kubernetes (us-east-1 cluster) so the new token and policy settings were loaded by running gateway instances on INTGW-NODE-04 and peer nodes. Rollout completed at 11:08 UTC.

Adjusted retry and backoff settings from a fixed 3-second interval to exponential backoff (initial 5s, max 30s, jitter enabled) to reduce immediate repeat attempts that were amplifying downstream latency and masking the primary authorization failure.

Validated successful authenticated calls and confirmed scheduled data sync jobs completed without new 401 or 504 errors. Priya Nair (pnair) verified from the Houston operations center that all pending sync batches cleared by 11:15 UTC, then continued monitoring for recurrence via the Monitoring System alerting dashboard.
agent_questions: We are seeing both 504 timeout errors and 401 Unauthorized responses from the Integration Gateway. Hi Marcus, can you please confirm whether any token or policy change was pending for the downstream API integration? We're also checking with Derek Whitfield (dwhitfield) from the platform engineering team to verify recent credential rotation schedules. Please respond to this thread or reach out at 512-884-3091 if you have additional context.

title: Integration Gateway: API timeouts
description: Scheduled nightly data sync jobs through the Integration Gateway began failing around 03:10 UTC on 2025-12-06 in us-east-1. The affected integration, managed by service account svc-datasync-prod (employee ID EMP-40821), showed elevated API latency with repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses and preceding 401 Unauthorized errors from the API service endpoint at api-gateway-east.corplabs.internal. This blocked the nightly synchronization workflow for the data-sync-service until authentication was restored and the gateway could complete API calls successfully. Issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Denver integration operations team.
root_cause: The Integration Gateway service account token expired, and the scheduled rotation job did not refresh the credential in time, causing authentication failures that cascaded into integration call timeouts.
resolution_steps: Validated that the integration service account token for svc-datasync-prod (EMP-40821) had expired at 2025-12-06T03:00:00Z and confirmed the active credential in the secrets vault (secret/prod/datasync/api-token) no longer matched a usable API token. Verification performed by Rafael Ortiz (rortiz) from the platform engineering team.

Rotated the expired API service token for the svc-datasync-prod integration account and updated the centralized secrets vault entry (secret/prod/datasync/api-token) with the new credential. New token issued with a 90-day TTL and confirmed valid against api-gateway-east.corplabs.internal.

Restarted the Integration Gateway service on INTGW-PROD-01.corplabs.internal (pod intgw-prod-deployment-7c4d9 in the eks-prod-east cluster) so the application reloaded the refreshed secret and stopped sending unauthorized requests.

Re-ran the failed nightly sync workflow (job data-sync-nightly-20251206) and verified the integration completed successfully without further 401 or 504 errors. Confirmation provided by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) from the Denver operations team at 17:45 UTC.

Adjusted the credential rotation schedule from 90-day to 60-day intervals with a 7-day pre-expiry warning alert, and updated retry/backoff settings (max retries from 3 to 5, exponential backoff ceiling raised to 60s) to reduce the risk of future token-expiry-related timeout failures. Changes reviewed by Priya Nair (pnair) and committed to the infrastructure-as-code repository.
agent_questions: Reviewing the nightly sync failure window now. I can see the alerts originated from host INTGW-PROD-01.corplabs.internal in us-east-1. Please confirm whether there were any recent credential, secret rotation, or integration account changes to the svc-datasync-prod service account before the 03:10 UTC failures started. Also, Marcus — was anyone else on the Denver team aware of pending vault secret expirations?

title: API calls to third-party timing out via Integration Gateway
description: Internal integration users on the data-ops team (reported by Marcus Delgado, emp ID EMP-40291) were trying to run overnight data syncs through the Integration Gateway (gateway node igw-prod-east-07) to a third-party vendor API (vendor: Nextera Data Services) in Kubernetes us-east-1, but requests intermittently stalled for 30-60 seconds and returned 504 Gateway Timeout responses. Multiple integration jobs failed — specifically jobs SYNC-4401, SYNC-4402, and SYNC-4405 — and data synchronization to the downstream CRM pipeline was delayed. The issue was observed starting around 09:30 UTC from workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MDELGADO (IP 10.42.17.88), with no confirmed recent application deployment, and token rotation history for service account svc-integ-nextera was initially unclear.
root_cause: Third-party API responsiveness degraded during the affected sync window, causing upstream requests from the Integration Gateway to exceed the configured timeout and return repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses. Token expiry could not be substantiated from available evidence, while the observed timeout pattern and gateway behavior were more consistent with downstream latency than authentication failure.
resolution_steps: Reviewed Integration Gateway failures on node igw-prod-east-07 during the affected 09:30–10:15 UTC window and confirmed repeated upstream timeout behavior (504 responses on jobs SYNC-4401, SYNC-4402, SYNC-4405) rather than an application-side parsing or routing error.

Validated available credential records for service account svc-integ-nextera in the credential vault and confirmed there was no clear evidence of token rejection or authentication-specific failures (no 401/403 codes) requiring emergency secret rotation. Flagged the 92-day-old token for scheduled rotation per policy.

Retried failed integration jobs (SYNC-4401, SYNC-4402, SYNC-4405) after the downstream Nextera Data Services API response pattern stabilized around 10:20 UTC to restore delayed synchronization. All three jobs completed successfully on retry as confirmed by Marcus Delgado.

Escalated the incident to the Nextera Data Services third-party provider (support reference NEXTERA-SR-88712) with the affected time window (09:30–10:15 UTC), 504 timeout pattern from igw-prod-east-07, and request latency symptoms for confirmation of downstream service degradation. Escalation handled by Sandra Cho (sandra.cho@corplabs.com).

Standardized the gateway retry and backoff handling guidance for the Nextera Data Services integration on igw-prod-east-07 (increased timeout to 45s, added exponential backoff with jitter) and documented the need to capture X-RateLimit-Remaining/Retry-After response headers and svc-integ-nextera token rotation history in future occurrences to speed isolation of rate-limit versus latency conditions. Documentation updated by Priya Nair in the integration runbook.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please provide Integration Gateway logs from igw-prod-east-07 for the 09:30-09:45 UTC window and confirm whether failed responses include rate-limit headers (X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After) or any authentication errors (401/403). Also verify the last known token rotation time for the svc-integ-nextera service account. You can pull the logs from the Monitoring System dashboard at https://monitoring.corplabs.internal/gateway/igw-prod-east-07. — Priya Nair, Integration Support (priya.nair@corplabs.com)

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts impacting data sync
description: Users reported failed scheduled integration jobs and delayed data synchronization for the API Integration used by the Order Processing App. During the past hour, the Integration Gateway in Kubernetes (us-east-1) showed a spike in HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout responses along with intermittent 401 Unauthorized errors, preventing normal authenticated API calls and delaying downstream data updates. The issue was initially flagged by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Austin office, who noticed that order sync jobs for client account OP-4417 were stalling. Additional reports came in from Priya Nair (emp ID: E-20587) confirming the same behavior from the Portland office.
root_cause: Expired API token used by the Integration Gateway caused token refresh failures and intermittent 401 Unauthorized responses, which cascaded into repeated gateway retries and HTTP 504 timeouts for integration jobs.
resolution_steps: Validated the gateway and downstream API logs to confirm token refresh failures and authentication errors consistent with an expired integration token. Rachel Ito (rito) reviewed logs on the us-east-1 Integration Gateway pods and the API Service audit trail for service account svc-orderproc, confirming over 340 failed refresh attempts between 03:22 and 04:49 UTC.

Rotated the expired API token used by the Integration Gateway and updated the active secret so new authenticated requests could be established successfully. The new token was generated for svc-orderproc and stored in the Kubernetes secret integration-gateway-token in the orderproc namespace.

Restarted gateway pods to ensure the new token was loaded and stale authenticated sessions or connection pools were cleared. All three gateway replica pods in us-east-1 were rolling-restarted, completing by 04:48 UTC.

Adjusted Integration Gateway retry and backoff settings to better tolerate short downstream latency without cascading into prolonged timeout conditions. Specifically, the max retry count was reduced from 10 to 5 and exponential backoff ceiling was set to 8 seconds, as recommended by Rachel Ito.

Implemented or updated the automated token rotation policy and monitoring coverage to alert before token expiry and to detect renewed 401 or 504 patterns early. A scheduled CronJob was added to rotate the svc-orderproc token every 60 days, and a Monitoring System alert rule was configured to fire when 401 error rate exceeds 5% over a 5-minute window, with notifications routed to mdelgado@corplabs.com and the Application Support channel.

Monitored request success rate, error counts, and integration job completion for approximately one hour and confirmed traffic returned to baseline. Rachel Ito and Marcus Delgado verified via the Monitoring System dashboard that all Order Processing App sync jobs completed without errors through 05:50 UTC.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts during nightly sync
description: During the nightly DataSync App synchronization through the Integration Gateway, multiple API calls initiated by the ETL service account (svc-datasync-etl) to the downstream API exceeded the 30-second timeout window and some requests returned HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout. The overnight batch job (job ID: SYNC-BATCH-20251207-0200) could not complete successfully, causing delayed data availability for downstream consumers in us-east-1 on the EKS-hosted integration path. Reported by Marcus Delgado (emp ID E-40291) from the Richmond ETL Operations team. Immediate token rotation provided only intermittent improvement, while monitoring during the same job window showed elevated downstream service latency as the main blocker rather than an authentication failure. The integration pod running on host WORKSTATION-ETLNODE-MD logged repeated connection timeouts starting at approximately 02:05 UTC.
root_cause: downstream service latency during the nightly sync window caused requests to exceed the Integration Gateway timeout threshold
resolution_steps: Validated that the Integration Gateway token for svc-datasync-etl was not the primary fault domain after rotation produced only intermittent improvement and logs showed no token-expiry events. Confirmed with Priya Nair (pnair) that authentication was healthy across the gateway cluster.

Adjusted the nightly integration retry behavior to use exponential backoff (initial interval 5s, max 3 retries, backoff multiplier 2x) and aligned the temporary request timeout increase from 30s to 60s to better tolerate transient latency spikes during batch processing on job SYNC-BATCH configuration.

Correlated failed job batches (SYNC-BATCH-20251207-0200) with elevated downstream p95/p99 response times (38s/47.2s) and HTTP 504 timeout behavior during the same overnight window (02:00–04:30 UTC) to isolate the issue to downstream service performance. Analysis led by Tomás Herrera (therrera) using the Monitoring System latency dashboards.

Opened and tracked a priority escalation (ESC-DS-1207) with the downstream service team contact Kenji Watanabe (kwatanabe) for latency mitigation during the nightly processing window and requested targeted remediation and ETA. Marcus Delgado (E-40291) added as stakeholder on the escalation ticket.

Continued end-to-end monitoring of job completion, timeout frequency, and downstream latency metrics via the Monitoring System to confirm recovery and verify that nightly synchronization returned to expected processing windows. Alerts configured to notify m.delgado@corplabs.com and the ETL Operations channel if p99 latency exceeds 25s during the sync window.

title: Integration Gateway API calls timing out and returning authorization errors
description: During the nightly synchronization window starting at 02:00 UTC on 2025-12-07, internal applications routed through the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east.corpsync.internal) were unable to complete downstream API data sync jobs. The issue was first flagged by Rajesh Menon from the platform engineering team after the HR data pipeline and finance reconciliation feeds both failed. Monitoring dashboards on the Monitoring System and gateway access logs showed repeated HTTP 401 Unauthorized responses from the downstream API endpoint (api.dataservices.corpsync.internal/v2/sync), followed by cascading API call timeouts at the 30-second threshold. This increased job failure rates across 14 scheduled integration tasks and delayed data synchronization for multiple internal consumers including payroll and inventory services. Investigation by the application team focused on authentication token health and downstream API availability, ultimately determining that the gateway service account token (svc-igw-sync) had exceeded its 30-day rotation window by 15 days.
observed_errors: integration job failure during nightly sync
root_cause: The Integration Gateway service account API token had expired because token rotation had not occurred within the 30-day policy window, causing downstream API authentication failures (401 Unauthorized). Repeated retries during nightly sync jobs then cascaded into request timeouts.
resolution_steps: Rotate the Integration Gateway service account API token for svc-igw-sync in the secrets manager (Vault path secret/igw/prod/api-token) and update the Kubernetes secret igw-api-token in namespace igw-prod used by the gateway deployment. Rotation performed by Marcus Tan (E-50921) and verified by Lina Chowdhury.

Restart the Integration Gateway pods in the igw-prod namespace on k8s-cluster (us-east-1) so the running containers load the newly rotated token from the updated Kubernetes secret instead of the expired cached credential. Confirmed 3/3 pods recycled successfully by Marcus Tan.

Validate authenticated calls from the gateway (igw-prod-east.corpsync.internal) to the downstream API (api.dataservices.corpsync.internal/v2/sync) and confirm that 401 Unauthorized responses are no longer present in logs. Post-rotation test calls returned HTTP 200 with average latency of 195ms.

Re-run the 14 failed or pending synchronization jobs (including HR sync, finance reconciliation, and inventory feed) and verify they complete within the expected 30-second timeout window without elevated retries. All jobs completed successfully; Rajesh Menon confirmed data consumers received updated records.

Update token rotation monitoring and alerting in the Monitoring System so missed rotations beyond the 30-day policy for svc-igw-sync and other gateway service accounts are detected at the 25-day mark — 5 days before expiry — ensuring alerts reach the platform operations team (marcus.tan@corpsync.com, rajesh.menon@corpsync.com) before nightly sync processing is impacted.
agent_questions: Hi Rajesh — we are seeing both API timeouts and 401 Unauthorized responses during the nightly sync window (02:00–04:00 UTC). Logs from igw-prod-east.corpsync.internal show failures across multiple integration job IDs. Can you confirm whether the failures affect all scheduled sync jobs or only a subset, and whether there was any recent credential or secret change for the gateway service account svc-igw-sync? Also, please confirm if your team or anyone in DevOps — perhaps Lina Chowdhury — performed a manual secret rotation recently. I'm checking from my workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RM at 10.42.17.88.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: Nightly order sync jobs in the Order Sync Application were unable to complete because calls from the Integration Gateway (gateway-prod-ordersync.corplabs.internal) to the downstream partner API (partner-api.logisticshub.com) repeatedly timed out and returned 504 responses. The gateway logs on pod igw-ordersync-7b4d also showed authentication failures with "invalid_token," indicating the partner credential provisioned under service account svc-ordersync had expired. Retries were exhausted after 12 consecutive failures, causing approximately 4.5 hours of delayed downstream order data for the OrderProcessing group in us-east-1. Issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Atlanta fulfillment operations team.
root_cause: Expired downstream partner API token in the Integration Gateway credential configuration caused authentication failures, which manifested as repeated 504 timeout responses during nightly order sync retries until the job exhausted its retry limit.
resolution_steps: Validated from gateway logs on igw-ordersync-7b4d and failed sync attempts (ordersync-20251207-0100 through ordersync-20251207-0512) that partner API calls to partner-api.logisticshub.com were returning authentication-related errors including "invalid_token" alongside repeated 504 timeout failures. Reviewed by Kevin Marsh (kmarsh, EMP-90214) and confirmed with Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) from the Atlanta operations team.

Coordinated with the partner team via Priya Nair (pnair, EMP-78503) to rotate the expired API token for service account svc-ordersync and obtain a new valid credential (SHA256 fingerprint verified) for the downstream API integration with partner-api.logisticshub.com.

Updated the stored partner API credential for svc-ordersync in the Integration Gateway credential vault and restarted the gateway pods (igw-ordersync-7b4d, igw-ordersync-7b4e) on k8s-cluster-42 so new authenticated sessions were established against partner-api.logisticshub.com. Restart performed from workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-KM at 10.200.4.31.

Adjusted the integration retry policy for the Order Sync Application to use exponential backoff (initial 5s, max 120s, jitter enabled) and reduce immediate retry storms when downstream authentication or timeout conditions occur. Configuration change committed by kmarsh and reviewed by pnair.

Ran validation checks on the next scheduled sync (ordersync-20251207-2200) and confirmed subsequent nightly sync executions completed successfully with 200 OK responses from partner-api.logisticshub.com, then monitored backlog processing via the Monitoring System dashboard until all 1,247 delayed order records were cleared by 2025-12-08T02:15Z.
agent_questions: Reviewing the failed nightly syncs now — I can see the job history for svc-ordersync on k8s-cluster-42. Can you confirm whether the gateway logs on igw-ordersync-7b4d show authentication-related messages, especially any token or credential errors tied to the partner-api.logisticshub.com endpoint, in addition to the 504 timeouts? Also tagging Priya Nair from the integration platform team for visibility. — Agent: Kevin Marsh (kmarsh, EMP-90214)

title: API timeouts during data sync — conflicting evidence between expired token and
description: Overnight API Integration data sync jobs running on Kubernetes us-east-1 (namespace: api-sync-prod) began failing or completing late starting around 02:15 UTC on 2025-12-08, leaving users in the Columbus office with delayed record updates and failed integration runs. The issue was first flagged by integration lead Marcus Delgado (EMP-40821) after the morning handoff review. Monitoring detected repeated 504 Gateway Timeout events against the API Service endpoint api-gw.corpsvc.internal:8443 during the same period that Integration Gateway logs on host INTGW-PROD-04 recorded 401 Unauthorized errors for an expired token tied to service account svc_apisync. The overlapping authentication and latency symptoms blocked normal scheduled synchronization and created uncertainty about whether the primary failure was credential expiry, downstream slowness, or retry amplification. Ticket raised by r.nakamura@corplabs.com on behalf of the Application Support group.
root_cause: Primary cause was an expired API token on the Integration Gateway, which generated 401 authentication failures and triggered repeated retry behavior. The increased retry volume overlapped with elevated downstream API latency and intermittent rate-limit pressure, producing correlated 504 timeout spikes. Rotating the token and tuning retry/backoff removed the recurring failure pattern and restored sync stability, while downstream latency remained an external contributing factor monitored through escalation.
resolution_steps: Validated the Integration Gateway authentication path on INTGW-PROD-04 and rotated the expired API token for service account svc_apisync used by the API Integration; new token issued with a 90-day expiry and registered in the secrets vault by Priya Venkatesh.

Restarted the affected Integration Gateway pods (3 replicas in namespace api-sync-prod on Kubernetes us-east-1) so the updated secret was loaded consistently by all running instances; confirmed new token active via health-check endpoint.

Adjusted the API Integration retry and backoff policy from 5 retries at 2-second intervals to 3 retries with 10-second exponential backoff, to reduce immediate retry storms that were amplifying latency and timeout conditions against api-gw.corpsvc.internal:8443.

Verified post-change behavior by reviewing gateway logs on INTGW-PROD-04 and the Monitoring System dashboard to confirm the 401 expired-token errors stopped and all five sync profiles (customer-records, inventory-delta, order-fulfillment, billing-extract, compliance-audit) resumed without recurring timeout spikes; Marcus Delgado (EMP-40821) confirmed records were current by 05:10 UTC.

Escalated the observed downstream latency to the external service owner under REF INC-DOWNSTREAM-987 and kept correlation alerts in place for any future overlap between authentication failures and 504 events; escalation contact notified via r.nakamura@corplabs.com with Priya Venkatesh as the internal point of contact.
agent_questions: We found overlapping 504 timeout alerts and 401 expired-token entries from the Integration Gateway (INTGW-PROD-04). Reviewing the logs for service account svc_apisync, the token expiration timestamp was 2025-12-08T01:59:00Z — roughly 15 minutes before the first failed sync job.
