Please confirm whether the overnight failures affected all scheduled sync jobs or only specific integrations, and whether any recent credential change was expected. Also, can Marcus Delgado or anyone on the Columbus team confirm if there was a planned token rotation window that may have been missed? — Agent: Priya Venkatesh

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data syncs
description: Scheduled data sync jobs through the Integration Gateway (namespace: intg-gateway-prod, cluster: k8s-east-prod-04) began failing or queuing at approximately 09:12 UTC on 2025-12-08 because POST requests to the downstream API Service endpoint https://api-svc.corplabs.internal/v2/sync were returning repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Application Support team in the Charlotte office, noting that data lag for the integration workflow in the Kubernetes environment in us-east-1 had exceeded 45 minutes and was blocking timely completion of routine sync processing for the customer-data pipeline. Investigation focused on whether the failures were caused by expired authentication tokens, API rate limiting, or elevated downstream response latency. Ticket was assigned to senior integration engineer Priya Nair (emp ID: EMP-40821) for triage.
root_cause: Sustained elevated latency in the downstream API Service caused Integration Gateway requests to exceed the configured upstream timeout threshold, producing 504 Gateway Timeout responses and causing scheduled sync jobs to fail or backlog.
resolution_steps: Validated that authentication was not the trigger by confirming there was no matching pattern of 401 or 403 failures for service account svc-intg-sync during the timeout window (09:12–09:24 UTC); token expiry date verified as 2026-03-15.

Confirmed the timeout condition was latency-driven by correlating 14 failed integration jobs with downstream API latency spikes (p95: 48s vs. 1.2s baseline) and repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses on pod intg-gw-worker-7b4d9, as identified by Priya Nair.

Temporarily increased the Integration Gateway request timeout from 30 seconds to 90 seconds in the intg-gateway-prod namespace ConfigMap so in-flight downstream calls could complete during the latency event; change applied at 09:31 UTC.

Adjusted retry and exponential backoff settings on upstream calls (max retries: 5, initial backoff: 2s, multiplier: 2x) to reduce immediate job failure rates and avoid excessive retry pressure while the downstream service remained slow.

Cleared 14 queued integration jobs and monitored processing throughput via the Monitoring System until the sync backlog returned to acceptable levels at 09:48 UTC; confirmed with Marcus Delgado in Charlotte that data lag was resolved.

Escalated the incident to the downstream API service team lead Robert Cheng (rcheng) via ESC-7841 with supporting latency trends, Grafana snapshots, and request traces (trx-8a3f29c), and updated Monitoring System alert thresholds to detect future 95th-percentile latency spikes above 10 seconds earlier.

title: Integration Gateway outbound API requests timing out across environments
description: Multiple application teams (including the Order Processing and Inventory Sync groups managed by Priya Venkatesh) were trying to complete scheduled data syncs through the Integration Gateway, but outbound calls to the third-party API (vendor endpoint: api.partnerlogistics.com) began timing out after peak traffic this morning. Monitoring dashboards on the us-east-1 cluster and gateway logs from node igw-pod-07.integration.corplabs.internal showed repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses, elevated downstream latency (upstream_latency_ms>2000), and TokenExpiredError events starting around 08:15 UTC. The issue was first reported by rchandra@corplabs.com and affected multiple environments (staging and production), blocking normal integration job completion until gateway authentication was restored. Ticket raised on behalf of the integration-team user group by Marcus Ellison (EMP-40821).
root_cause: An expired API token on the Integration Gateway caused authentication failures during outbound calls to the downstream third-party API. Repeated token refresh failures left the gateway using invalid credentials, which increased latency and resulted in 504 timeouts for scheduled integration jobs.
resolution_steps: Validated that outbound request failures aligned with token expiry on the svc-igw-sync service account and repeated token refresh errors in Integration Gateway logs (igw-pod-07.integration.corplabs.internal), with initial report from rchandra@corplabs.com.

Rotated the expired API token used by the Integration Gateway service account svc-igw-sync for downstream third-party API authentication via the API Service secrets vault; rotation performed by Marcus Ellison (EMP-40821).

Restarted all Integration Gateway pods in us-east-1 and cleared cached credentials so all gateway instances loaded the updated token for svc-igw-sync; verified pod health on the Monitoring System dashboard.

Verified successful token refresh behavior for svc-igw-sync and confirmed authenticated outbound API requests completed without timeout errors; Priya Venkatesh and David Kowalski (EMP-55934) confirmed their respective OrderSync-Prod and InventoryPull-Staging jobs resumed successfully.

Adjusted retry and backoff settings (max_retries=5, initial_backoff=500ms, backoff_multiplier=2) on the Integration Gateway to reduce integration job failures during future token refresh windows and monitored request latency on the Monitoring System until normal operation was restored; also scheduled a review of the API Service credential rotator to prevent silent refresh failures.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing PaymentSync failures
description: PaymentSync backfill and scheduled synchronization jobs intermittently failed between 02:10 and 02:40 UTC on 2025-12-08 when the Integration Gateway (gateway-prod-east-07.payments.internal) timed out while calling the downstream payment API endpoint at https://api.payments.internal/v2/sync. This caused queued sync work on the paymentsync-worker pods in the us-east-1 Kubernetes cluster, delayed payment data updates for Finance Users, and repeated 504 timeout responses logged by the gateway. The issue was initially reported by Rajesh Menon (rmenon@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office after the PaymentSyncApp dashboard showed stalled jobs. Immediate recovery was observed after token rotation by ops engineer Lisa Cheng, but available validation evidence did not show token expiry, so the incident is best explained as downstream latency with token rotation treated as a coincidental or non-causal mitigation.
root_cause: Intermittent downstream payment API latency exceeded the Integration Gateway timeout window, causing 504 responses and PaymentSync job failures; token rotation coincided with recovery but was not supported as the primary cause by token validation evidence.
resolution_steps: Validated that the integration token for service account svc-paymentsync was still accepted by existing API Service token checks and recorded that the token rotation performed by Lisa Cheng (EMP-90274) did not have supporting evidence as the primary failure cause; no 401/403 rejections were logged.

Correlated the PaymentSync failure window (02:10–02:40 UTC) with Integration Gateway logs from gateway-prod-east-07.payments.internal showing repeated 504 responses and upstream latency averaging 7.2s against the 5s configured timeout threshold, confirmed via Monitoring System traces.

Applied a gateway-side stability change on gateway-prod-east-07.payments.internal by increasing the request timeout from 5s to 12s and adjusting retry and backoff behavior (exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 retries) to reduce repeated PaymentSync job failures during transient downstream slowdowns.

Escalated the incident (ESC-PAY-0819) to the downstream payment service team lead David Okafor (dokafor@corplabs.com, phone +1-571-884-2039) with the failure window, timeout evidence, Monitoring System trace IDs, and a request for extended request tracing and latency analysis on https://api.payments.internal/v2/sync.

Monitored queue recovery and PaymentSync processing from the Monitoring System dashboard after the gateway tuning change to confirm jobs resumed and the ~1,200-item backlog began clearing without further immediate failures; Rajesh Menon (rmenon) confirmed Finance Users data sync restored by 03:15 UTC.
agent_questions: Hi Rajesh — we are checking whether the PaymentSync failures are caused by authentication or downstream slowness. I've pulled the Integration Gateway logs from gateway-prod-east-07.payments.internal and the Monitoring System alerts for the paymentsync-worker namespace. Please confirm whether jobs failed only during the 02:10–02:40 UTC window and whether any change besides the token rotation performed by Lisa Cheng (EMP-90274) was made at that time. Also, can you verify whether the service account svc-paymentsync was showing any auth errors in the API Service audit trail?

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts affecting daily data sync
description: Daily customer data synchronization through the Integration Gateway began failing around 2025-12-09 03:20 UTC with repeated HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout responses. The affected workflow — managed by the Application Support team under Marcus Delgado (EMP-40821) — could not complete customer data sync jobs on time, causing delayed downstream updates to the Billing API Integration pipeline. Monitoring dashboards on host INTGW-MON-01 and distributed traces from the us-east-1 cluster showed elevated upstream response times from the downstream CRM API while no recent Integration Gateway configuration changes were identified. Initial report was filed by Priya Nair (priya.nair@corplabs.com) from the Charlotte office.
root_cause: Downstream API latency increased enough for Integration Gateway requests to exceed configured timeout thresholds, which produced repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses and caused daily sync job failures.
resolution_steps: Validated monitoring alerts on INTGW-MON-01 and distributed traces to confirm the timeout failures were correlated with elevated downstream CRM API response times (1200–1800ms) rather than a new gateway deployment or configuration change. Verification performed by Raj Okonkwo (rokonkwo) from the Charlotte office.

Escalated the latency issue to the downstream CRM API provider (contact: Lisa Fernandez, lfernandez@partnerservices.net) with supporting trace evidence showing sustained slow upstream responses during the failed sync window (03:20–04:50 UTC on 2025-12-09).

Temporarily increased the Integration Gateway timeout from 30 seconds to 60 seconds for the affected integration path (/v2/customer-sync) so in-flight requests from client IP 10.42.17.88 could complete while the downstream service stabilized. Change implemented by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado).

Adjusted the integration retry and backoff policy (initial delay 2s→10s, max retries 5→3) to reduce immediate retry pressure and limit cascading retries during periods of elevated upstream latency. Configuration updated in the Kubernetes ConfigMap for the intgw-worker deployment.

Monitored post-change gateway 504 rates on INTGW-MON-01, upstream latency, and daily sync execution results over the following 48 hours, then verified that timeout volume dropped to zero and scheduled customer data sync jobs completed successfully by 2025-12-10 03:25 UTC. Final confirmation provided by Priya Nair.
agent_questions: We are seeing recurring 504 Gateway Timeout errors on the Integration Gateway during the daily sync window (starting approximately 03:20 UTC). Requests originating from integration pod intgw-worker-7b4c on the Kubernetes cluster in us-east-1 are timing out against the downstream CRM API endpoint. Can you confirm whether any gateway configuration changed recently, or if downstream API latency is elevated at the same time? Assigning initial triage to Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) on the Application Support team.

title: Intermittent API timeouts from Integration Gateway
description: Batch integrations from the Integration Gateway (gateway node igw-prod-east-04.corplabs.internal) to the downstream API Service began failing intermittently starting 2025-12-09 09:38 UTC. Users in the Application Support group, initially reported by Marcus Delgado (EMP-40821), observed repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses and occasional 401 Unauthorized errors on integration jobs running under service account svc_intgateway. Retries did not clear the backlog, and the issue affected all API integration jobs routed through the us-east-1 cluster, delaying data synchronization for the Charlotte office until authentication and gateway configuration were corrected.
root_cause: An expired API token combined with a stale Integration Gateway configuration reference to TokenRotationPolicy_v1 caused token validation failures against the downstream API. The resulting authentication failures increased retry activity and contributed to intermittent 504 timeout behavior.
resolution_steps: Rotated the expired API token for service account svc_intgateway used by the Integration Gateway and updated the downstream token store on api-svc-east-02.corplabs.internal with the new valid secret. Rotation was executed by Priya Nair (pnair).

Updated the Integration Gateway configuration on igw-prod-east-04.corplabs.internal to replace the stale TokenRotationPolicy_v1 reference with TokenRotationPolicy_v2, ensuring future automatic rotations align with the 60-day credential lifecycle.

Redeployed the integration connector pods in the us-east-1 Kubernetes cluster so the new token and updated TokenRotationPolicy_v2 reference were loaded into the running service. Rolling restart completed at 10:14 UTC with zero dropped connections.

Adjusted retry and backoff behavior on the Integration Gateway to use safer exponential backoff (initial interval 2s, max 60s, multiplier 2×) and applied temporary timeout tuning (raised to 25s) to reduce repeated failures during token propagation across the connector fleet.

Validated successful authenticated API calls for svc_intgateway and monitored 401 and 504 error rates via the Monitoring System until integration processing returned to baseline. Confirmation sign-off provided by Marcus Delgado (EMP-40821) at 11:02 UTC.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please pull the latest Integration Gateway error log from igw-prod-east-04.corplabs.internal and confirm when the API token for service account svc_intgateway was last rotated. We need to verify token age against the TokenRotationPolicy_v1 reference currently configured. Also, can you check whether Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) made any recent credential changes on the API Service side? That will help us rule out a manual rotation mismatch.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data syncs
description: Scheduled integration jobs on the Integration Gateway (gateway node igw-prod-east-01) in us-east-1 began failing at approximately 06:15 UTC this morning while sending data to the downstream API Service endpoint https://api.corpsync.internal/v2/ingest on behalf of the Application. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corpnet.com) from the Atlanta office, who noticed missing ingest records during the daily reconciliation. The gateway returned elevated HTTP 504 timeout and HTTP 429 rate-limit responses on the /v2/ingest path, retry volume increased sharply across all scheduled jobs, and queue backpressure developed on the integration bus. This delayed daily data sync processing and caused missing records in the Application ingest until authenticated API access and retry behavior were corrected. The service account svc-igw-sync used for outbound calls was confirmed to be affected.
root_cause: A stale expired API token cached on the Integration Gateway caused failed or delayed authenticated requests, while concurrent downstream API rate limiting (HTTP 429) amplified retries and pushed requests past the gateway timeout window, resulting in job failures and sync delays.
resolution_steps: Rotated the Integration Gateway API token for service account svc-igw-sync via the credentials vault and validated that new outbound requests from igw-prod-east-01 (10.42.8.17) to the downstream API Service at https://api.corpsync.internal/v2/ingest were successfully authenticated with HTTP 200 responses.

Cleared the stale token cache on gateway node igw-prod-east-01 and changed token refresh cadence from the previous 24-hour interval to 15 minutes to prevent reuse of expired credentials beyond the 90-day TTL boundary.

Updated the integration retry policy from 2 fixed retries (5 s interval) to 5 attempts with exponential backoff and jitter (base 2 s, max 60 s) to reduce retry storms during transient throttling; configuration deployed to igw-prod-east-01 by Priya Nair.

Reprocessed the 14 affected scheduled integration jobs (job group daily-sync-east, run IDs 4401–4414) after the token and retry configuration changes to clear queue backpressure (queue depth returned from 4,200 to ~200) and restore delayed syncs for records reported missing by Marcus Delgado and the Atlanta and Denver office users.

Escalated persistent downstream rate-limit spikes (~40 429s/min post-fix) to the downstream service team contact Rafael Ochoa (rochoa@corpsync.com) under ticket DS-789 for follow-up capacity or throttling review; Priya Nair added as watcher on DS-789.
agent_questions: We are seeing elevated 504 and 429 responses from the downstream API Service at https://api.corpsync.internal/v2/ingest. Monitoring System dashboards for gateway node igw-prod-east-01 show a spike beginning around 06:15 UTC. Please confirm whether the missing records reported by Marcus Delgado align with this morning's scheduled sync window (06:00–07:00 UTC) and whether the issue is limited to data arriving through the Integration Gateway path rather than direct Application submissions. Also, can you verify whether the service account svc-igw-sync credentials were recently renewed? — Priya Nair, Application Support

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: Customers and scheduled integration jobs managed by user rsanchez were attempting to synchronize data through the Integration Gateway to a third-party API (PartnerData API v2), but starting around 2025-12-09 08:00 UTC the syncs became delayed and some jobs failed intermittently. The visible impact was repeated HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout errors and request timeouts at the gateway, which caused queued work, increased sync lag, and delayed downstream data updates for batch-job processing in us-east-1 Kubernetes workloads. The issue was initially reported by Priya Nair (priya.nair@corplabs.com) from the Austin integration operations team after observing failed sync alerts on host WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN. Approximately 140 integration jobs were affected across the CustomerApp and API Integration pipelines.
root_cause: Downstream API latency spike caused Integration Gateway requests to exceed the configured client timeout, producing HTTP 504 errors and delayed sync processing.
resolution_steps: Correlated integration job failures (batch-sync-4401 through batch-sync-4438 and subsequent queued jobs submitted by rsanchez) with gateway traces from node 10.42.18.77 and downstream PartnerData API dependency latency to confirm the timeout condition was caused by backend response degradation rather than authentication failure.

Applied a temporary Integration Gateway timeout increase from 60s to 90s to reduce immediate job failures while the downstream service issue was being investigated. Change executed by Marcus Delgado (EMP-60891) and approved by Jennifer Okafor (EMP-70234).

Adjusted retry and backoff behavior on the Integration Gateway from 5 retries at 2s fixed interval to 2 retries with exponential backoff (ceiling 30s) to prevent rapid retry storms and reduce queue pressure during the degradation window.

Escalated to the downstream PartnerData API team via David Hwang (david.hwang@partnerdata.io, +1-512-555-0193) with trace evidence showing sustained 30-45s response times from gateway node 10.42.18.77, and coordinated remediation of the latency-inducing backend connection pool misconfiguration.

Validated that downstream latency returned to normal (p99 < 1.5s) after the vendor-side fix deployed at 20:38 UTC, then confirmed all ~140 queued sync jobs drained successfully and normal synchronization rates resumed. Priya Nair confirmed data integrity from the Austin operations side.

Updated monitoring thresholds on the Integration Gateway Prometheus alerting rules to trigger at p95 latency > 5s (previously 15s) and added a PagerDuty escalation path to better detect rising dependency latency before gateway timeouts impact customer and batch sync workloads. Follow-up review scheduled by Jennifer Okafor for 2025-12-16.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing nightly data sync failures
description: The nightly Sales Data Sync integration job (job ID: sync-sales-nightly-0312) failed at 03:12 UTC on 2025-12-10 when the Integration Gateway (gateway node igw-prod-east-07) could not complete authenticated calls to the API Service endpoint https://api.corplabs.com/v2/sales-ingest. During the failure window, monitoring on the Monitoring System dashboard showed repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses, spikes of 429 Too Many Requests from the rate limiter, and a token refresh failure (AuthFailure: TokenRefreshFailed) on service account svc-salessync, which prevented the scheduled sync from completing. The backlog in the downstream data load queue grew to approximately 14,200 pending records. Reported by Marcus Delgado (Platform Integrations team, emp ID EMP-40821) from the Austin office.
root_cause: Expired API token on the Integration Gateway caused authentication refresh failure; repeated retries against the API Service then contributed to 504 timeout and 429 rate-limit responses during the nightly sync window.
resolution_steps: Rotated the expired API token for service account svc-salessync used by the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east-07) to authenticate to the API Service at https://api.corplabs.com/v2/sales-ingest. Rotation performed by Priya Nair at 03:45 UTC.

Validated successful authentication with the new token by issuing test calls from igw-prod-east-07 to the API Service and confirmed the endpoint was accepting authenticated requests for svc-salessync with <200ms response times.

Temporarily increased retry delay from 2s to 10s and adjusted exponential backoff ceiling from 30s to 120s on the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east-07) to reduce rapid retry bursts during recovery, as approved by team lead Raj Mehta.

Retried the failed nightly synchronization (job sync-sales-nightly-0312) at 04:15 UTC and processed the accumulated backlog of ~14,200 records successfully; completion confirmed at 04:38 UTC by Marcus Delgado.

Reviewed rate-limit behavior with the downstream vendor (contact: vendor-support@databridge.io) and scheduled permanent tuning for retry handling. Added Monitoring System alerts for token refresh failures on svc-salessync and threshold-based alerting for 429/504 spikes exceeding 10 events per 5-minute window. Follow-up review scheduled by Raj Mehta for 2025-12-17.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — we confirmed repeated 504 and 429 responses during the 03:12 UTC run on gateway node igw-prod-east-07. Logs from the Monitoring System show the first 504 at 03:12:04 UTC and 429 bursts starting at 03:12:18 UTC. Can you verify whether the token rotation job for service account svc-salessync reported any refresh or authentication failures around the same window? Also, please confirm whether the client host WORKSTATION-INTG-MD was used to trigger any manual retries. — Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com)

title: Integration Gateway API requests timing out
description: During the nightly customer sync window starting 2025-12-10 03:00 UTC, clients calling the Integration Gateway (gw-prod-east.corpsync.internal) experienced intermittent 504 Gateway Timeout errors and failed integration jobs. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office, noting that the Customer Sync Service and Billing App feeds were stalling. The issue affected customer data synchronization for dependent applications, with the Monitoring System dashboard showing elevated gateway response times (p95 > 4.2s) and downstream API latency on the Order Fulfillment API. Authentication failures (ERR_AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID) were also observed early in the event around 03:12 UTC, but token rotation on service account svc-custsync only reduced those errors temporarily and did not eliminate the timeout pattern. Downstream host api-orders.corpsync.internal was identified as the slow responder.
root_cause: Primary cause was elevated latency in the downstream API service during the nightly sync window, causing the Integration Gateway to exceed timeout thresholds and return intermittent 504 responses. An authentication issue from an aging or invalid token contributed noise early in the incident, but token rotation only addressed the auth failures and did not resolve the underlying downstream performance bottleneck.
resolution_steps: Validated and rotated the Integration Gateway API token for service account svc-custsync (previous token issued 2025-10-03, expired beyond 60-day validity), then verified client credentials against the gateway auth provider to remove the authentication failure condition (ERR_AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID) observed at the start of the incident. Performed by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, E-40291) from the Arlington office.

Cleared the Integration Gateway cache on gw-prod-east.corpsync.internal and confirmed authentication errors dropped from ~38/min to near zero after the credential refresh. Verified via Monitoring System dashboard that no further ERR_AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID events were generated post-rotation.

Adjusted gateway retry and backoff settings (exponential backoff increased from 1s to 3s, max retries set to 5) on gw-prod-east.corpsync.internal to reduce customer sync job failures while downstream latency on api-orders.corpsync.internal remained elevated. Configuration change applied by Priya Nair (pnair) and validated against the Customer Sync Service and Billing App integration feeds.

Correlated gateway 504 errors with increased downstream API response times (p95 4,200ms, peak 6,800ms vs. 2s timeout threshold) on api-orders.corpsync.internal during the nightly sync window (03:00–04:30 UTC) and isolated the remaining issue to downstream Order Fulfillment service performance rather than gateway authentication or rate limiting.

Escalated the incident to the downstream Order Fulfillment service team (contact: Raj Mehta, rmehta@corplabs.com, phone ext. 4782 at the Denver operations center) with logs, distributed traces, and timing correlation for remediation of the latency spike, then placed post-change monitoring in effect via the Monitoring System to confirm timeout stabilization. Escalation tracked by Tom Hargrove (thargrove, E-50134).

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts during nightly sync
description: The nightly sync job running under service account svc-nightlysync in us-east-1 began failing around 2025-12-10 09:05 UTC when calls from host WORKSTATION-SYNC-MR to the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east.corpsys.internal) started returning 504 Gateway Timeout and intermittent 401 Unauthorized responses. The sync workflow orchestrated by the data-integration namespace on Kubernetes stalled, downstream jobs were delayed, and retry activity increased traffic against the API Service endpoint /api/v2/data-sync. The issue was first reported by Marcus Reeves (mreeves@corplabs.com) from the Atlanta integration engineering team and affected the Integration Gateway path used by the nightly data synchronization process. Approximately 1,400 records queued for sync to the downstream CRM pipeline were blocked.
root_cause: Expired API token on the Integration Gateway caused authentication failures during token refresh, producing 401 responses and triggering aggressive retries that amplified load and led to 504 timeouts during the nightly sync.
resolution_steps: Rotated the expired API token (last valid rotation: 2025-11-09) used by the Integration Gateway service account svc-nightlysync and dependent API clients on igw-prod-east.corpsys.internal so authenticated calls could succeed again. Rotation performed by Marcus Reeves at 14:02 UTC.

Forced a token refresh on the affected integration path (/api/v2/data-sync) and validated that subsequent sync requests from pod IP 10.42.17.88 were accepted without 401 Unauthorized responses. Priya Nair confirmed OAuth handshake success in gateway logs.

Updated the Integration Gateway retry policy for the data-integration namespace to use exponential backoff (initial 2s, max 60s, jitter enabled) with reduced immediate retry pressure to prevent another retry storm during auth failures. Configuration change applied by Priya Nair and reviewed by Daniel Cho (dcho@corplabs.com).

Monitored gateway timeout rate, authentication errors, and downstream job completion on the Monitoring System dashboard for the Atlanta region pipeline after the change to confirm nightly sync processing returned to normal. All 1,400 queued records processed successfully by 15:18 UTC.

Scheduled automated token rotation verification for the svc-nightlysync nightly sync workflow (every 25 days, 5-day buffer before expiry) and added Monitoring System alerting for token refresh failures before the next sync window. Alert notifications configured to route to mreeves@corplabs.com and pnair@corplabs.com.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — can you confirm whether a token rotation happened recently for the svc-nightlysync service account and share Integration Gateway log entries from igw-prod-east.corpsys.internal for the 401 and 504 responses between 09:00–09:30 UTC so we can align them with token refresh activity? Also, please verify whether the client IP 10.42.17.88 matches the expected pod source. I'm assigning this to Priya Nair on the platform side for parallel review.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts to downstream service
description: Monitoring detected intermittent 504 and timeout responses from the Integration Gateway (igw-prod-east.corplabs.internal) when proxying requests to the downstream Order Fulfillment API service in EKS us-east-1. Caller application sync jobs submitted by the backend-integration-team — specifically jobs triggered by user dmorales (EMP-40821) — were delayed and sometimes failed because downstream calls exceeded the gateway's 30-second timeout window and triggered retry storms. A gateway pod restart on igw-prod-east-pod-3 did not resolve the issue, and no recent timeout-related deployment change was identified. The alert was initially raised by Priya Nair via the #api-incidents Slack channel. Missing initial context included token expiry state and whether the downstream service was slow or rate limiting during the failure window.
observed_errors: Integration job marked failed due to API timeout
root_cause: Downstream API latency intermittently exceeded the Integration Gateway timeout window, and the gateway retry behavior amplified the impact into retry storms. Token expiry was not confirmed as the cause, and available evidence points more strongly to downstream response slowness with possible transient throttling pressure rather than an authentication failure.
resolution_steps: Validated that no recent gateway deployment introduced the failures by reviewing the CI/CD pipeline history for igw-prod-east.corplabs.internal (last deploy: 2025-12-08T14:12Z, unrelated config change). Reviewed failing request patterns showing 504s and upstream timeouts clustered around slow downstream Order Fulfillment API responses rather than immediate authentication rejection.

Confirmed the integration token path (client_id: svc-orderfulfillment-prod) required verification but did not show evidence of a broad auth failure pattern in the gateway logs, so token rotation was not performed to avoid introducing an unnecessary credential change during the incident. Daniel Morales (EMP-40821) was asked to schedule a post-incident token rotation as a precaution.

Applied a gateway mitigation on igw-prod-east.corplabs.internal by increasing the downstream request timeout from 30s to 60s for affected order-sync-batch traffic and updating retry behavior to use bounded exponential backoff (base 2s, max 3 retries, jitter enabled) to stop retry storms from compounding downstream slowness.

Captured failing request traces (trace-8a4f21, trace-8a4f34, trace-8a4f47) from the Monitoring System and correlated them with downstream response timing to isolate the bottleneck to the downstream Order Fulfillment API latency window (p99 at 45–55s) rather than the gateway pod itself.

Escalated the latency evidence and trace samples to the downstream service owner Rachel Chen (rchen@corplabs.com) on the Seattle platform team for remediation while keeping the gateway mitigation in place to stabilize sync job completion for the Austin fulfillment queue.

Monitored post-change behavior via the Monitoring System dashboard and verified timeout volume dropped from ~120/min to <5/min and order-sync-batch processing stabilized after the timeout and retry configuration adjustments. Confirmed with Daniel Morales that sync jobs completed successfully by 20:15 UTC.
agent_questions: Hi Daniel — please confirm whether the current downstream API token (client_id: svc-orderfulfillment-prod) is still within its validity window and whether the downstream Order Fulfillment service reported any latency or throttling during the period when 504 timeouts began around 19:00 UTC on 2025-12-10. You can check token issuance via the Integration Gateway admin console at https://igw-admin.corplabs.internal. Also, can you verify from the Monitoring System dashboard whether host WORKSTATION-DMORALES was the primary caller origin?

title: Intermittent API timeouts from Integration Gateway to downstream API
description: Scheduled integration jobs and live API calls from Integration Gateway v3.2 in us-east-1 began failing after about 03:10 UTC on 2025-12-11 with 504 Gateway Timeout responses and elevated downstream latency. The issue was first reported by integration admin rchandra (Rajesh Chandra, emp ID EMP-40821) from the Arlington office, who noticed that the nightly order-sync job and real-time inventory push to the downstream Fulfillment API were returning ERR_API_TIMEOUT. Retries were exhausted after the default 3-attempt cycle, delaying data synchronization across dependent systems and preventing normal API integration processing until the downstream performance issue was corrected. Alerts were firing on the Monitoring System dashboard for gateway node igw-east-node04 (10.42.18.77) and the issue was visible from the submitter's workstation WORKSTATION-RCHANDRA at 10.200.5.34.
root_cause: A downstream API database query became slow during the incident window, increasing response latency beyond the Integration Gateway timeout threshold and causing repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses and retry exhaustion.
resolution_steps: Reviewed Integration Gateway logs on igw-east-node04 (10.42.18.77) and Monitoring System dashboards to confirm the failure pattern, showing 47 failed jobs with repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses and a sustained downstream latency spike (p99 peaking at 18.4 s) between approximately 03:10 and 03:30 UTC. Initial triage was performed by agent mtovar (Maria Tovar).

Validated that the issue was not caused by authentication failures by checking request behavior for service account svc-igw-fulfillment and confirming the symptom pattern was timeout-related (504/ERR_API_TIMEOUT) rather than token rejection (401/403). The bearer token was confirmed valid through 2026-03-15.

Escalated the incident to the downstream Fulfillment API team lead Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) with timing, latency, and 504 evidence from the Monitoring System so they could investigate backend performance during the affected window.

The downstream Fulfillment API team, led by Priya Nair, identified and remediated a slow database query (full table scan on order_items due to a missing index after a recent schema migration) on their PostgreSQL backend that was causing the response-time degradation and intermittent 504 errors. The fix was applied at approximately 03:28 UTC.

Updated the Integration Gateway per-request timeout from 10 seconds to 30 seconds on igw-east-node04 and adjusted retry/backoff settings (max retries increased from 3 to 5, exponential backoff base from 2 s to 4 s) to better tolerate short-lived latency spikes without immediately exhausting retries. Change was applied by rchandra per change request CR-20251211-088.

Monitored gateway and downstream metrics via the Monitoring System for 24 hours after the fix, confirmed latency returned to the ~1.2 s baseline, and verified scheduled jobs resumed without further timeout spikes. Final confirmation received from Rajesh Chandra (rchandra@corplabs.com) at the Arlington office on 2025-12-12.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts during nightly sync — expired token and stale
description: Nightly DataSync jobs initiated by the Application Support team to the ThirdParty API (partner endpoint: api.thirdparty.io/v2/sync) began failing at approximately 02:00 UTC during the scheduled sync window on 2025-12-11, with repeated Integration Gateway timeouts and HTTP 504 responses logged against the production gateway cluster igw-prod-east.corpsync.internal. The downstream data synchronization was delayed by over four hours, reducing data availability for morning reporting in the Dallas office. Initial triage by Marcus Ellison (emp ID: E-40821) tied the failures to token validation errors on the Integration Gateway while processing high-volume sync traffic in the AKS-hosted production environment (namespace: datasync-prod). The issue was reported by Priya Venkatesh via the Application Support queue after automated Monitoring System alerts fired on her dashboard.
root_cause: The Integration Gateway was configured with a deprecated authentication policy that referenced expired client credentials. During nightly sync load, token validation failed, causing authenticated requests to stall and return repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses until the token and policy were corrected.
resolution_steps: Rotated the expired API token used by the Integration Gateway service account datasync-svc-prod, issued new client credentials via the corporate credential vault, and validated successful token issuance against igw-prod-east.corpsync.internal. Rotation performed by Raj Anand (ranand@corpsync.com).

Deployed the replacement gateway authentication policy 'IGW-Auth-Policy-v2' to the datasync-prod namespace and removed the deprecated 'IGW-Auth-Policy-v1' policy reference that pointed to expired credentials. Change approved by Marcus Ellison under CHG-88214.

Cleared stale authentication state on the gateway pod igw-datasync-7b4f9 and verified the updated policy 'IGW-Auth-Policy-v2' was active across all replicas in the affected AKS deployment (datasync-prod namespace, 3 replicas confirmed).

Validated retry and backoff behavior for the nightly DataSync job — adjusted exponential backoff from 5s/10s/20s to 10s/30s/60s with jitter to reduce burst retries during transient authentication failures, and confirmed configuration via the Integration Gateway admin console.

Confirmed successful end-to-end sync execution in the nightly window (02:00–02:47 UTC on 2025-12-12) with zero 504 errors, and updated Monitoring System alerting rules to trigger on token validation failures within 5 minutes and to warn 7 days before credential expiration for datasync-svc-prod. Alert recipients updated to include pvenkatesh@corpsync.com and mellison@corpsync.com.
agent_questions: Hi Priya — please confirm whether the nightly failures are limited to the Integration Gateway path (specifically the igw-prod-east.corpsync.internal cluster) and whether any recent auth policy or credential changes were made before the 504 spikes started around 02:00 UTC. Also, can you verify whether the service account datasync-svc-prod was recently modified in the credential vault? We want to rule out any upstream changes before diving deeper. — Marcus Ellison

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: Customers were trying to sync data through the Integration Gateway (gateway-prod-us-east-1.corplabs.internal) to the downstream API Service, but requests began timing out with intermittent HTTP 504 errors over roughly the last 90 minutes starting around 11:15 UTC. This caused delayed data sync completion for integration jobs owned by the Application Support team, some failed batch runs reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com), and impact to nightly batch processing on the Data Sync Worker cluster. Gateway logs from pod igw-worker-7b on host WORKSTATION-IGWNODE-MD showed sustained downstream response time spikes above the normal 5-second timeout window along with some auth retries against the /v2/token endpoint; token rotation by engineer Priya Nair reduced auth-related noise briefly, but the main customer-visible issue remained downstream latency from the API Service side. Reported from workstation 10.42.18.77 in the Arlington office.
root_cause: Elevated downstream API Service latency exceeded the Integration Gateway timeout window, causing intermittent HTTP 504 responses during sync traffic; token-related auth retries were secondary noise and not the primary failure driver.
resolution_steps: Validated and retained the rotated API token (client_id: igw-sync-prod-01) after confirming authentication errors were reduced from ~12% to <1%, separating auth noise from the primary timeout condition. Priya Nair (pnair) verified the token via manual endpoint test from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN.

Restarted Integration Gateway pods (igw-worker-7a through -7d) in the igw-prod namespace on EKS to clear transient session and connection state while confirming the timeout pattern persisted after restart, ruling out stale connection pooling as a contributing factor.

Temporarily increased retry and backoff behavior on integration jobs — retry count raised from 3 to 5, exponential backoff ceiling increased from 10s to 30s — to reduce immediate job failure rates while downstream latency was being addressed. Change applied by Priya Nair and confirmed in the Integration Job Runner configuration.

Enabled additional timeout and request tracing on the Integration Gateway (X-Trace-Enabled header, extended access log format) to capture evidence of elevated downstream response times and repeated HTTP 504 behavior. Trace samples (trace-a4f8c1, trace-b7d902) were exported for the escalation package.

Escalated the incident to the downstream API Service owners — team lead Raj Venkatesh (rvenkatesh@corplabs.com) in Dallas — with evidence of sustained latency (avg 6.2s, p99 8.4s), request impact across 247 timed-out calls, and a request to review recent deploy api-svc-v3.14.2 (rolled out 10:30 UTC), capacity, and scaling health in us-east-1. Escalation filed by Carlos Medina (cmedina, emp ID E-22814).

Continued monitoring after escalation via the Monitoring System igw-prod-latency dashboard and treated the service as resolved from the gateway side once mitigation (adjusted retry/backoff) and ownership transfer to Raj Venkatesh's team were in place for the downstream latency issue. Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) was notified of the interim mitigation and downstream escalation status.

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: Integration jobs from the Integration Gateway to the downstream API began timing out around 11:15 UTC on 2025-12-11, causing failed sync runs and delayed data movement for CustomerDataSync and InternalAPIIntegration in us-east-1. The issue was reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Atlanta application support team. Monitoring on host INTGW-PROD-01.corplabs.internal correlated the failures with elevated downstream API latency and repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses from the API Service endpoint at api-service.corplabs.internal, preventing connectors from completing within the original retry and timeout window. Affected connector jobs included job_4729 and job_4731, both initiated from integration node 10.42.18.55.
root_cause: Elevated latency on the downstream API caused repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses, and the Integration Gateway connector retry/backoff behavior exhausted before requests could complete successfully.
resolution_steps: Validated that the integration API token for service account svc-intgateway remained active (expiry 2026-03-15) so authentication was not contributing to the failures.

Correlated Integration Gateway job failures (job_4729, job_4731) on node 10.42.18.55 with downstream API latency spikes and 504 Gateway Timeout events observed from 11:12 to 11:47 UTC on INTGW-PROD-01.corplabs.internal, as confirmed by Priya Nair (pnair).

Escalated the downstream latency condition to Downstream API Support under ticket DS-1023 — contacted Raj Okonkwo (rokonkwo@corplabs.com) for service-side investigation and stabilization of api-service.corplabs.internal.

Updated the Integration Gateway connector on 10.42.18.55 to use exponential retry/backoff behavior (base 2s, max 5 retries) and increased the request timeout from 30 seconds to 90 seconds to better tolerate temporary latency spikes.

Restarted the affected connectors (CustomerDataSync, InternalAPIIntegration), cleared the backlog of 47 queued sync tasks, and monitored sync processing until timeout errors subsided and delayed data synchronization returned to normal by 12:30 UTC.

title: Orders sync failing
description: Scheduled order-sync processing (job: order-sync-prod-batch-7a) to the external API through the Integration Gateway began failing around 2025-12-12 03:40 UTC with repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (order-processing team lead) after downstream order data failed to appear in the external fulfillment system. Retries are not draining the backlog — queue depth reached ~4,200 pending records on pod order-sync-worker-6d8f4 in us-east-1. Impact is limited by manual retry handling initiated by mdelgado from workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD (10.42.18.93), but the sync workflow remains blocked until gateway timeout behavior, token validity, and possible downstream latency or rate limiting are verified. Contact: mdelgado@corplabs.com / ext 4-7831.
root_cause: Primary cause remains unconfirmed because Integration Gateway logs for the failure window and token rotation history were not provided. Current evidence supports an upstream integration timeout condition affecting outbound calls from the Integration Gateway to the API Service, with the most likely contributors being expired integration credentials, downstream API latency beyond the configured timeout window, or API rate limiting during the 03:30-04:00 UTC period.
resolution_steps: Collect and review Integration Gateway logs from node igw-prod-east-01 for 2025-12-12 03:30–04:00 UTC to identify whether the 504 responses align to authentication failures (HTTP 401/403), rate-limit behavior (HTTP 429), or sustained upstream latency exceeding the 30-second timeout threshold. Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) to coordinate log extraction with the platform team.

Validate the integration token (credential ID: cred-ordersync-ext-2025) used by service account svc-ordersync and compare its rotation or expiry history to the incident start time at 03:40 UTC; rotate the credential immediately via the secrets vault if it is expired or was changed without corresponding gateway configuration updates on igw-prod-east-01.

If credentials are valid, review gateway and downstream API latency during the incident window using Monitoring System traces for pod order-sync-worker-6d8f4 (IP 10.42.18.107) and confirm whether response times exceeded the current order-sync timeout threshold of 30 seconds.

Check for rate-limit (HTTP 429) or retry-exhaustion indicators in igw-prod-east-01 gateway records and, if present, reduce burst behavior by tuning order-sync retry intervals from the current 5-second fixed delay to an exponential backoff policy (initial 2s, max 60s, jitter enabled) rather than increasing immediate retry count.

After evidence is collected, rerun the failed synchronization backlog (~4,200 pending records) in controlled batches of 200 from pod order-sync-worker-6d8f4 and escalate to the downstream API team (contact: Ramon Ortiz, rortiz@corplabs.com) if 504 behavior persists with valid credentials and normal request volume.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — this is Priya Nair from Application Support. Please provide Integration Gateway logs from gateway node igw-prod-east-01 for the 03:30–04:00 UTC window, and confirm whether the API token (credential ID: cred-ordersync-ext-2025) was rotated or if request volume increased during that window. We need to separate timeout, auth, and rate-limit causes. Also, can you verify from your end whether the service account svc-ordersync shows any recent credential changes in the vault? You can reach me at pnair@corplabs.com or ext 4-2209.

title: Integration Gateway - Nightly sync API timeouts (Billing API)
description: Nightly data synchronization from the Integration Gateway to the external Billing API began failing around 02:30 UTC on 2025-12-12 in us-east-1. The integration service account (svc-billing-sync) running on gateway node intgw-prod-east-04 reported multiple jobs receiving 504 Gateway Timeout responses and 30-second request timeouts, causing retries to accumulate and some sync jobs to fail outright. Reported by Marcus Delgado (emp ID EMP-40821) from the Denver application support team. This blocked completion of the scheduled billing data sync until the downstream service recovered and the retry backlog was cleared.
observed_errors: Request to billing API timed out after 30s
root_cause: Elevated latency and upstream instability in the external Billing API caused repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses during the nightly sync window, which exceeded the Integration Gateway timeout and exhausted the configured retry/backoff policy.
resolution_steps: Correlated Integration Gateway failures on intgw-prod-east-04 with Monitoring System alerts (alert ID MON-88412) showing repeated 504 responses and increased downstream billing-service latency (p99 spiking to 45–60s) between approximately 02:28 and 02:40 UTC. Cross-referenced X-Request-Id values req-a83f21c4, req-b90e55d7, req-c12d88a1 to confirm the correlation.

Collected gateway log evidence from intgw-prod-east-04, including timestamped request identifiers and upstream timeout behavior, and Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) escalated the incident to the external Billing API provider contact at billing-ops@externalpay.io for remediation, attaching the evidence package and Monitoring System snapshots.

Coordinated with the downstream provider on a service restart/recovery action to restore normal responsiveness on the billing side. Provider confirmed recovery at approximately 02:52 UTC and attributed the degradation to an internal database connection pool exhaustion.

Adjusted Integration Gateway retry settings on intgw-prod-east-04 by increasing retry attempts from 3 to 5 and extending backoff windows from 10s/20s/30s to 15s/30s/60s/90s/120s so transient upstream latency would be tolerated during recovery. Change approved by team lead Raj Venkatesh (rvenkatesh, EMP-30195).

Validated that API calls from svc-billing-sync were succeeding again with sub-3-second response times, reran the 47 queued nightly sync jobs, and confirmed the retry backlog cleared without further 504 timeout failures by 03:15 UTC.

Documented the escalation path (internal → Priya Nair → billing-ops@externalpay.io), log-correlation approach using X-Request-Id tracing, and revised retry/backoff settings for future nightly sync timeout events. Added runbook entry RB-INT-0064 for the Denver application support team.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm whether gateway logs on intgw-prod-east-04 around 02:30 UTC show upstream 504 responses from the Billing API endpoint and share any request IDs or X-Request-Id values (e.g., from the svc-billing-sync service account logs) so we can correlate with the downstream billing alerts. Also, can you verify whether the issue is isolated to your workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD or visible across the monitoring dashboard? — Priya Nair, Integration Support

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts to Billing API causing delayed data sync
description: Automated monitoring detected that Integration Gateway requests to the Billing API in us-east-1 began timing out around 2025-12-12T09:40:00Z. Outbound calls from integration node INTGW-PROD-04 (10.22.18.97) returned repeated 504 Gateway Timeout responses and some requests exceeded the 30 second timeout window, causing integration jobs to fail and delaying customer billing data synchronization. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the AppIntegrationTeam in Charlotte. The issue affected API-based sync processing on Kubernetes (EKS) and created downstream data freshness impact until Billing API latency was reduced. Ticket opened on behalf of the integration operations group by agent Priya Nair (EMP-40821).
root_cause: Elevated downstream Billing API response latency caused Integration Gateway requests to exceed the configured timeout window, resulting in 504 Gateway Timeout errors and failed sync jobs.
resolution_steps: Correlated the Integration Gateway alert window on INTGW-PROD-04 (source IP 10.22.18.97) with downstream Billing API latency metrics in the Monitoring System and confirmed timeout failures were aligned with increased response times (p99 ~48s) from the dependent service between 09:40 and 11:52 UTC. Analysis performed by Priya Nair (pnair, EMP-40821).

Applied a temporary mitigation by increasing the Integration Gateway request timeout from 30 seconds to 60 seconds on INTGW-PROD-04 to reduce immediate job failures while the dependency issue was investigated. Change logged under CR-20251212-0041 and approved by pnair.

Adjusted the gateway retry and backoff policy on INTGW-PROD-04 (max retries increased from 3 to 5, exponential backoff base set to 2 seconds) to better tolerate transient downstream slowness and allow delayed requests to complete successfully.

Escalated the incident to the Billing API team lead Tomás Reyes (treyes) with evidence of repeated 504 responses and elevated latency observed from Integration Gateway transactions on INTGW-PROD-04. Escalation included distributed trace samples and latency percentile charts from the Monitoring System covering the 09:40–11:52 UTC window.

Validated recovery after the Billing API team reduced service latency (connection pool fix deployed by treyes) by monitoring end-to-end requests from INTGW-PROD-04 and confirming timeout rates dropped to 0% and billing data sync jobs completed successfully. Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) in Charlotte confirmed data freshness restored in the operations dashboard.

title: Expired TLS certificate and incomplete load balancer chain update caused internal TLS
description: Internal users across the Chicago office were trying to access the Internal Web Service (https://internal-ws.corplabs.com) and dependent Service API over TLS, but browsers showed certificate warnings and integrations failed validation with CERT_HAS_EXPIRED, ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR, and certificate verify failed. The issue was first reported by Maria Koduya (emp ID: EMP-40821) and persisted after an earlier remediation by James Harrelson claimed the certificate was renewed and deployed, indicating the outage was still affecting internal-services users behind the F5 load balancer in us-east-1 and blocking normal application access from workstations including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MK.
root_cause: The service certificate was renewed at the Certificate Authority, but the full renewed certificate chain was not correctly applied on the F5 load balancer. As a result, the load balancer continued serving the old expired chain to clients even though application-side renewal activity had been performed.
resolution_steps: Retrieved the renewed server certificate and complete intermediate chain from the internal Certificate Authority and verified the certificate matched the Internal Web Service endpoint naming requirements (CN=internal-ws.corplabs.com, SAN: internal-ws.corplabs.com). Verification performed by Tomás Reyes.

Uploaded the renewed certificate bundle to the F5 load balancer (lb-east-01.corplabs.internal) and explicitly updated the virtual server configuration to use the new full chain instead of the previously served expired chain, correcting the gap left by the earlier incomplete deployment.

Applied the load balancer configuration and reloaded the LB service on lb-east-01.corplabs.internal so the updated certificate chain was actively presented to clients in the Chicago office and all us-east-1 internal-services users.

Validated the served certificate chain from client and load balancer perspectives — confirmed from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MK (10.42.17.89) and additional test hosts that the expired certificate was no longer presented and TLS handshakes completed successfully for the Internal Web Service and Service API. Maria Koduya (koduya) confirmed normal access restored.

Restored certificate monitoring and added load balancer chain verification plus deployment evidence requirements (including post-deployment client-side validation step) to the certificate rotation process to prevent recurrence. Alert subscription updated for pnandakumar@corplabs.com and treyes@corplabs.com.
agent_questions: We can confirm renewal activity at the CA for CN=internal-ws.corplabs.com, but need validation from the active endpoint. Are users still seeing CERT_HAS_EXPIRED and do we have any record that the F5 load balancer chain was explicitly updated? I've asked jharrelson to provide deployment logs from the earlier attempt. — Agent: Priya Nandakumar (pnandakumar@corplabs.com)

title: Expired TLS certificate on Internal Web Service behind Load Balancer
description: Internal users and dependent services were trying to reach the svc-internal endpoint (svc-internal.corplabs.internal) over TLS through the load balancer LB-EAST-02, but clients began showing certificate warnings and rejecting the connection. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office, who noticed that requests from her workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MC were returning NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID errors. The load balancer presented an expired certificate (CN=svc-internal.corplabs.internal, expired 2025-12-10T00:00:00Z) and an incomplete chain after the renewal window was missed, which blocked normal access to the internal web service and caused TLS handshake failures for internal integrations in us-east-1. Multiple teams including the payroll integration service (contact: David Ortiz, emp ID E-40291) confirmed downstream failures.
observed_errors: certificate expired presented by load balancer
root_cause: The svc-internal certificate presented by the load balancer expired, and the load balancer configuration was not updated with the renewed intermediate certificate. Certificate monitoring and renewal alerting also failed to notify before expiration, allowing the invalid chain to remain in production.
resolution_steps: Renew the svc-internal TLS certificate (CN=svc-internal.corplabs.internal) with the internal Certificate Authority CA-EAST-01 and verify the renewed certificate matches the service endpoint name and SAN entries. Renewal performed by Raj Patel (rpatel, E-50184).

Deploy the renewed server certificate and the full trusted chain, including the renewed CorpLabs Internal Intermediate CA G2 certificate, to load balancer LB-EAST-02 serving svc-internal. Deployment coordinated by Lisa Nguyen (lnguyen).

Remove the temporary self-signed certificate workaround from LB-EAST-02 listener configuration and update the load balancer certificate chain configuration so clients receive the correct full chain (root → intermediate → leaf) for svc-internal.corplabs.internal.

Validate from a client perspective that load balancer LB-EAST-02 now presents a non-expired certificate (new expiry 2026-12-10) and a complete chain, and confirm TLS handshakes succeed for dependent internal services. Verification performed from WORKSTATION-PC-MC (10.42.17.88) and WORKSTATION-LX-RP (10.42.18.203) in the Arlington office.

Restore certificate renewal monitoring and alerting on CA-EAST-01 for svc-internal.corplabs.internal, re-enable the 30-day expiry alert rule, configure notifications to infra-alerts@corplabs.com and lnguyen@corplabs.com, then test that certificate expiration warnings and renewal job failures generate notifications before the next renewal window.
agent_questions: Please confirm whether clients are failing on certificate expiry only or also reporting chain trust issues from the load balancer endpoint LB-EAST-02 for svc-internal.corplabs.internal. Maria Chen (mchen) reported the initial browser warnings from 10.42.17.88 — can the network team verify what the load balancer is actually presenting? Also, has anyone checked whether the renewal job on CA-EAST-01 ran successfully? — Raj Patel, Infrastructure Support

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal service TLS outage
description: Users and internal integrations were trying to access the Internal Web Service at internal-web.svc.cluster.local, but browsers showed certificate warnings and dependent API calls began failing TLS validation. The issue was first reported by platform engineer Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from the Austin office at approximately 05:15 UTC. Monitoring detected TLS handshake failures from multiple client IPs including 10.42.17.88, and load balancer logs on LB-EAST-01 showed an expired certificate was being presented, causing an internal service outage until the certificate chain on the load balancer was corrected.
observed_errors: automation job error: access denied when writing LB config
root_cause: The TLS certificate for internal-web.svc.cluster.local expired, and the replacement certificate chain was not deployed to the load balancer because the automated renewal job failed with access denied due to missing permissions to update load balancer configuration.
resolution_steps: Issued a replacement TLS certificate from the internal Certificate Authority for internal-web.svc.cluster.local and exported the full certificate chain (new serial 5B:A1:09:EE:44:C7), performed by Kevin Briggs (kbriggs, EMP-40291).
Uploaded and applied the renewed certificate chain to the internal load balancer instance LB-EAST-01 serving the service endpoint, replacing the expired leaf certificate serial 3A:7F:02:CB:91:DE.
Reloaded the load balancer configuration on LB-EAST-01 so the new certificate chain was presented to clients, verified by kbriggs at 05:42 UTC.

Validated successful TLS handshakes from internal clients including workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (10.42.17.88) and WORKSTATION-DESK-RP, and browser access by Maria Chen and Raj Patel, confirming the expired certificate warning was cleared.

Corrected the renewal automation permissions so the service account svc-certrenew can update load balancer configuration on LB-EAST-01, reverting the RBAC change made by dwhitfield, then tested the renewal workflow with a dry run and restored certificate expiry monitoring with alerts routed to kbriggs@corplabs.com.
agent_questions: Please confirm whether users are seeing certificate date warnings at the service URL https://internal-web.svc.cluster.local and whether dependent internal API calls through internal-api-gateway are failing with TLS handshake errors. Can you also confirm which user accounts or workstations have reported the issue? — Kevin Briggs (EMP-40291), Infrastructure Support

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS failures
description: Users and internal services were trying to reach internal.web.internal over HTTPS, but browsers displayed certificate warnings and dependent API clients failed TLS handshakes. The load balancer (LB-PROD-F5-01) in front of the internal web service was presenting an expired certificate and outdated chain, which blocked normal access to the internal web service and caused downstream internal API failures in us-east-1. The issue was initially reported by Maria Chen (emp ID EMP-40291) from the Portland office, who noticed API integration tests failing at approximately 11:05 UTC. Additional reports came in from developers on the internal-developers Slack channel, including jparker and dmorales, confirming that both browser-based and programmatic access to internal.web.internal were affected.
platform: F5 Load Balancer / Linux web nodes
observed_errors: 502 bad gateway (due to TLS handshake failure at LB)
root_cause: The TLS certificate for internal.web.internal expired on the load balancer, and the renewed leaf certificate plus intermediate chain had not been deployed, causing certificate validation failures and TLS handshake errors.
resolution_steps: Requested and obtained a renewed TLS certificate for internal.web.internal from the internal Certificate Authority (serial 8B:12:D4:F7, valid 2025-12-13 through 2026-12-13) before restoring service. The CSR was generated by rpatel and approved by the PKI team lead Sarah Lin (slin, EMP-60112).

Installed the renewed leaf certificate and full intermediate certificate chain on the production load balancer that terminates TLS for the internal web service. The certificate bundle was deployed to LB-PROD-F5-01 (10.200.1.15) by rpatel at 11:40 UTC, replacing the expired leaf (serial 4A:7C:3E:91) and outdated intermediate with the current chain from the internal CA vault.

Reloaded the load balancer TLS listener so the endpoint stopped presenting the expired certificate and began serving the updated chain. The reload was executed on LB-PROD-F5-01 at 11:42 UTC with zero dropped connections using the graceful reload procedure.

Validated the HTTPS endpoint from multiple internal client perspectives to confirm the certificate subject matched the service name and the handshake completed successfully. Verification was performed from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (10.42.17.88, user mchen) in the Portland office and from a test host in Austin (10.42.22.61, user jparker), both returning valid certificate chains with no warnings.

Re-enabled and tested certificate expiry monitoring and renewal alerting so future notifications trigger ahead of the renewal window. The alert rule for internal.web.internal was restored in the monitoring platform with 30-day and 7-day expiry thresholds, and test notifications were confirmed delivered to infra-certs@corplabs.com and the on-call channel.

title: Internal Web Service TLS outage
description: Internal staff in the Arlington data center were trying to access the Internal Web Service over HTTPS for the internal-service-api and internal-dashboard endpoints (internal-service.company.local), but browsers showed certificate warnings and requests through the F5 load balancer (lb-prod-east-01.company.local) failed TLS negotiation. Users could not reach the service securely, and monitoring reported TLS handshake failures and 502 responses in us-east-1-dc1 after the service certificate passed its expiration on 2025-12-13 without the renewed chain being deployed. Initially reported by Maria Castillo (mcastillo@company.local) from the Finance team, who was unable to load the internal dashboard from her workstation WORKSTATION-MC-FIN.
root_cause: The TLS certificate for internal-service.company.local issued by the Internal Certificate Authority expired and the renewed full certificate chain was not deployed to the F5 load balancer, causing TLS handshake rejection and HTTPS outage for the Internal Web Service.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the presented certificate for internal-service.company.local was expired (Not After: 2025-12-13T00:00:00Z) and identified that the active chain on the load balancer lb-prod-east-01.company.local was no longer valid for client trust. Verification performed by Derek Huang (dhuang) from the Arlington NOC.

Requested and obtained a renewed TLS certificate from the Internal Certificate Authority for the affected service endpoint (CN=internal-service.company.local, SAN: internal-service.company.local, internal-dashboard.company.local). CSR generated by dhuang, approved by Nicole Williams (nwilliams).

Installed the renewed certificate and complete certificate chain on the Internal Web Service endpoint (internal-svc-prod-01.company.local) and reloaded the service TLS configuration. Deployment verified by dhuang via openssl s_client handshake test.

Updated the F5 load balancer (lb-prod-east-01.company.local) to present the renewed certificate chain on VIP 10.50.1.20:443 and reloaded the affected HTTPS virtual service. Confirmed chain validity from client subnet 10.22.14.0/24 by Derek Huang.

Validated successful end-to-end TLS handshakes from client (WORKSTATION-MC-FIN at 10.22.14.87) and monitoring perspectives across regions, and restored certificate expiration alerting to PagerDuty (notifying infra-certs-team@company.local) to prevent recurrence. Maria Castillo and James Okafor confirmed service access restored. Closure approved by Nicole Williams (nwilliams).
agent_questions: Hi Maria — thanks for reporting this. Please confirm whether users are seeing browser certificate warnings specifically for internal-service.company.local and whether failures occur only over HTTPS through the load balancer (lb-prod-east-01.company.local). Also, can you confirm if the issue is affecting users in Arlington only or other sites as well? I'm assigning this to our network infrastructure lead, Derek Huang (dhuang), for immediate investigation. You can also reach me at ext. 4127 or nwilliams@company.local if you have additional details.

title: Expired TLS certificate from internal CA causing TLS failures on Load Balancer
description: Internal employees at the Denver office were trying to access the Internal Web Service at https://portal.internal.corplabs.com, but browsers and monitoring began reporting certificate warnings and failed TLS validation. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID: E-40291) via email to the service desk. TLS captures from workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (IP 10.42.17.88) showed the Kubernetes ingress/load balancer presenting a certificate issued by the internal CA that expired on 2025-12-13, causing ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID and blocked HTTPS access to the service until the certificate and full chain were updated on the load balancer.
root_cause: The load balancer continued presenting an expired TLS certificate issued by the internal Certificate Authority because the renewed certificate and full trust chain were available in the CA store but were not deployed and referenced in the load balancer configuration before the prior certificate expired.
resolution_steps: Retrieve the renewed server certificate and complete intermediate/root chain from the internal Certificate Authority for the Internal Web Service endpoint (CN=portal.internal.corplabs.com). Kevin Orozco (korozco) downloaded the renewed bundle portal-2025.pem and full chain from the CA portal.

Replace the expired certificate bundle in the load balancer certificate store and update the load balancer configuration to reference the new certificate and full chain instead of the old file/path. Specifically, the ingress TLS secret was updated to point from /etc/tls/certs/portal-2024.pem to /etc/tls/certs/portal-2025.pem by korozco.

Reload or restart the load balancer/ingress process so the active listener begins presenting the renewed certificate. Kevin Orozco (korozco) performed a rolling restart of the ingress controller pods in us-east-1 at 2025-12-13T23:15:00Z to pick up the new TLS secret.

Validate from a client and from the load balancer side that the presented certificate is unexpired, matches the service hostname, and the full chain validates without missing or expired intermediates. Maria Chen (mchen) and Raj Patel (rpatel) confirmed from their workstations (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC and WORKSTATION-DESK-RP) that the certificate warning was resolved and HTTPS access to https://portal.internal.corplabs.com was restored.

Restore and tune certificate expiry monitoring and renewal reminders so alerts fire before expiration and deployment tasks are tracked through completion. Lisa Nguyen (lnguyen) re-enabled the cert-expiry-30d alert subscription and added a new cert-expiry-7d critical alert. Deployment tracking was added to the runbook so that certificate renewal is not marked complete until the load balancer configuration is verified by the infrastructure team.
agent_questions: Please confirm whether the TLS warning is seen by multiple users and whether the endpoint certificate details show the same expiration date across browsers or monitoring checks. Specifically, can you verify from your machine (hostname and IP) and ask a colleague such as your team lead to check from their browser as well?

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage
description: Users were trying to access the Internal Web Service (https://appportal.corplabs.internal) through the internal nginx load balancer at lb-web-east.corplabs.internal, but browsers showed expired-certificate warnings (NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) and dependent clients failed TLS handshakes. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen from the Austin office at approximately 04:20 UTC on 2025-12-14. The service became unavailable over TLS because the presented certificate (CN=appportal.corplabs.internal, issued by CorpLabs Internal CA) had passed its expiration date of 2025-12-13 and the updated certificate chain had not been deployed on the load balancer, blocking normal internal application access for the internal_users group.
root_cause: The Internal Web Service TLS certificate expired, and the renewed certificate chain was not applied on the load balancer. The outage was prolonged because near-expiration certificate monitoring was not active to trigger renewal before the expiry date.
resolution_steps: Requested and issued a renewed TLS certificate (CN=appportal.corplabs.internal, new serial 5B:1D:09:FA, valid until 2026-12-13) from the internal Certificate Authority (CorpLabs Internal CA) for the Internal Web Service, processed by Kevin Marsh.

Installed the renewed certificate and private key on the Internal Web Service backend at appportal.corplabs.internal:8443 and verified the service was configured to present the updated certificate via openssl s_client check from 10.22.45.88.

Updated the certificate bundle and intermediate chain on the load balancer lb-web-east.corplabs.internal under /etc/nginx/ssl/, then Raj Patel reloaded the nginx configuration so clients received the corrected chain with the new leaf and current intermediate certificates.

Validated successful TLS handshakes from internal clients in Austin and Raleigh through the load balancer and confirmed browser certificate warnings no longer appeared. Maria Chen verified access from WORKSTATION-MC-4417 at 10.22.45.88 was restored without errors.

Restored and documented certificate-expiry monitoring for CN=appportal.corplabs.internal with 60-day, 30-day, and 7-day alert thresholds sending to infra-certs@corplabs.com, and updated the renewal policy to ensure alerts occur before future certificate expiration. Kevin Marsh confirmed the monitoring rule is active in the platform dashboard.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — we are checking whether the certificate issue is on the service itself or on the internal load balancer path (lb-web-east.corplabs.internal). Could you confirm whether users are seeing browser certificate warnings when navigating to https://appportal.corplabs.internal, and whether the failure occurs only when accessing through the load balancer? Also, please let us know if direct access to the backend on port 8443 shows the same warning. I've looped in Raj Patel from the network team for the load balancer side. — Kevin Marsh, Infrastructure Support

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage
description: Users and internal service clients were trying to reach https://internal.example.corp, but beginning around 08:20 UTC on 2025-12-14 the endpoint started returning browser certificate warnings and TLS handshake failures. The issue was first reported by Priya Nair (priya.nair@example.corp) from the Austin office, who noticed ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID when accessing the portal from her workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN. Affected users across the internal developers and services group could not safely open the internal web service, and dependent API clients saw HTTPS failures across multiple zones (us-central-1a, us-central-1b, us-central-1c). The issue impacted the internal web service behind the load balancer (lb-prod-central-01.infra.example.corp) after the service certificate expired and the load balancer continued presenting an outdated certificate chain. Ticket escalated by Marcus Delgado (emp ID E-40821) from the infrastructure operations team.
observed_errors: 502 via load balancer when TLS negotiation fails
root_cause: The TLS certificate for internal.example.corp expired, and the load balancer continued serving a stale certificate chain. Certificate renewal alerting was not active, so the expiration was not detected and remediated before client TLS validation began failing.
resolution_steps: Issued a new TLS certificate for internal.example.corp (new serial 7B:22:AF:01:CC:D4:90:E3, valid until 2026-12-14) through the Certificate Authority, requested by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, E-40821), before restoring production traffic handling.

Installed the renewed certificate on the Internal Web Service application nodes in us-central-1a/1b/1c and verified via openssl s_client that the local service presented the expected certificate for the endpoint name internal.example.corp with the updated serial and validity dates.

Updated the Load Balancer lb-prod-central-01.infra.example.corp to use the renewed certificate and full intermediate chain (leaf + intermediate CA), then rolled the configuration across all LB nodes in us-central-1 to remove the stale chain. Configuration change executed by Jenna Whitfield (jwhitfield) from the network_team.

Validated end-to-end TLS negotiation from multiple zones (us-central-1a, 1b, 1c) and from client IPs including 10.42.17.88 (Priya Nair, Austin) and 10.42.22.105 (Tomás Reyes, API integrations). Confirmed browser warnings and API client handshake failures were no longer occurring. Service restored at approximately 11:15 UTC.
