Restored certificate renewal alerting in the Certificate Management platform for internal.example.corp with a 30-day and 7-day pre-expiry notification threshold, subscribed to mdelgado@example.corp and infra-ops@example.corp, and added recurring certificate health checks so future expirations are detected before the renewal window closes.
agent_questions: Can you confirm whether users are seeing browser certificate warnings (e.g., ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) versus a generic application error, and whether API clients are failing during TLS handshake or after connection establishment? Also, could you verify whether the issue is isolated to a specific zone or affects all zones behind lb-prod-central-01.infra.example.corp? Please share any screenshots or client-side error output if available. — Marcus Delgado, Infrastructure Operations

title: Expired TLS certificate caused Internal Web Service TLS outage — resolved
description: Users in the Austin office were trying to access the Internal Web Service (https://internal-web.corplabs.com) and dependent internal API endpoints, but browsers displayed NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID warnings and automated health checks failed TLS handshakes. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) from the DevOps team at approximately 15:45 UTC on 2025-12-14. The service began presenting an expired or incomplete certificate chain after a renewal was performed at the internal Certificate Authority without fully updating the HAProxy load balancer configuration on LB-FRONT-01. This blocked normal HTTPS access for internal users across the Austin and Denver locations and caused the incident to reappear after the initial partial fix attempted by the on-call engineer.
root_cause: The TLS certificate was renewed at the Certificate Authority, but the full certificate chain was not deployed to the HAProxy load balancer serving the Internal Web Service. The issue recurred after a scheduled certificate renewal performed on 2025-12-16 because the renewed certificate and full chain were not consistently deployed across all three load balancer nodes (LB-EAST-01, LB-EAST-02, LB-EAST-03), leaving the service intermittently unavailable over TLS and causing user-visible trust errors for approximately 14 hours.
observed_errors: 502 Bad Gateway (LB when backend TLS fails)
root_cause: The service certificate renewal was completed, but deployment was incomplete: not all load balancer nodes received the updated full certificate chain. As a result, some clients were served an expired or incomplete chain, triggering certificate warnings, TLS handshake failures, and intermittent 502 errors when backend TLS validation failed.
resolution_steps: Renewed and validated the TLS certificate with the CorpLabs Internal Certificate Authority, confirming the new expiration date (2026-12-17) and endpoint name coverage for internalapp.corplabs.com and *.internalapp.corplabs.com before redeployment. Validation performed by Robert Kovacs (rkovacs).

Propagated the renewed certificate and complete certificate chain (leaf + CorpLabs Issuing CA G2 intermediate) to all three load balancer nodes (LB-EAST-01, LB-EAST-02, LB-EAST-03) rather than the partially updated subset, using the centralized cert-deploy automation pipeline.

Reloaded TLS configuration on each load balancer node via nginx -s reload and verified all three nodes were serving the same leaf certificate (serial 8B:12:D4:77) and intermediate chain by running openssl s_client against each node's direct IP.

Deployed the renewed certificate to the Internal Web Service Kubernetes endpoints in the us-east-1 cluster and restarted service pods (kubectl rollout restart deployment/internalapp) so active listeners presented the updated certificate consistently. Confirmed by David Pratt from the network team.

Re-enabled and corrected certificate renewal alerting (suppressed since 2025-12-16T20:15Z by rkovacs), then updated the load balancer certificate deployment playbook to require full-node propagation across all LB nodes and post-change TLS handshake validation from both client and LB perspectives. Added automated openssl verification for every node in the pool before closing renewal change requests.
agent_questions: We are rechecking the certificate presented by the internal service endpoint https://internalapp.corplabs.com. Please confirm whether users are still seeing the browser certificate warning on all paths or only intermittently after the earlier renewal change pushed by rkovacs yesterday evening. We need to determine if the issue is isolated to specific load balancer nodes or affecting the entire cluster.

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage

resolution_steps: Requested and obtained a renewed TLS certificate (CN=*.corp.internal) from the internal Certificate Authority for the internal web service endpoint. The renewal request was submitted by Kevin Marsh (kmarsh) and approved within 20 minutes.

Installed the renewed server certificate and complete intermediate chain (CorpLabs Internal CA G2) on load balancer LB-EAST-VIP-02 TLS virtual server, replacing the expired certificate bundle. Installation performed by Priya Nair (pnair).

Restarted the TLS termination process on load balancer LB-EAST-VIP-02 so the updated certificate and chain were actively presented to clients. Reload was confirmed successful at 2025-12-17T21:02:00Z by Priya Nair.

Validated the HTTPS endpoint (https://appportal.corp.internal) from the client side (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD at 10.42.17.88) and load balancer side to confirm the certificate was no longer expired and the full chain completed successfully. Marcus Delgado confirmed browser access was restored without warnings.

Re-enabled and tested certificate expiration monitoring and renewal alerting in Nagios for *.corp.internal to ensure future renewals are detected at least 30 days before expiry. Kevin Marsh verified alert delivery to the infrastructure on-call rotation managed by Raj Venkatesh.
agent_questions: We are seeing TLS handshake failures and certificate warnings on the internal service at https://appportal.corp.internal. title: Internal Web Service TLS certificate expired, causing TLS warnings and service unavailability
description: Users were trying to access the internal web service at internal.websvc.corp starting around 2025-12-18 08:12 UTC, but browsers displayed NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID warnings and TLS connections failed. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID E-40291) from the Chicago office, who noticed the certificate warning while accessing the HR onboarding portal served behind internal.websvc.corp. Internal health checks running from health-checker on the Kubernetes cluster in us-east-1 also began returning 502 errors on TLS backend probes, preventing normal access to the service from inside the network. The load balancer (lb-prod-east-01.infra.corp) was still presenting a stale certificate bundle with an incomplete chain, which compounded the issue until both the certificate and chain were corrected.
root_cause: The TLS certificate for internal.websvc.corp expired, and the load balancer continued serving the old certificate with an incomplete chain. In parallel, the certificate expiry monitoring threshold was misconfigured, so the renewal alert did not fire before expiration.
resolution_steps: Issued a replacement TLS certificate for internal.websvc.corp (new serial 5B:8D:4E:A2, valid 2025-12-18 to 2026-12-17) from the internal Certificate Authority (CorpCA) before returning the service to production traffic. Certificate request submitted by Samantha Liu (sliu@corp.internal).

Deployed the renewed certificate to the internal web service endpoint running on the Kubernetes cluster in us-east-1 and verified that the presented certificate matched the service hostname internal.websvc.corp with correct SAN entries. Deployment confirmed by ops engineer Samantha Liu.

Updated the full certificate chain on lb-prod-east-01.infra.corp, replacing the stale certificate bundle (dated 2024-12-15) with the new chain including the renewed CorpCA Intermediate G2, and reloaded the TLS process so the new chain was actively served to all client connections.

Corrected the CertWatch certificate expiry monitoring threshold from 0 days to the org-standard 30 days for internal.websvc.corp and validated that renewal and expiry alerts would trigger with sufficient lead time before future expirations. Alert recipient list updated to include rpatel@corp.internal and sliu@corp.internal.

Confirmed successful TLS handshakes and healthy probe results from multiple internal regions (us-east-1, us-west-2), including verification from monitoring nodes at 10.22.50.88 and 10.34.12.55, then updated the certificate rotation runbook to include chain validation during deployment and mandatory post-deployment verification from at least two network zones.
agent_questions: Hi team — can you run an openssl s_client check against internal.websvc.corp:443 and share the certificate details including expiration date and SAN entries? Also, please confirm whether lb-prod-east-01.infra.corp has the updated full chain deployed, and check with Raj Patel (rpatel@corp.internal) on the infrastructure monitoring side whether any certificate expiry alerts fired before the outage window. We need to understand if the CertWatch alerting threshold was set correctly.

title: Internal Web Service TLS outage
description: Users across the Portland office were unable to access the internal web service at https://portal.internal.corplabs.com over TLS starting around 12:45 UTC on 2025-12-18. Browsers displayed NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID warnings and internal health checks on the Kubernetes cluster failed TLS handshakes after the service certificate (CN=portal.internal.corplabs.com) expired. An initial renewal was applied by the infrastructure team, but internal consumers routed through the F5 load balancer (lb-east-01.corplabs.internal) still received the expired leaf certificate, causing continued service unavailability for approximately 200 users in the Internal Services group. The incident was reopened by Marcus Delgado after the first closure, and was not fully resolved until certificate deployment and chain validation were completed end to end across both the backend pods and the load balancer termination point.
root_cause: The renewed TLS leaf certificate was issued, but the load balancer continued serving the expired leaf certificate and chain because the renewal/deploy workflow did not fully propagate the updated certificate to the LB. Certificate monitoring and renewal alerting also failed to trigger the expected redeploy validation before expiration.
resolution_steps: Renewed the TLS leaf certificate for portal.internal.corplabs.com through the internal Certificate Authority (ca.corplabs.internal), generating a new certificate (serial 7A:3F:01:CC, SHA-256 fingerprint verified) and confirmed the replacement certificate validity dates (2025-12-18 through 2026-12-17) and SAN coverage for portal.internal.corplabs.com.

Updated the load balancer lb-east-01.corplabs.internal with the renewed certificate, private key, and full certificate chain (leaf + intermediate CA), then reloaded the LB configuration via the Load Balancer Controller so it stopped presenting the expired leaf certificate (serial 4E:91:DA:07). Reload confirmed by Priya Nair at 13:52 UTC.

Redeployed the renewed certificate to the internal web service pods (portal-web-* in namespace prod-services) via kubectl rollout restart to keep the service endpoint and LB termination points in sync, verified by Rachel Owens.

Validated TLS handshakes and certificate presentation from both internal (10.42.17.88, WORKSTATION-PC-MD) and external paths to confirm the renewed chain was being served without date or trust errors. Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) confirmed access restored from the Portland office.

Restored certificate expiration monitoring and renewal alerting (re-enabled Prometheus alert rule 'cert-expiry-30d'), and added an operational check to verify load balancer certificate sync after future renewals. Alert notifications configured to infra-certs@corplabs.com and on-call channel.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm whether the certificate warning appears only on the public service path (https://portal.internal.corplabs.com) or also from internal consumers behind the load balancer (lb-east-01.corplabs.internal), and whether the browser still shows a date-invalid certificate (NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID). Could you also share the hostname or IP you're testing from? We want to rule out DNS caching. — Priya Nair, Infrastructure Engineering

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal web service TLS outage
description: Internal users and monitoring were trying to reach svc-internal-web through the ALB (alb-prod-east-01.corplabs.internal), but starting around 08:15 UTC on 2025-12-19 the service began failing TLS handshakes and showing certificate warnings. Dependent internal clients including the internal-admin-portal could not establish secure connections, causing the internal web service to be unavailable over TLS in us-east-1. Additional reports came in from employees in the Raleigh office confirming the same behavior.
root_cause: The TLS leaf certificate issued by the internal Certificate Authority expired, and the renewed certificate chain was not deployed on the ALB, so the load balancer continued presenting the old expired chain. A misconfigured suppression filter on the certificate renewal alert also prevented timely notification before expiration.
resolution_steps: Requested and issued a renewed TLS certificate (new serial 6F:A1:22:D4:CC:18) for svc-internal-web.corplabs.internal from the internal Certificate Authority, coordinated by Sandra Okafor (sokafor@corplabs.com), before revalidating the certificate subject and intended endpoint coverage including SAN entries.

Cleared the load balancer certificate cache on alb-prod-east-01.corplabs.internal and forced a fresh TLS presentation to remove the stale expired certificate (serial 4A:7C:3E:91:BB:02) from active handshakes.

Validated the service endpoint from multiple internal client paths — including WORKSTATION-PC-MCHEN (10.42.17.88) in Arlington and WORKSTATION-LT-DHOLL (10.42.23.115) in Raleigh — and through the load balancer to confirm the certificate expiration date (2026-12-19), chain trust, and successful TLS handshake behavior. Maria Chen and Derek Holloway confirmed service restoration.

Removed the suppression filter (rule ID CW-SUPP-0447, originally created by jparker) from the certificate renewal monitoring rule in CertWatch and tested alert delivery to sokafor@corplabs.com and the #infra-certs Slack channel so future certificate expiry conditions are detected before service impact.

title: Expired TLS certificate caused Internal Web Service TLS outages
description: Internal users and dependent services were trying to reach the internal-api HTTPS endpoint (internal-api.corplabs.internal), but starting 2025-12-19 09:13 UTC the service presented an expired TLS certificate. The issue was first reported by Rachel Nguyen (EMP-40291) from the Austin office, who noticed browsers showed certificate warnings (ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) when accessing internal-api from her workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (10.42.17.88). root_cause: The Internal Web Service certificate expired, and the automated renewal process did not successfully update the renewed certificate and full chain on the Load Balancer. resolution_steps: Obtain and validate a renewed TLS certificate from the Internal CA for internal-api, confirming the certificate subject and SANs matched the service endpoint. Update the Kubernetes secret used by the Internal Web Service with the renewed certificate material and perform a controlled pod restart so the service consumed the new certificate. The secret tls-internal-api in namespace web-services was patched by Marcus Delgado at 12:34 UTC, and a rolling restart of the internal-api deployment (3 replicas) completed by 12:37 UTC.

Correct the certificate chain order and import the renewed certificate plus intermediates to the Load Balancer, then reload the Load Balancer configuration so clients were served the current full chain. The corrected bundle (leaf → IntCA-Corp-G2 → RootCA-Corp) was imported to LB-EAST-01 by Marcus Delgado and the configuration was reloaded at 12:41 UTC. Priya Sharma (psharma) confirmed from WORKSTATION-DESKTOP-PS (10.55.22.103) in the Boston office that the analytics-pipeline TLS calls resumed successfully.

Run end-to-end TLS validation from representative internal clients and CI paths to confirm successful handshakes, no certificate date warnings, and normal HTTPS connectivity to internal-api. Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen@corplabs.com) verified from her workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN (10.42.17.88) in the Austin office that browser access and curl tests returned valid certificate responses with no warnings. CI pipeline tls-smoke-test passed at 12:48 UTC.

Restore certificate expiry monitoring and validate the automated renewal workflow with alerting set before expiration, including a dry-run or job-history verification to confirm future renewals will update the served chain. Marcus Delgado re-enabled the certificate expiry monitoring rule in the observability platform with a 30-day and 7-day pre-expiry alert threshold, and updated the cert-renew-job-east webhook URL to point to the current LB-EAST-01 API endpoint. A dry-run of the renewal job was executed at 13:05 UTC and confirmed successful chain deployment to the Load Balancer. Alert notification was verified via email to infra-certs@corplabs.com and phone 303-719-5548 (on-call rotation).

The service could not be accessed normally over HTTPS because the presented certificate had passed its validity date (expired 2025-12-20T00:00:00Z) and the load balancer LB-CENTRAL-04.infra.internal was still serving an outdated certificate chain containing the old intermediate CA. Automated health checks from the CI/CD pipeline on host WORKSTATION-BUILD-MD also began failing with SSL errors around the same time.
observed_errors: curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: certificate has expired
root_cause: The TLS leaf certificate for auth.internal.example expired on 2025-12-20. A suppressed renewal alert prevented timely renewal response, and the updated certificate chain was not deployed to the load balancer, causing client certificate validation failures and TLS handshake errors.
resolution_steps: Reissued a valid TLS certificate (serial 7B:22:E1:A5, valid 2025-12-20 through 2026-12-20) for auth.internal.example from the internal Certificate Authority (CA-ROOT-CENTRAL.infra.internal). Certificate reissuance was performed by Tomás Rivera (trivera).

Deployed the renewed leaf certificate and full certificate chain — including the current intermediate CA (CN=Internal Issuing CA G3) — to the load balancer LB-CENTRAL-04.infra.internal configuration serving the internal web service on vip 10.200.1.50:443.

Restarted the affected load balancer TLS listener on LB-CENTRAL-04.infra.internal and reloaded the service endpoints so the new certificate chain was actively presented to clients. Reload completed at 2025-12-20T12:05:00Z with no dropped connections.

Validated the endpoint from client and browser perspectives — tested from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN (pnair, 10.42.18.77) and WORKSTATION-BUILD-MD (svc-authtest) — to confirm the certificate dates, hostname match (SAN: auth.internal.example), and full trust chain were correct and TLS handshakes succeeded without errors.

Restored certificate monitoring by having Jayesh Kumar (jkumar) remove the suppression rule SUPP-2025-1110 from the cert-monitor pipeline and added a pre-expiry renewal/runbook check at 60-day and 30-day thresholds to prevent missed renewals. Alert recipients updated to include mdelgado@internal.example and the platform-eng-oncall@internal.example distribution list.

resolution_steps: Verified the affected devices (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RN for rnguyen, WORKSTATION-DESKTOP-MD for mdelgado, WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PK for pkapoor) were still referencing an older compliance policy revision (CompliancePolicy-Encryption-Check-v1) during evaluation and identified the stale encryption compliance assignment in the Arlington Mobile Workforce group.

Provided user guidance to Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen@corplabs.com), Marcus Delgado, and Priya Kapoor for the remaining edge cases to confirm local encryption state via the Company Portal app and reboot the device, then rechecked compliance until status updated successfully. title: Internal DNS names failing to resolve from corporate resolver
description: Internal users and dependent services across the Denver office were trying to resolve hostnames under corp.local through the corporate DNS resolver (dns-resolver-01.corp.local, 10.20.1.10), but lookups intermittently returned NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, or outdated A records instead of the current internal addresses. The issue was first reported by Marcus Ellison (EMP-40821) from the infrastructure team, who noticed that internal-portal.corp.local, service-discovery.corp.local, and inventory-api.corp.local were unreachable by name from his workstation WORKSTATION-DELL-ME (10.20.44.87). Monitoring indicated the authoritative internal DNS servers (ns1-auth.corp.local, ns2-auth.corp.local) had updated records while the corporate resolver continued serving stale cached responses from corp-dc-1. Several other users including Priya Nagarajan also confirmed intermittent failures from their machines.
root_cause: Corporate DNS resolver cache contained stale internal A records and continued serving outdated answers after authoritative corp.local zone records had been updated.
resolution_steps: Flushed the stale cache entries on the primary corporate DNS resolver (dns-resolver-01.corp.local / 10.20.1.10) using rndc flush to remove outdated A records (e.g., 10.10.10.5) being returned for affected corp.local hosts including internal-portal.corp.local, service-discovery.corp.local, and inventory-api.corp.local.

Verified the authoritative internal DNS zone contents on ns1-auth.corp.local and ns2-auth.corp.local for impacted records and confirmed the current addresses (10.20.30.15, 10.20.30.22, 10.20.30.40) were correct on the authoritative servers. SOA serial and zone transfer status validated between both authoritative nodes.

Adjusted TTL values for the affected zone records from 86400 seconds (24 hours) to 3600 seconds (1 hour) to reduce the likelihood and duration of long-lived stale cache entries after future record changes. Change approved by Raj Mehta and applied to the corp.local zone on ns1-auth.corp.local.

Validated name resolution from representative clients — Marcus Ellison's workstation WORKSTATION-DELL-ME (10.20.44.87) and Priya Nagarajan's workstation WORKSTATION-HP-PN (10.20.44.93) — and Network Monitoring paths to confirm the resolver now returned the same current addresses as the authoritative servers. All three affected service endpoints confirmed reachable by FQDN.

Documented the cache validation and flush procedure (rndc flush on dns-resolver-01.corp.local) in the DNS support playbook and continued post-change monitoring via Network Monitoring for 48 hours for recurrence. Sent closure notification to mellison@corpnet.com and pnagarajan@corpnet.com confirming resolution.
agent_questions: Comparing affected corp.local lookups between the corporate resolver (dns-resolver-01.corp.local / 10.20.1.10) and authoritative DNS servers (ns1-auth.corp.local, ns2-auth.corp.local) now. Running nslookup and dig queries for internal-portal.corp.local, service-discovery.corp.local, and inventory-api.corp.local from Marcus Ellison's workstation WORKSTATION-DELL-ME at 10.20.44.87 and from the Network Monitoring probe in Denver. Need to confirm whether failures are stale answers at the resolver or missing records in the internal zone. — Raj Mehta, Network Engineering

title: Intermittent NXDOMAIN for internal host 'app-db.internal' from one client subnet
description: Users on client subnet 10.20.30.0/24 (primarily the finance team in the Columbus office) were trying to resolve the internal database host app-db.internal, but lookups intermittently returned NXDOMAIN while the same name resolved successfully from other subnets. The issue was originally reported by Maria Gonzalez (mgonzalez@corplabs.com, emp ID FIN-40821) who noticed her application dashboard could not reach the internal database dependency by hostname in corp-datacenter-1. No recent DNS record change was logged, and Maria did not have access to internal DNS zone data or resolver configuration, so resolver path and forwarding behavior required verification by the network team.
root_cause: Subnet-specific DNS resolution was caused by an affected resolver path for clients on 10.20.30.0/24 that had incorrect or stale conditional forwarding/cache data for the internal zone. This caused that resolver to return NXDOMAIN for app-db.internal while other resolver paths continued to return the correct internal record.
resolution_steps: Identify the resolver serving clients on 10.20.30.0/24 — confirmed as dns-res-east-02.corplabs.internal (10.20.30.2) — and compare its response for app-db.internal against a known-good internal resolver (dns-res-core-01.corplabs.internal, 10.50.1.10). NXDOMAIN was returned only by dns-res-east-02.

Review the resolver's conditional forwarder or zone forwarding configuration for the .internal domain on dns-res-east-02.corplabs.internal and correct the forwarding target/path — the forwarder was pointing to a decommissioned upstream server — so requests are sent to the proper authoritative internal DNS servers (dns-auth-01.corplabs.internal / dns-auth-02.corplabs.internal).
Flush the DNS cache on the affected resolver dns-res-east-02.corplabs.internal after the forwarding correction to remove cached NXDOMAIN responses and stale lookup data for app-db.internal.

Re-test name resolution for app-db.internal from the affected subnet (Maria Gonzalez's workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MG at 10.20.30.47) and from a known-good subnet (Raj Patel on 10.40.10.0/24) to confirm both return the same internal answer (A 10.60.5.22).

Document the resolver-specific DNS correction (forwarding target update on dns-res-east-02.corplabs.internal, performed by Kevin Osei) and configure Network Monitoring alerts to detect recurrence of subnet-specific NXDOMAIN responses on the .internal zone, particularly for the Columbus office subnets.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please confirm the DNS resolver IP used by a client on 10.20.30.0/24 (you can check with 'nslookup' or 'ipconfig /all' on your workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MG). Also, can you run 'dig app-db.internal' and let us know whether it returns NXDOMAIN consistently from that subnet? For comparison, I've verified the same lookup succeeds from the management VLAN via resolver 10.50.1.10. — Agent: Darren Whitfield

title: Internal hostname fails to resolve — stale A record in internal DNS
description: Multiple internal users and monitoring agents were trying to reach app.example.internal, but name resolution intermittently returned NXDOMAIN or the outdated IP address 10.20.5.47 from internal DNS. The issue was first reported by Priya Nambiar (emp ID E-40291) from the Austin office, who noticed the internal-app-service dashboard was unreachable by hostname. Additional reports came in from the Portland development team. The application could not connect to its backend by hostname, impacting internal app access across datacenter-1. Investigation focused on the internal BIND 9 zone data on dns-primary-01.dc1.internal and resolver cache behavior after a stale A record remained in the zone for a decommissioned address (10.20.5.47) instead of the current backend at 10.20.8.112.
observed_errors: Application error: unable to resolve host
root_cause: A stale A record for app.example.internal remained in the internal DNS zone and pointed to a decommissioned IP. Resolver and downstream cache entries then served outdated or failed responses, causing intermittent NXDOMAIN and incorrect address resolution.
resolution_steps: Corrected the A record for app.example.internal in the internal DNS zone file /etc/named/zones/db.example.internal so it pointed to the active backend IP 10.20.8.112 instead of the decommissioned address 10.20.5.47.

Incremented the zone serial from 2025121801 to 2026010501 and reloaded named on the primary DNS server dns-primary-01.dc1.internal via `rndc reload example.internal` so the updated zone data was published correctly.

Reloaded or synchronized the change to secondary DNS server dns-secondary-02.dc1.internal to ensure consistent authoritative responses across internal resolvers. Verified zone transfer completed via `rndc zonestatus example.internal`.

Flushed cached DNS entries on the primary and downstream resolvers (dns-primary-01 and dns-secondary-02) using `rndc flush` to remove stale responses for 10.20.5.47 and force retrieval of the updated record.

Validated name resolution from affected client paths including WORKSTATION-L490-PN (pnambiar, 10.30.14.88) and Network Monitoring dashboard checks, confirming that app.example.internal consistently resolved to the correct address 10.20.8.112.

Recommended adjusting the internal DNS TTL policy from 86400s to 3600s for application-tier hostnames to reduce the duration and impact of stale cached records in future changes. Flagged for review by the network team lead Deepak Rao.

title: Internal hostname svc-db.internal fails DNS resolution
description: Internal application teams were trying to reach the database service by the internal hostname svc-db.internal, but several application pods intermittently failed name resolution and could not connect to the DB. root_cause: Intermittent NXDOMAIN responses were caused by a stale A record for svc-db.internal in the internal DNS zone and a deprecated internal DNS management policy reference that allowed outdated zone data to persist on dns-resolver-01 and dependent resolvers.
resolution_steps: Verified that svc-db.internal had an outdated A record (10.20.5.14, last modified 2025-06-12) in the internal DNS zone and confirmed the currently required target IP 10.20.9.42 with database infrastructure owner Priya Nair (pnair) before making changes.

Updated the A record for svc-db.internal in the internal DNS zone to the correct current IP 10.20.9.42 and reviewed the zone entry metadata and TTL (set to 300s from previous 86400s) under change record CHG-88214.

Replaced the deprecated internal-dns-policy-v1 reference with internal-dns-policy-v2 in the zone management configuration to prevent continued publication of stale record state and ensure automatic zone synchronization across all resolvers.

Flushed cache on dns-resolver-01.corp.internal using `rndc flush` and cleared/propagated cache refresh on dependent resolvers dns-resolver-02 and dns-resolver-03 so fresh zone data would be served immediately across the Phoenix datacenter.

Validated successful hostname resolution from affected application hosts (WORKSTATION-LINUX-MD at 10.42.17.88, app-node-03, app-node-07) and confirmed Network Monitoring no longer observed NXDOMAIN responses for svc-db.internal. Marcus Delgado confirmed internal-order-service, payment-processor, and reporting-worker health checks all passing.

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failure for internal service
description: Developers on the platform engineering team (reported by Marcus Delgado, emp ID E-20487) were trying to reach service.internal.corp for internal-service-api and the developer portal from the Austin and Raleigh office locations, but name resolution from internal resolver 10.1.1.10 intermittently returned NXDOMAIN or timed out. Direct queries to the authoritative DNS server dns-auth-01.internal.corp returned the expected A record (10.40.16.55), so users were blocked by inconsistent internal DNS responses rather than a missing service record. Impact was cross-site and intermittent, affecting access to internal endpoints and application connectivity. Initial report came in via Slack from mdelgado@corplabs.com.
root_cause: Resolver 10.1.1.10 had an internal DNS forwarding/cache issue for the internal zone: the authoritative server held the correct A record for service.internal.corp, but the resolver intermittently served NXDOMAIN or timed-out responses until conditional forwarder behavior and cached zone data were corrected.
resolution_steps: Validated that the authoritative DNS server dns-auth-01.internal.corp (10.1.1.30) for the internal zone returned the expected A record for service.internal.corp (10.40.16.55, TTL 300) and confirmed the issue was isolated to recursive resolver 10.1.1.10 behavior rather than a missing zone record. Verification performed by Raj Venkatesh from the Raleigh network monitoring host.

Reviewed and corrected the conditional forwarder path for the internal zone on resolver 10.1.1.10 — removed stale secondary forwarder target 10.1.1.22 (decommissioned) so queries for service.internal.corp consistently routed only to the valid authoritative DNS server dns-auth-01.internal.corp (10.1.1.30).

Cleared stale cached entries and negative cache data (rndc flush) on the affected internal resolver 10.1.1.10 after the forwarder configuration was corrected, ensuring no residual NXDOMAIN responses persisted from the decommissioned target.

Retested repeated lookups for service.internal.corp from the affected resolver and from multiple client locations — including Marcus Delgado's workstation WORKSTATION-MBP-MD (10.22.4.117, Austin) and Priya Nair's machine WORKSTATION-LNX-PN (Raleigh) — to confirm the resolver now returned 10.40.16.55 consistently without NXDOMAIN or timeout responses. 100/100 queries succeeded.

Monitored resolver and DNS query behavior via Network Monitoring dashboards for 2 hours after the change to verify timeout spikes stopped and internal applications (internal-service-api, developer-portal) could consistently resolve the service endpoint. Confirmed with Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) that CI/CD pipeline and portal access were fully restored.

Retested name resolution from monitoring host mon-agent-04 and multiple internal clients including WORKSTATION-MDLG-PC (mdelgado) and Raj Okonkwo's session (rokonkwo) to confirm api.service.corp.local consistently resolved to the updated IP address 10.42.17.20.

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failures for internal services
description: Users in the Chicago office were trying to reach internal services by the hostname svc.internal.corp, but DNS resolution intermittently returned different A records after a same-day zone edit performed by network engineer David Kowalski (emp ID NE-40821). Some clients resolved the new address 10.10.5.21 and connected successfully, while others received the previous IP 10.10.4.9 and application requests to internal endpoints failed by name. observed_errors: NXDOMAIN not observed but inconsistent A record responses
Resolver returned stale A record 10.10.4.9 for svc.internal.corp after zone update
root_cause: A stale cached A record for svc.internal.corp remained on internal DNS resolver/forwarding paths after the authoritative internal zone was updated to 10.10.5.21, causing different clients to receive either the old address 10.10.4.9 or the new address depending on which resolver cache answered the query.
resolution_steps: Validated that the authoritative internal DNS zone on dns-auth-01.corplabs.internal for svc.internal.corp contained the intended A record value of 10.10.5.21 and confirmed the earlier zone change by David Kowalski (dkowalski) at 13:45 UTC had been applied correctly.

Flushed DNS cache entries on the internal resolver path using rndc flush on dns-res-02.corplabs.internal and dns-res-03.corplabs.internal — the primary and secondary resolver nodes involved in serving or forwarding the internal.corp zone to the Chicago subnets — to remove the stale 10.10.4.9 response.

Reviewed and verified conditional forwarder configuration on dns-res-02 and dns-res-03 for the internal.corp zone so queries were routed consistently to dns-auth-01.corplabs.internal as the correct authoritative source rather than returning mixed cached results.

Re-ran DNS lookups from multiple resolver paths and client subnets (10.22.14.0/24, 10.22.15.0/24) to confirm svc.internal.corp now resolved consistently to 10.10.5.21. Verified with affected users Maria Chen (mchen) and Jorge Ramirez (jramirez) that application connectivity was restored.

Documented TTL and change-propagation guidance for future internal zone edits — including a recommended post-change cache-flush checklist for all resolver nodes — so stale cached responses can be minimized and validated immediately after record changes. Shared documentation with the network team lead, Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com), for inclusion in the DNS runbook.

title: Intermittent internal hostname lookup failing
description: Multiple users and monitoring in corp-dc-1 reported intermittent failures resolving service.corp.internal for internal-portal and service.backend. The issue was initially flagged by Rajesh Patel (emp ID EMP-40291) from the Engineering team at the Denver office, who noticed that the hostname sometimes returned NXDOMAIN, sometimes an old decommissioned IP (10.20.5.47), and sometimes timed out. This prevented the applications from reaching the internal service endpoint by name from affected subnets. Additional reports came in from Maria Chen on the same floor.
root_cause: An internal DNS resolver retained and served a stale cached A record for service.corp.internal that pointed to a decommissioned IP, while some lookups also returned NXDOMAIN during inconsistent cache state, causing intermittent internal name resolution failures.
resolution_steps: Verified the authoritative internal DNS zone for service.corp.internal and corrected the A record to the current production IP 10.20.8.130, replacing the decommissioned entry 10.20.5.47.

Flushed cache on all internal DNS resolvers (dns-res-01, dns-res-02) serving the affected Denver clients and restarted the resolver service on dns-res-02 where cache purge did not fully clear stale entries.

Confirmed conditional forwarding and resolver path behavior for the corp.internal zone so subsequent queries were answered from the correct authoritative source; verified from WORKSTATION-LP-RPATEL and WORKSTATION-DT-MCHEN.

Validated fresh DNS responses for service.corp.internal from multiple subnets including 10.20.3.0/24 and 10.20.4.0/24, and compared results against authoritative lookups to confirm the stale (10.20.5.47) and NXDOMAIN responses were eliminated. title: Intermittent internal hostname resolution failures for db.internal.example.com
description: Internal services were trying to resolve and connect to db.internal.example.com, but multiple hosts across at least two racks (Rack 14A and Rack 14B) in the Arlington datacenter began intermittently failing name resolution around 08:30 on 2026-01-07. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (emp ID E-40821) from the platform engineering team after deployment pipelines on WORKSTATION-MDELGADO started failing database connectivity checks. Affected clients reported a mix of NXDOMAIN responses and DNS lookup timeouts, and some resolver checks returned an older A record pointing to 10.22.4.17 instead of the expected 10.22.6.50. The issue impacted name-based access to the internal database endpoint across multiple subnets (10.22.4.0/24 and 10.22.6.0/24) in the on-premises us-east-1 datacenter. Additional reports came in from Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) on the observability team, confirming the same symptoms from hosts in Rack 14B.
root_cause: Intermittent internal DNS resolution was caused by stale or inconsistent resolver data for db.internal.example.com, likely due to an incorrect or outdated internal zone record and/or resolver forwarder/cache state serving old answers across subnets.
resolution_steps: Verify the authoritative internal DNS zone entry for db.internal.example.com, confirm the correct A record value (10.22.6.50) and TTL (300s), and correct the record where it differs from the intended database endpoint address. The stale record pointing to 10.22.4.17 was updated by jlin on the primary zone server.

Clear cache on the affected internal DNS resolvers (dns-resolver-1.internal.example.com and dns-resolver-2.internal.example.com) so stale responses and negative cache entries for db.internal.example.com are removed and new queries return fresh zone data reflecting the corrected 10.22.6.50 address.

Flush DNS cache on representative affected clients — including WORKSTATION-MDELGADO (10.22.4.103) and WORKSTATION-PNAIR (10.22.6.88) — and retest name resolution from multiple subnets (10.22.4.0/24 and 10.22.6.0/24) to confirm the hostname consistently resolves to the current address 10.22.6.50 without NXDOMAIN or timeout behavior.

Review and correct any conditional forwarder or delegation path used for the internal.example.com zone on dns-resolver-1.internal.example.com so queries are routed to the proper authoritative source. The stale conditional forwarder entry was updated and validated by the network team.

Validate steady-state resolution by repeating lookups from impacted racks (Rack 14A and Rack 14B in Arlington) and monitoring via Network Monitoring dashboards for consistent answers (10.22.6.50) and elimination of intermittent lookup failures. Marcus Delgado and Priya Nair confirmed resolution from their respective hosts.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm whether all affected hosts use the same internal DNS resolver path (e.g., are they all pointed at dns-resolver-1.internal.example.com and dns-resolver-2.internal.example.com?) and whether failed lookups return NXDOMAIN, timeout, or an unexpected IP when querying db.internal.example.com. title: Internal hostname svc-db.corp.internal intermittently fails to resolve

The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, Emp ID E-40291) from the Richmond data center operations team. Users observed nslookup returning either NXDOMAIN or the outdated IP address 10.22.4.87 (the decommissioned database host), and dependent applications in the backend-app-cluster lost connectivity to the svc-db service by name. observed_errors: NXDOMAIN for svc-db.corp.internal observed from resolver
resolver returned outdated A record (old IP) on tests
root_cause: The internal DNS zone contained a stale A record for svc-db.corp.internal that still referenced a decommissioned IP address, and internal DNS resolver cache retained outdated data, causing intermittent NXDOMAIN and stale address responses.
resolution_steps: Updated the A record for svc-db.corp.internal in the internal DNS zone on dns-int-east-01.corp.internal from the decommissioned address 10.22.4.87 to the current database service IP 10.22.9.140, and confirmed the decommissioned address was removed. Reviewed the zone entry TTL (adjusted from 3600s to 300s temporarily) and recent record state to ensure the corrected record would propagate as expected across internal resolvers including dns-resolver-east-02.corp.internal.
Flushed cached DNS entries on the affected internal resolver infrastructure (dns-resolver-east-02.corp.internal) so stale NXDOMAIN and outdated A record responses pointing to 10.22.4.87 were cleared.

Retested name resolution for svc-db.corp.internal from multiple affected application servers including WORKSTATION-BKND-MD (mdelgado) and WORKSTATION-BKND-RL (rlewis) and confirmed consistent return of the current IP 10.22.9.140.

Validated that backend applications could reconnect to the database service using the hostname and monitored Network Monitoring alerts for recurrence after the change. Marcus Delgado confirmed batch jobs resumed successfully at 09:15 UTC.

title: Internal host failing to resolve
description: Engineering users in the Arlington office were trying to reach internal-app.company.local on the internal network, but between 09:12 and 09:40 EST the hostname intermittently failed to resolve and client systems received NXDOMAIN responses. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, EMP-40821) via the #dns-ops Slack channel and affected access to the internal application by name through the BIND 9 cache cluster (cache-east-01.infra.company.local / cache-east-02.infra.company.local) in the us-east-1 primary datacenter. Investigation tied the failures to an outdated internal DNS A record pointing to the decommissioned IP 10.22.4.17 instead of the current 10.22.8.55, and delayed remediation because the runbook referenced a deprecated DNS change-control policy (POL-DNS-2019, superseded by POL-DNS-2025).
platform: internal network DNS infrastructure (BIND 9 cache cluster)
observed_errors: Resolver returned NXDOMAIN from caching resolver (cache-hit)
root_cause: An outdated A record for internal-app.company.local remained in the authoritative internal DNS zone, and a deprecated change-control policy reference in the runbook slowed validation and correction of the DNS change.
resolution_steps: Correct the authoritative A record for internal-app.company.local in the internal DNS zone on ns-auth-01.infra.company.local from the stale address 10.22.4.17 to the current service IP address 10.22.8.55 (change performed by Priya Nair, pnair).

Increment the zone serial from 2025120901 to 2026010701 and reload the updated zone on the authoritative DNS server ns-auth-01.infra.company.local via `rndc reload company.local` so secondaries (ns-auth-02.infra.company.local) can receive the change via AXFR.

Confirm the corrected record has propagated to secondary DNS servers serving the internal zone by querying ns-auth-02.infra.company.local and verifying the serial matches 2026010701 and the A record returns 10.22.8.55.

Flush cached DNS entries on the primary and secondary resolvers (cache-east-01.infra.company.local and cache-east-02.infra.company.local) using `rndc flush` and restart the named caching service on the primary resolver cache-east-01 to clear stale NXDOMAIN responses.

Validate successful resolution for internal-app.company.local from Network Monitoring probes and from affected client subnets (10.22.50.0/24, 10.22.51.0/24, 10.22.52.0/24), confirming the hostname now returns the expected address 10.22.8.55. Confirmed with mdelgado and jtorres that their workstations resolve correctly.

Update the DNS runbook to replace the deprecated policy reference POL-DNS-2019 with the current POL-DNS-2025 so future DNS record corrections follow the current change process without delay. Runbook update assigned to Priya Nair (pnair) with review by team lead David Chen (dchen).
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — can you confirm the exact hostname and the failure window so we can correlate NXDOMAIN responses with resolver logs on cache-east-01.infra.company.local and cache-east-02.infra.company.local and cross-reference the internal zone data on ns-auth-01.infra.company.local? Also, could you share the client IP or hostname where you first saw the failure? — Priya Nair, Network Engineering

title: Internal-service DNS resolution failures
description: Multiple internal application teams reported to engineer Priya Nair that they were unable to reach the inventory-sync service using the hostname internal-service.corp.local. Name resolution intermittently failed for approximately 2 hours starting around 18:10 UTC. Internal DNS resolvers (dns-resolver-east-01.corp.local and dns-resolver-east-02.corp.local) returned NXDOMAIN or timeouts from subnets in the Arlington data center, while direct access by IP (10.40.12.55) still worked, confirming the service itself was reachable and the outage was limited to internal DNS resolution. Affected teams included the order-processing group led by Marcus Okonkwo (emp ID E-90214) and the logistics integration team. Impact was loss of application connectivity by name until DNS zone updates and resolver caches were corrected.
observed_errors: lookup timed out from some subnets
root_cause: Stale cached DNS data on internal BIND9 resolver instances after a recent internal zone update caused inconsistent responses for internal-service.corp.local. The authoritative zone record and propagation state were not fully aligned across resolver/cache layers until the zone serial was incremented, the zone reloaded, and resolver caches flushed.
resolution_steps: Verified the correct A record value for internal-service.corp.local on the primary internal DNS zone (dns-auth-east-01.corp.local) and confirmed the record had been updated to the intended IP address 10.40.12.55 by Carlos Medina, replacing the decommissioned 10.40.12.40.

Incremented the DNS zone serial from 2026010701 to 2026010702 and reloaded the zone on the primary authoritative server dns-auth-east-01.corp.local using rndc reload so the change could propagate correctly to downstream resolvers.

Confirmed the zone reload and AXFR transfer/update state to secondary authoritative DNS servers (dns-auth-east-02.corp.local) handling the corp.local internal zone. Serial 2026010702 was reflected on all secondaries.

Flushed stale cache entries on internal BIND9 resolver instances dns-resolver-east-01.corp.local and dns-resolver-east-02.corp.local using rndc flush so resolvers would stop serving the outdated 10.40.12.40 result.

Validated fresh resolution with dig from multiple subnets (Arlington, Reston, Ashburn) including from Priya Nair's workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-PN and Marcus Okonkwo's host WORKSTATION-DESK-MO, and confirmed the hostname returned the expected address 10.40.12.55 consistently.

Confirmed Network Monitoring alerts for internal-service.corp.local cleared after cache flush and zone propagation completed at 20:41 UTC, indicating full service restoration. Priya Nair notified affected application teams including Marcus Okonkwo's order-processing group.

title: Intermittent internal DNS resolution failures for app.payments.corp
description: Internal applications were trying to resolve the backend hostname app.payments.corp, but lookups intermittently returned NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, or timed out against internal DNS after the prior night's DNS maintenance. The issue was reported by engineer Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com, EMP-40821) and observed from multiple clients and regions including the Chicago and Austin offices, preventing the payments service from reliably reaching its internal dependency by name and causing intermittent application failures across the corp-net environment.
root_cause: DNS maintenance left inconsistent internal resolver state for the app.payments.corp zone path, with stale or incorrect cached data and/or forwarder handling causing intermittent negative responses and timeouts despite the zone record needing to resolve internally. The incident behavior across multiple hosts and regions points to resolver-side cache/forwarder inconsistency rather than a single client issue.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the internal zone record and recent maintenance changes for app.payments.corp to confirm the expected target value (10.30.5.120) and TTL (300s) after the DNS work performed during change CHG-90412 by mreeves on 2026-01-07.

Validated resolution from affected clients (WORKSTATION-PN-7241 at 10.44.12.87 for pnair in Chicago, WORKSTATION-DLEE-3390 at 10.44.18.22 for dlee in Austin) against the internal resolver and compared results with the authoritative or known-good internal DNS path to confirm inconsistent resolver behavior.

Cleared positive and negative caches on the impacted internal caching resolvers (DNS-CACHE-01.corplabs.internal and DNS-CACHE-03.corplabs.internal) and verified conditional forwarder or zone routing configuration for the payments.corp namespace, ensuring the forwarder pointed to DNS-AUTH-02.corplabs.internal.

Corrected the resolver-side DNS path so app.payments.corp returned the current internal record (10.30.5.120) consistently, then restarted or refreshed the caching service where required on DNS-CACHE-01 and DNS-CACHE-03.

Had affected clients (pnair on WORKSTATION-PN-7241, dlee on WORKSTATION-DLEE-3390) flush local DNS cache and retest name resolution, confirming the hostname resolved consistently without NXDOMAIN or timeout responses.

Monitored resolver metrics and incident symptoms via Network Monitoring after the change window to verify the spikes in NXDOMAIN and timeouts did not recur, with mreeves confirming stable resolution across Chicago and Austin regions for 4 hours post-fix.
agent_questions: Hi Priya — please confirm whether app.payments.corp fails only through the standard internal resolver (DNS-CACHE-01.corplabs.internal, 10.20.1.53) or also when tested against another known-good internal DNS path such as DNS-AUTH-02.corplabs.internal, and whether the issue started immediately after last night's DNS maintenance. Also, can you let us know which client hostnames or IPs you tested from?

title: Internal hostname resolution failing via internal DNS resolver
description: Internal services were trying to resolve service-internal.company.local through the primary internal DNS resolver at 10.10.0.5 (DNS-RESV-01.infra.company.local) in the Newark datacenter, but the resolver intermittently returned NXDOMAIN while direct queries to the authoritative internal DNS server at 10.10.0.12 (DNS-AUTH-01.infra.company.local) returned the correct A record (10.20.5.44). This was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, employee ID E-40821) from the platform engineering team after the internal-api-gateway on host APPGW-PROD-02 began logging connection failures to service-internal.company.local. The issue prevented internal APIs that rely on name-based routing from reaching the internal endpoint by hostname and caused inconsistent application connectivity across the on-premises environment, affecting multiple downstream consumers.
observed_errors: NXDOMAIN (negative response) returned by internal resolver
inconsistent resolution between resolver and authoritative server
root_cause: One internal DNS resolver was missing the required conditional forwarder for the internal zone, causing some queries for service-internal.company.local to be routed incorrectly. The resolver then cached the negative response, so it continued serving stale NXDOMAIN answers even though the authoritative internal DNS server had the correct A record.
resolution_steps: Added the missing conditional forwarder for the internal company.local zone on the affected resolver DNS-RESV-01 at 10.10.0.5, pointing to the authoritative server DNS-AUTH-01 at 10.10.0.12, so requests are consistently sent to the correct authoritative internal DNS path. Change performed by Priya Nair (pnair).

Flushed the DNS-RESV-01 resolver DNS cache via dnscmd /clearcache to remove the stale negative NXDOMAIN entry for service-internal.company.local and force fresh lookup results for the affected hostname.

Retested resolution for service-internal.company.local against both the affected resolver DNS-RESV-01 (10.10.0.5) and the authoritative internal DNS server DNS-AUTH-01 (10.10.0.12) to confirm the resolver now returns the expected A record 10.20.5.44. Verified from WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.40.12.88) and APPGW-PROD-02.

Validated that dependent internal API traffic on internal-api-gateway (APPGW-PROD-02) using name-based routing could resolve and reach service-internal.company.local normally after the DNS change. Marcus Delgado confirmed application connectivity was restored.

Updated DNS monitoring in Network Monitoring and operational guidance to alert on NXDOMAIN spikes for internal zones (company.local) and to verify conditional forwarder consistency across all resolvers (DNS-RESV-01, DNS-RESV-02). Added a quarterly forwarder audit task assigned to the network infrastructure team.

title: Intermittent internal hostname resolving to old IP
description: Users and monitoring reported that app.example.corp intermittently failed to resolve after an internal DNS A record change performed on 2026-01-07 by the infrastructure team. Multiple developers in the Portland office, including Marcus Delgado (mdelgado), reported that some clients and recursive resolvers returned the previous IP 10.0.1.23, while others returned the new IP 10.0.2.45 or intermittently saw NXDOMAIN/timeouts. Affected workstations included WORKSTATION-MACBOOK-MD and others on the 10.12.0.0/16 subnet. This prevented internal services and developers from reliably reaching the application endpoint by hostname after the DNS update, impacting CI/CD pipelines and local development environments.
root_cause: Stale cached DNS data remained on specific recursive resolvers and at least one resolver was not honoring TTL/refresh behavior correctly after the internal A record was updated, causing mixed answers including the previous IP and intermittent NXDOMAIN during propagation.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the authoritative internal DNS zone on dns-auth-west-01.corplabs.internal for app.example.corp contained the intended A record value 10.0.2.45 (SOA serial 2026010802) and reviewed the recent record change committed at 12:55 UTC and TTL settings (300s).

Flushed cache entries via rndc flush on primary and secondary internal recursive resolvers (dns-rec-west-02.corplabs.internal and dns-rec-west-03.corplabs.internal) serving the affected clients in the Portland and Seattle offices to remove stale answers for app.example.corp.

Restarted the resolver service (named) on dns-rec-west-03.corplabs.internal where cached responses persisted despite the flush, addressing the resolver instance that was not honoring TTL refresh behavior correctly. Tanya Reeves (treeves) confirmed the service came back clean with no residual cache entries.

Verified resolver and forwarder behavior by querying the hostname from affected resolvers and known-good resolvers, including tests from Marcus Delgado's workstation (10.12.4.87) and Priya Nair's machine (10.12.4.92), until responses consistently returned 10.0.2.45 across all paths.

Validated end-to-end propagation with dig +trace and Network Monitoring probes across Portland and Seattle segments, then continued short-term monitoring (24-hour window) for residual stale responses from downstream or external recursive caches until they aged out. No further anomalies detected as of 2026-01-09T14:00 UTC.

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failure for internal-service.corp (near-duplicate)
description: Multiple internal services on the corporate network intermittently failed to resolve internal-service.corp starting around 2026-01-08 09:40 UTC. Affected applications, including internal-service and service-gateway, were blocked from reaching the internal endpoint by hostname. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the Arlington office, who noticed service-gateway connections timing out. Some clients received NXDOMAIN while others resolved the hostname to a stale IP address (192.0.2.50), creating inconsistent connectivity across recursive resolvers and client caches in us-east-1. Workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD was among the first endpoints observed exhibiting the failure.
observed_errors: stale DNS record present in resolver cache
root_cause: Stale and inconsistent DNS cache entries on recursive resolvers caused internal-service.corp to return NXDOMAIN or an outdated A record (192.0.2.50) instead of the authoritative value (192.0.2.75).
resolution_steps: Validated that the authoritative Internal DNS Zone on ns-auth.corplabs.internal for internal-service.corp was correct and publishing A record 192.0.2.75 (SOA serial 2026010802, updated 2026-01-07 22:15 UTC).

Compared responses from affected recursive resolvers ns-rec-01.corplabs.internal and ns-rec-02.corplabs.internal against the authoritative zone and confirmed cache divergence, including stale A record 192.0.2.50 and intermittent NXDOMAIN responses affecting clients such as 10.22.9.34 (mdelgado) and 10.22.14.88 (kcho).

Flushed DNS cache on the primary resolver ns-rec-01.corplabs.internal and affected recursive nodes ns-rec-02 and ns-rec-03 to remove stale and negative cached entries for internal-service.corp. Flush performed by Ramon Estrada (restrada, EMP-55190).

Cleared client-side DNS cache on impacted application nodes including WORKSTATION-PC-MD (Marcus Delgado, 10.22.9.34) and WORKSTATION-LT-KC (Kevin Cho, 10.22.14.88) and re-ran lookups to confirm consistent resolution to 192.0.2.75.

Temporarily reduced the record TTL from 3600s to 300s to accelerate propagation of the corrected answer and monitored resolver responses via Network Monitoring for 30 minutes to confirm stability after cache refresh. TTL will be restored to 3600s after 24-hour observation window.

title: Intermittent internal DNS resolution failures for internal services
description: Internal services intermittently fail to resolve internal hostnames needed by the HR Portal (hrportal.corp.eastnet.local), Payroll API (payroll-api.corp.eastnet.local), and Internal Inventory Service (inventory.corp.eastnet.local) in the on-premises us-east-1 environment at the Newark data center. Application calls sometimes return NXDOMAIN, time out, or resolve to an older IP (10.40.2.17 instead of the current 10.40.5.33) depending on resolver location and timing. The inconsistent behavior is preventing internal-services users and application nodes from reliably reaching internal endpoints by name. Reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, EMP-40821) from the Infrastructure Operations team. The reporter did not provide a complete hostname list or precise failure timestamps, which limited scope validation.
observed_errors: stale address observed in resolver cache
root_cause: Intermittent resolution was most consistent with inconsistent internal DNS pathing: one or more resolvers had stale cached records while conditional forwarding or zone delegation for the affected internal zone was not consistently returning authoritative answers. This caused different resolvers to return NXDOMAIN, timeouts, or outdated addresses for the same hostname until cache and forwarder configuration were corrected.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the affected internal DNS zone records on DNS-AUTH-EAST-01 for the corp.eastnet.local zone, validated current A records (hrportal → 10.40.5.33, payroll-api → 10.40.5.41, inventory → 10.40.5.52) and TTL values (300s), and corrected stale record data where resolver responses did not match the authoritative zone.

Verified conditional forwarder and zone routing configuration between internal resolvers DNS-RES-EAST-01 / DNS-RES-EAST-02 and the authoritative DNS server DNS-AUTH-EAST-01, then added the missing forwarder path on DNS-RES-EAST-02 for the corp.eastnet.local namespace.
Flushed DNS cache on impacted internal resolvers DNS-RES-EAST-01 and DNS-RES-EAST-02 (dnscmd /clearcache) and repeated lookups to remove stale answers (10.40.2.17) previously being served from cache.

Retested name resolution from multiple resolver paths and client locations — including WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.40.12.88, mdelgado), APPNODE-EAST-04, and APPNODE-EAST-07 — using repeated nslookup/dig queries to confirm the same current address was returned consistently for all three affected service hostnames.

Enabled follow-up monitoring via Network Monitoring for internal name resolution on the corp.eastnet.local zone so future NXDOMAIN, timeout, or stale-answer patterns can be correlated with affected hostnames and timing if the issue recurs. Notified Marcus Delgado (mdelgado), Janelle Torres (jtorres), and Raj Mehta (rmehta) of the resolution.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please provide any affected internal hostnames (e.g., hrportal.corp.eastnet.local, payroll-api.corp.eastnet.local), approximate failure times, and whether the NXDOMAIN or timeout behavior changes by site or application server so we can compare resolver paths. Also, can you confirm which client machines or app servers you've tested from? If you have nslookup or dig output from WORKSTATION-PC-MD or any of the app nodes, please attach those as well. — Priya Nair, Network Engineering

title: Internal hostname svc-inventory.corp fails to resolve
description: Users and dependent internal applications at the Charlotte office were trying to reach the Inventory Service by the internal hostname svc-inventory.corp, but DNS lookups intermittently returned NXDOMAIN from multiple subnets while direct connections to the service IP (10.42.16.55) still worked. The issue was first reported by Marcus Ellison (mellison, EMP-40821) and affected internal name resolution for the service, causing application connectivity failures until the stale DNS record was corrected and caches were cleared.
root_cause: A stale A record for svc-inventory.corp remained cached on the primary resolver and was associated with a decommissioned host, and the long TTL allowed the incorrect data to persist and be served during internal DNS lookups.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the internal DNS zone corp.internal for svc-inventory.corp and corrected the A record so it pointed to the current service IP 10.42.16.55 instead of the decommissioned host reference 10.42.16.12.
Reduced the TTL on the affected DNS record from 86400 seconds to 300 seconds to shorten persistence of incorrect cached data during propagation of the corrected entry.
Flushed DNS cache entries on the primary resolver DNS-PRI-EAST.corp.internal and secondary resolver DNS-SEC-EAST.corp.internal to remove the stale record immediately.

Validated name resolution for svc-inventory.corp from multiple client subnets (10.42.16.0/24 and 10.42.20.0/24) and confirmed the hostname consistently returned the expected address 10.42.16.55. Reporter mellison and application owner rtorres both confirmed service restoration.

Updated DNS monitoring logic in Network Monitoring and operational guidance for the Charlotte network team to better detect stale-record and elevated NXDOMAIN patterns for internal service names, including automated alerting thresholds for NXDOMAIN spikes.

title: Internal hostnames intermittently failing to resolve from DNS resolver
description: Internal users and monitoring in the Charlotte office intermittently failed to reach services by name under corp.local because the internal resolver bind-resolver-01 (10.20.5.12) returned NXDOMAIN or a stale A record for service1.corp.local. The issue was initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, EMP-40291) from the internal-ops team after the deployment dashboard on his workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD could not connect to service1.corp.local. The authoritative internal DNS zone on ns-auth-01.corp.local already contained the correct current address (10.50.12.88), so applications depending on internal hostname resolution were intermittently unable to connect until resolver cache and configuration state were corrected.
observed_errors: cached old A record returned by resolver
root_cause: bind-resolver-01 was serving stale cached DNS data for corp.local due to an outdated DNS update policy reference and cache entries that were not invalidated after the authoritative record changed, causing intermittent NXDOMAIN and old A record responses despite the authoritative zone being correct.
resolution_steps: Verified the authoritative corp.local zone on ns-auth-01.corp.local contained the correct A record (10.50.12.88) for service1.corp.local and corrected the record where needed so the source of truth matched the intended service IP.

Reviewed the resolver configuration on bind-resolver-01 (10.20.5.12) and updated the outdated DNS update policy reference in /etc/bind/named.conf.options contributing to stale response behavior, as identified by Priya Nair.
Flushed the DNS cache on bind-resolver-01 via rndc flush and restarted the named service to remove stale NXDOMAIN and old A record entries (10.50.12.60) for service1.corp.local.

Queried service1.corp.local from the resolver and from affected internal hosts — including WORKSTATION-PC-MD (mdelgado, 10.20.41.77) and trivera's workstation (10.20.41.93) — to confirm the resolver now returned the same current address 10.50.12.88 as the authoritative zone.

Confirmed dependent service checks and Network Monitoring alerts cleared after cache refresh and configuration correction, with hostname resolution for service1.corp.local remaining stable across all queried clients in the Charlotte office.
agent_questions: We are comparing answers from bind-resolver-01 (10.20.5.12) against the authoritative corp.local zone on ns-auth-01.corp.local to confirm whether the issue is with the source record or stale resolver data for service1.corp.local. Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) reported that his workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD at 10.20.41.77 was receiving NXDOMAIN responses when querying the hostname. Network engineer Priya Nair is leading the investigation.

title: Intermittent DNS resolution for internal-app.example.corp returns NXDOMAIN or stale IP
description: Multiple internal users in the Charlotte office were trying to reach internal-app.example.corp, but DNS lookups intermittently returned NXDOMAIN or the previous A record value 10.0.2.5 after a recent DNS record change performed by network engineer David Kowalski (EMP-40291). The inconsistent name resolution prevented the application from reliably reaching its internal endpoint by name and caused partial outage symptoms across users depending on which resolver answered the query. Initial reports came from Rachel Nguyen (rnguyen) and Kevin Park (kpark) on the finance team.
observed_errors: stale address 10.0.2.5 returned by some resolvers
root_cause: After the A record change for internal-app.example.corp, some DNS resolvers and forwarders continued serving cached stale data, and some queries returned NXDOMAIN during inconsistent propagation because not all downstream caches had refreshed from the updated internal zone.

title: Internal hostname intermittently fails DNS resolution for internal-portal.company.local

Validated that authoritative name servers (dns-auth-01.corp.local, dns-auth-02.corp.local) and multiple site resolvers now returned the same updated IP 10.22.8.40, and confirmed via the Monitoring Dashboard that DNS error rates for internal-portal.company.local returned to baseline. agent_questions: Hi Marcus — can you confirm whether the Internal Portal service IP changed recently (we show a migration was scheduled for internal-portal.company.local last weekend) and whether users in both the Chicago and Atlanta offices are seeing NXDOMAIN or an old address (10.22.4.17)? title: Intermittent DNS resolution failure for internal-service.local

Flushed DNS cache on the primary resolver dc-resolver1 and on caching forwarders fw-resolver1 and fw-resolver2 to remove stale responses for internal-service.local. Executed by Kevin Briggs (kbriggs, Network Operations).

Adjusted internal zone refresh interval from 3600 to 900 seconds and reduced default TTL policy to 300 seconds to reduce the likelihood and duration of stale-cache behavior after future service IP changes.

Verified successful name resolution from multiple client subnets (10.20.0.0/16, 10.21.0.0/16), including workstations WORKSTATION-MC2041 (Maria Castillo) and WORKSTATION-RP3087 (Raj Patel), confirming consistent responses to the current address 10.10.7.18 with no further NXDOMAIN results.

Monitored DNS lookup alerts via Network Monitoring and client resolution behavior for 2 hours after the change (until 2026-01-10T09:15:00Z) and observed stable resolution with no recurrence. Confirmed with Maria Castillo (mcastillo@corplabs.com) that the issue was fully resolved.

title: Intermittent DNS resolution for internal-service.example.com
description: Users and monitoring systems across multiple offices were trying to resolve internal-service.example.com for access to the internal-service endpoint, but DNS responses were intermittent across locations. Reports originated from users in the Charlotte and Raleigh offices, as well as automated health checks from the Network Monitoring platform. Some client lookups (e.g., from workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MREEVES, IP 10.50.12.88) and resolver checks returned the current internal A record 10.2.3.50, while other resolvers—particularly those serving the Raleigh site—continued to return the old IP 10.1.2.45 or timed out, causing applications to intermittently fail to reach the service by hostname after a recent DNS record update. Ticket raised by Marcus Reeves (mreeves, EMP-40821) on behalf of the internal-users group.
observed_errors: nslookup returned old IP 10.1.2.45 from some resolvers
timeout resolving internal-service.example.com from select locations
NXDOMAIN not observed; inconsistent A record responses
root_cause: Stale cached A record data on downstream/internal resolvers and conditional forwarding path inconsistency caused some clients to receive the previous address 10.1.2.45 after the authoritative zone had already been updated to 10.2.3.50.
resolution_steps: Validated that the authoritative internal DNS zone on ns1-internal.corplabs.net for internal-service.example.com contained the intended A record value 10.2.3.50 and confirmed the change (originally made by admin jmartinez at 2026-01-10T10:30:00Z) was present on authoritative servers with correct SOA serial.

Flushed caches on primary internal DNS resolvers dns-resolver-east-01 and dns-resolver-east-02 using rndc flush and reloaded DNS services to remove stale entries serving the previous address 10.1.2.45. Verified immediate improvement for clients in the Raleigh office.

Coordinated cache clears on downstream resolvers dns-resolver-east-04 and dns-resolver-south-01 involved in conditional forwarding, with assistance from network engineer David Cho (dcho, EMP-40955), so clients in Charlotte and other affected sites no longer received mixed responses from different resolution paths.

Temporarily reduced the DNS TTL for the affected record from 3600s to 300s to shorten cache persistence during propagation and future address changes. Change documented in the Internal DNS Zone change log.

Reviewed and corrected conditional forwarder behavior on dns-resolver-east-04 for the internal zone (ensured direct forwarding to ns1-internal.corplabs.net rather than through intermediate resolver dns-resolver-south-01), then verified from multiple locations—Charlotte (Marcus Reeves, WORKSTATION-PC-MREEVES), Raleigh (Priya Nair, WORKSTATION-LT-PNAIR), and us-east-1 monitoring probes—that resolvers consistently returned 10.2.3.50 without timeouts or old-address responses.

title: Intermittent internal hostname resolution failure for AppTeam
description: AppTeam engineer Priya Nair (emp ID: E-40291) reported that two application hosts (APPNODE-PRD-01 and APPNODE-PRD-02) in the corp-datacenter-1 on-prem environment at the Phoenix facility were unable to reliably reach the internal API endpoint api.internal.corp. root_cause: Internal DNS resolution for api.internal.corp was impacted by stale or incorrect resolver-side handling of the zone, most likely a missing or incorrect conditional forwarder and/or cached negative response on the corporate resolver path. The symptom pattern of intermittent NXDOMAIN from the internal resolver while another resolver returned A records is consistent with resolver configuration or cache state rather than an application issue.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the internal DNS zone on authoritative nameserver ns1.internal.corp (10.12.4.20) and confirmed the expected A record for api.internal.corp (10.20.50.12) and its TTL of 300 seconds were present and current.

Corrected the resolver path for the internal.corp zone by adding the missing conditional forwarder configuration on the corporate DNS resolver 10.12.4.10, pointing internal.corp queries to the authoritative nameserver ns1.internal.corp (10.12.4.20) to handle affected app-server queries.

Cleared stale DNS cache entries, including any negative cached NXDOMAIN responses for api.internal.corp, on the affected internal resolver 10.12.4.10 using `rndc flush` and instructed cache flush (`systemd-resolve --flush-caches`) on the impacted application hosts APPNODE-PRD-01 and APPNODE-PRD-02.

Re-ran name resolution tests from the affected hosts APPNODE-PRD-01 (10.20.31.44) and APPNODE-PRD-02 (10.20.31.45) against the corporate resolver 10.12.4.10 and confirmed api.internal.corp returned the expected A record (10.20.50.12) instead of NXDOMAIN.

Validated repeat queries after cache refresh from both application hosts and user workstation WORKSTATION-PNAIR to confirm resolution consistency across the Phoenix datacenter environment, and closed the incident after intermittent lookup failures were no longer reproducible over a 30-minute monitoring window.
agent_questions: Hi Priya — please run `dig @10.12.4.10 api.internal.corp A` from both APPNODE-PRD-01 (10.20.31.44) and APPNODE-PRD-02 (10.20.31.45), attach /etc/resolv.conf from both affected hosts, and confirm whether the NXDOMAIN response is coming only from the internal resolver path. Also, can you verify whether your teammate Raj Menon on the AppTeam cluster sees the same behavior from his workstation WORKSTATION-RM-PC? Please send results to dns-ops@corplabs.com so we can correlate. — Kevin Albrecht, Network Operations

title: Internal hostname service.example.local intermittent DNS failures — resolved
description: Users and the internal application team were trying to reach the internal service at service.example.local from application instances in the Newark data center, but beginning around 08:30 UTC on 2026-01-10 name-based access became intermittent. Some clients received NXDOMAIN responses while others resolved an outdated A record (10.42.8.17 instead of the current 10.42.12.55), even though direct connectivity to the service IP 10.42.12.55 still worked. observed_errors: dig +short service.example.local returned stale A record (old IP)
application DNS lookup timeout and name resolution failure
root_cause: A delayed update in the internal DNS zone left ResolverA serving a stale cached A record with an elevated TTL, causing intermittent responses of either an outdated IP or NXDOMAIN for service.example.local until the cache and zone data were corrected.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the internal DNS zone entry for service.example.local on DNS-ZONE-EAST.corplabs.internal and identified that the published record state (10.42.8.17, TTL 7200s) did not match the address expected by affected application clients (10.42.12.55).

Updated the A record in the internal DNS zone on DNS-ZONE-EAST.corplabs.internal to the correct current IP address 10.42.12.55 and reduced the record TTL from 7200 seconds to 300 seconds to limit stale cache persistence.
Flushed the cached entry on DNS-RES-01.corplabs.internal (ResolverA) via rndc flush so the resolver would stop serving the outdated response (10.42.8.17) immediately.

Verified that resolver cluster members (DNS-RES-01.corplabs.internal and DNS-RES-02.corplabs.internal) were returning the corrected record (10.42.12.55) consistently after the zone update and cache flush. Priya Nair (pnair) confirmed via dig queries from the Newark NOC.

Tested name resolution from affected application hosts APPHOST-NWK-04 and APPHOST-NWK-07 and confirmed that service.example.local resolved to the current IP 10.42.12.55 without further NXDOMAIN or stale-record responses. Kevin Ortiz (kortiz) validated application connectivity was fully restored.
