title: Internal hostname resolution failure - missing forwarder
description: Multiple internal users and application monitoring were trying to reach services by hostname under corp.internal, but internal names were returning NXDOMAIN from the primary resolver (DNS-RESOLVER-01.corp.internal, 10.40.2.10). The affected application, internal-service-app, could not make name-based connections to internal endpoints such as api-gateway.corp.internal and inventory-svc.corp.internal, creating a service interruption for users in the on-prem us-east-dc1 environment. Applied the same conditional forwarder configuration to the secondary DNS resolver (DNS-RESOLVER-02.corp.internal, 10.40.2.11) to restore consistent zone routing and redundancy across both resolvers.

Flushed DNS cache on both resolvers (DNS-RESOLVER-01 and DNS-RESOLVER-02) to clear stale negative and outdated NXDOMAIN entries for the impacted hostnames including api-gateway.corp.internal and inventory-svc.corp.internal.

Retested name resolution for affected corp.internal service names from resolver-side queries and from affected client networks — verified from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MS (10.40.17.55, user msandoval) in the Arlington office and from the Network Monitoring probe in us-east-dc1.

Confirmed monitoring and the dependent application (internal-service-app) could again resolve internal hostnames successfully. Maria Sandoval (E-40821) and Kevin Truong (ktruong) verified end-user and network-side restoration respectively, then documented the DNS forwarding configuration change under CHG-20260111-DNS.

title: Intermittent internal hostname resolution failures for service1.corp.local
description: Multiple internal application owners, including Raj Patel (DevOps lead) and members of the platform engineering team, were trying to reach service1.corp.local from several private subnets (10.20.0.0/16 and 10.30.0.0/16), but DNS lookups intermittently returned NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, or timed out, causing application timeouts for service1 and the internal-api-gateway. resolution_steps: Confirmed the authoritative DNS zone on ns1.corp.local and ns2.corp.local for service1.corp.local contained the intended current A record (10.50.12.40) and verified the low TTL (300s) and recent record change by kliu on 2026-01-11T21:47Z were correct.

Added the missing conditional forwarder configuration for the corp.local zone on dns-resolver-02.corp.local (10.50.1.11) so requests for the internal zone were routed to the correct authoritative path (ns1.corp.local, ns2.corp.local). Change performed by Marcus Webb (mwebb) and verified by Karen Liu.

Flushed caches on dns-resolver-01.corp.local (10.50.1.10) and dns-resolver-02.corp.local (10.50.1.11) using rndc flush to remove stale positive and negative cached entries that were continuing to return NXDOMAIN and timeouts after the record change. Verified cache clear via rndc dumpdb on both nodes.

Validated successful resolution of service1.corp.local from all monitored subnets — confirmed from rpatel's workstation at 10.20.5.88, pnair's host at 10.30.4.62, and additional test clients on 10.40.0.0/16 that all clients now received the same current address (10.50.12.40) consistently.

Continued monitoring via Network Monitoring dashboards after the change and performed staggered follow-up cache clearing on secondary caching layers where residual historical cache entries still produced intermittent lookup failures. Affected users include members of the platform engineering and QA groups working from the Newark office.
observed_errors: stale A record returned by resolver-01
root_cause: Internal DNS resolvers served stale cache data for internal-app.service.local, including an outdated A record pointing to a decommissioned IP, while TTL mismatch between the authoritative zone and resolver cache allowed the incorrect response to persist intermittently across resolver-01 and resolver-02.
resolution_steps: Verified the authoritative internal DNS zone entry on ns-auth-01.dns.corp.internal for internal-app.service.local and confirmed the A record was already updated to the current service IP 10.40.2.30; corrected the residual TTL value from 86400 to 300 seconds to match policy.

Flushed cached DNS entries on resolver-01.dns.corp.internal and resolver-02.dns.corp.internal using rndc flush to remove the stale record (10.40.1.15) and clear intermittent NXDOMAIN and timeout responses affecting users in the Newark region.
Restarted the DNS resolver service (named) on resolver-01.dns.corp.internal where persistent cached data was observed to ensure fresh zone data was served and no in-memory stale entries remained.

Validated name resolution from multiple internal clients — including Marcus Delgado's workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.22.4.87), the QA jump host at 10.22.6.50, and Network Monitoring probes in Newark and Ashburn — and confirmed queries returned the corrected A record (10.40.2.30) consistently.

Adjusted the internal TTL policy for service records to 300 seconds on ns-auth-01.dns.corp.internal and aligned resolver caching behavior (max-cache-ttl) on resolver-01 and resolver-02 to reduce the chance of prolonged stale responses. Change documented by Raj Okonkwo (rokonkwo) and reviewed by Priya Nair.

title: Intermittent internal name resolution failure for svc-db.internal
description: Users and monitoring systems in the Charlotte office were trying to resolve the internal service hostname svc-db.internal, but lookups intermittently returned NXDOMAIN from some internal resolvers (notably dns-resolver-02.corp.internal at 10.12.4.12) while other resolvers returned the expected A record (10.50.20.35). The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (emp ID E-40821) from the internal-devops team after a DNS zone update earlier the same day performed by network engineer Priya Nair. The failure impacted workstation access and monitoring consistency for the svc-db internal service across internal subnets in the us-east-1-internal environment.
observed_errors: Inconsistent A record answers between resolver-01 and resolver-02
root_cause: Inconsistent internal DNS state after the zone update: resolver-02 continued serving stale negative cache or outdated zone data for svc-db.internal while resolver-01 had refreshed, causing intermittent NXDOMAIN responses depending on which resolver answered the query.
resolution_steps: Verified the svc-db.internal A record (10.50.20.35), zone contents, and current SOA serial (2026011502) in the Internal DNS Zone to confirm the record existed and the post-change data committed by pnair was correct.

Compared lookup results across dns-resolver-01.corp.internal (10.12.4.11) and dns-resolver-02.corp.internal (10.12.4.12) and confirmed resolver-02 was the source of intermittent NXDOMAIN responses while resolver-01 returned the expected record 10.50.20.35 for svc-db.internal.

Flushed stale cache on the affected internal resolver dns-resolver-02.corp.internal (10.12.4.12) and reloaded the updated zone data so both resolvers served the same current answer (10.50.20.35) for svc-db.internal. Priya Nair confirmed the zone transfer completed successfully after the reload.

Reviewed resolver configuration for the internal zone on dns-resolver-02.corp.internal, including conditional forwarding and zone refresh behavior, to ensure resolver-02 was using the correct authoritative data path after the zone change. Corrected the forwarder target to point to the primary zone host rather than the lagging secondary.

Re-ran validation queries from affected internal paths — including Marcus Delgado's workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.12.6.88) and Lisa Hwang's machine — and confirmed consistent successful resolution of svc-db.internal (10.50.20.35) across resolvers and Network Monitoring checks. Notified mdelgado@corplabs.com that the issue was resolved.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm which resolver IP your workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD is using (we expect either 10.12.4.11 or 10.12.4.12) and whether the same lookup fails from other internal subnets so we can isolate whether the issue is client-specific or resolver-specific. You can run nslookup svc-db.internal from your machine and share the output. Also, can you confirm if colleagues on the same VLAN are seeing the same behavior?

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failures for internal service payroll-svc
description: Finance users in the Charlotte office were trying to reach payroll-svc.internal.corp this morning, but the internal service hostname intermittently failed to resolve from the primary on-prem DNS resolver (dns-resolver-01.internal.corp, 10.40.2.10). Some lookups returned NXDOMAIN or SERVFAIL, while direct access by IP (10.40.50.22) still worked, blocking normal access to the payroll service by name. The issue was first reported by Maria Espinoza (mespinoza, EMP-90412) via the Finance team channel. Investigation showed the primary resolver was intermittently serving a stale A record (pointing to decommissioned address 10.40.50.18) that did not match the current authoritative internal zone data on ns-auth-01.internal.corp.
root_cause: Primary on-prem DNS resolver cache retained and intermittently served a stale A record for payroll-svc.internal.corp that no longer matched the authoritative internal zone, causing intermittent NXDOMAIN/SERVFAIL and failed name resolution.
resolution_steps: Compared responses from the primary resolver dns-resolver-01.internal.corp (10.40.2.10) and the authoritative internal DNS server ns-auth-01.internal.corp to confirm the resolver was returning stale data (10.40.50.18) for payroll-svc.internal.corp instead of the current record (10.40.50.22).
Cleared cached DNS entries on the primary resolver dns-resolver-01.internal.corp using rndc flush to remove the outdated A record (10.40.50.18) from cache. Executed by ktran at 01:38 UTC.

Forced a reload of the authoritative internal zone on ns-auth-01.internal.corp using rndc reload to ensure the current payroll-svc.internal.corp record (10.40.50.22, zone serial 2026011502) was being served consistently.

Restarted the named service on the primary resolver dns-resolver-01.internal.corp (systemctl restart named) to reset resolver state and eliminate lingering stale cache behavior. Service confirmed healthy via rndc status.

Reduced the TTL for the affected A record from 86400s to 300s (5 minutes) and adjusted DNS caching policy for critical internal services in the internal.corp zone to reduce stale-serving windows during future record changes. Change documented under CHG-44821.

Validated successful name resolution with nslookup/dig from multiple sites — WORKSTATION-PC-ME (10.40.11.87, Charlotte) and WORKSTATION-PC-JW (10.40.12.44, Raleigh) — and confirmed Network Monitoring alerts cleared after fresh responses matched the authoritative zone. Maria Espinoza and James Whitfield confirmed payroll-svc.internal.corp was loading reliably by hostname.

title: Internal hostname resolving to stale IP
description: Multiple internal services, including the Inventory Service and Internal API Gateway, could not reliably reach api.internal.corp by name from Linux application servers in corp-dc-1 at the Denver data center. DNS lookups intermittently returned either a stale A record (10.0.1.45) or NXDOMAIN, blocking application connectivity to the internal API endpoint after a recent internal DNS record update. Issue was first reported by Marcus Jennings (emp ID: E-40821) from the platform engineering team, and subsequently confirmed by additional users on the same subnet.
observed_errors: stale A record 10.0.1.45 returned from resolver
root_cause: An outdated A record and stale cached DNS data for api.internal.corp were being served by internal resolvers after the zone record changed, causing inconsistent responses between the authoritative internal zone and resolver cache.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the authoritative internal DNS zone entry on ns1.corp-dc-1.internal for api.internal.corp and corrected the A record to the current service IP (10.0.2.90), confirming the update applied by kaldrich on 2026-01-15.
Validated the zone update in DNS management on ns1.corp-dc-1.internal and confirmed the record TTL (300s) and recent change state were consistent with the intended configuration.
Flushed stale cache entries on the primary DNS resolver dns-resolver-01.corp-dc-1.internal so new queries would no longer return the prior IP address 10.0.1.45.

Cleared local resolver caches on affected Linux application servers, including WORKSTATION-LNX-MJ (10.20.5.12) and the host at 10.20.5.17 where nscd had been restarted, to remove retained stale answers.

Retested name resolution and application connectivity from affected servers — Marcus Jennings confirmed api.internal.corp consistently resolved to 10.0.2.90 from WORKSTATION-LNX-MJ without NXDOMAIN responses, and Priya Nair verified the same from her host.

Monitored DNS and application health via Network Monitoring dashboards for two hours after remediation and confirmed no recurrence of lookup failures across the Denver data center. Kevin Aldrich closed the ticket after final verification.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm whether all affected hosts are resolving api.internal.corp to the same IP and whether failures show a stale address or NXDOMAIN. Could you also run nslookup from WORKSTATION-LNX-MJ and from at least one other app server (e.g., the host Priya Nair uses at 10.20.5.17) so we can compare? — Kevin Aldrich, Network Operations

title: Intermittent internal hostname resolution failing for api.internal.corp
description: Internal users and monitoring were trying to reach the service at api.internal.corp, but name resolution intermittently returned a stale A record (10.40.2.15) instead of the current service IP (10.40.5.80). The issue was first reported by Priya Nambiar from the Portland development team, who noticed API calls from her workstation WORKSTATION-DEV-PN were timing out. The authoritative internal zone already contained the updated record, yet some internal DNS resolvers and probes continued to answer with the previous address, causing intermittent failures for applications that connect to the API by hostname from corp-datacenter-1. Additional reports came in from dev team members Raj Menon and Lisa Cheng, confirming the issue was not isolated to a single client.
observed_errors: stale A record returned by resolver
inconsistent dig responses between authoritative server and resolver
root_cause: A stale cached A record remained on one or more internal recursive resolvers/forwarders after the DNS record change, so clients querying different resolver paths intermittently received the previous IP even though the authoritative zone had the updated address.
resolution_steps: Queried api.internal.corp against the authoritative DNS server (AUTH-DNS-01) and internal recursive resolvers (RSLV-INT-02, RSLV-INT-03) to confirm the authoritative zone served the new IP (10.40.5.80) while some resolver paths—particularly RSLV-INT-03 in Portland—still returned the previous address (10.40.2.15).

Flushed cache entries for api.internal.corp on the affected internal resolvers RSLV-INT-02 and RSLV-INT-03 and reloaded the resolver service so recursive nodes stopped serving the stale A record. Verified with user pnambiar that her workstation WORKSTATION-DEV-PN began resolving correctly after the flush.

Reviewed and corrected internal forwarder/cache behavior on FWD-ZONE-01 for the zone to ensure requests for the internal domain were routed to the proper authoritative source (AUTH-DNS-01) instead of reusing outdated cached data. Agent dkovalenko confirmed forwarder configuration was consistent with the expected zone delegation.

Kept the record TTL at 300 seconds to shorten cache persistence during the change window and verified the authoritative zone serial and A record data were current on the internal DNS infrastructure. DNS admin mforrester confirmed no further zone changes were pending.

Re-tested name resolution from multiple internal resolver paths and monitoring locations—including workstations belonging to pnambiar (10.22.17.44), rmenon, and lcheng—until dig responses consistently returned the updated IP (10.40.5.80) and the service was reachable by hostname without recurrence.

title: Internal DNS resolution failure for app-service.internal (stale A record)
description: The app team (reported by Marcus Delgado, emp ID E-40291) was trying to reach the internal service by the hostname app-service.internal in prod-east from the Ashburn data center, but clients intermittently failed name resolution. Monitoring on Network Monitoring dashboard showed bursts of NXDOMAIN responses and some lookups returning the retired IP 192.0.2.45 (previously assigned to decommissioned host WORKSTATION-APPOLD-MD), which prevented the application from consistently reaching its internal endpoint from multiple client subnets including 10.40.12.0/24. Initial report came via email to dns-ops@corplabs.com from m.delgado@corplabs.com.
root_cause: A duplicate and stale A record for app-service.internal remained in the internal DNS zone, and resolver caches continued serving the retired address 192.0.2.45, causing intermittent NXDOMAIN responses and stale DNS answers.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the internal DNS zone for app-service.internal (zone managed by dns-admin rchen) and identified the duplicate stale A record pointing to retired host IP 192.0.2.45, originally associated with decommissioned host WORKSTATION-APPOLD-MD.
Removed the stale DNS entry (performed by rchen via Internal DNS Zone console) and confirmed the authoritative zone retained only the correct A record 10.40.8.20 for app-service.internal.
Lowered the DNS TTL temporarily from 3600 to 300 seconds to speed propagation of the corrected record across internal resolvers and clients in the Ashburn prod-east environment.

Flushed DNS cache entries on dns-resolver-01.corplabs.internal and dns-resolver-02.corplabs.internal so cached stale responses (192.0.2.45) would no longer be served to clients such as WORKSTATION-DEV-KP (10.40.12.87).

Validated that monitoring and representative client hosts in prod-east (including WORKSTATION-DEV-KP at 10.40.12.87, user kpatel) resolved app-service.internal to the correct address 10.40.8.20 without further NXDOMAIN or stale-IP responses. Confirmed resolution with Marcus Delgado (m.delgado@corplabs.com).

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failures for svc-inventory.internal.corp
description: Users and monitoring reported intermittent DNS resolution failures for svc-inventory.internal.corp starting around 08:30 from some internal subnets in the Austin office. The issue was initially flagged by Rajesh Menon (r.menon, EMP-40821) from the platform engineering team. The service remained reachable by direct IP (10.42.16.55), but affected clients could not consistently reach the application by hostname because DNS queries intermittently timed out and sometimes returned NXDOMAIN for the internal zone. Affected workstations included WORKSTATION-RMENON-L1 on subnet 10.42.16.0/24.
root_cause: Intermittent name resolution was caused by an internal DNS resolver path issue affecting some subnets, most consistent with an incorrect or missing conditional forwarder and stale cached responses on one or more internal resolvers for the internal.corp zone.
resolution_steps: Validated that affected clients including WORKSTATION-RMENON-L1 (10.42.16.112, user r.menon) were using internal resolver 10.42.1.12 that intermittently returned timeouts and NXDOMAIN for svc-inventory.internal.corp while direct IP connectivity to the service at 10.42.16.55 remained healthy.

Reviewed the internal DNS zone on DNS-AUTH-02.internal.corp and confirmed the svc-inventory.internal.corp A record was present with the expected target 10.42.16.55, indicating the issue was in resolver pathing rather than service availability.

Corrected the conditional forwarder configuration on resolver 10.42.1.12 for the internal.corp zone — updated from the decommissioned server 10.42.1.5 to the active authoritative DNS server DNS-AUTH-02.internal.corp (10.42.1.20) — so queries for internal.corp were sent to the proper authoritative DNS servers. Change performed by Patricia Hwang (p.hwang).

Flushed DNS cache on the impacted internal resolver 10.42.1.12 to remove stale negative and outdated cached responses that were causing intermittent lookup failures for the Austin 10.42.16.0/24 subnet.

Retested name resolution from affected subnets — confirmed consistent successful lookups for svc-inventory.internal.corp from WORKSTATION-RMENON-L1 and other Austin hosts without further timeout or NXDOMAIN responses. Rajesh Menon (r.menon) confirmed the issue was resolved.

title: Intermittent failure resolving app.internal.corp from internal network
description: Multiple internal users and services were trying to reach the internal application endpoint app.internal.corp from different office subnets (primarily the Newark and Richmond offices), but DNS resolution intermittently failed. Reports were initially filed by Maria Chen (emp ID E-40821) and confirmed by additional users on the 10.16.0.0/16 and 10.18.0.0/16 segments. Some lookups returned NXDOMAIN while others resolved to an outdated IP address (10.20.30.40), preventing dependent services and users from consistently connecting to the application by hostname across the internal network. The issue was first noticed around 05:50 UTC when automated health checks from WORKSTATION-PC-MCHEN began failing.
observed_errors: NXDOMAIN for app.internal.corp from site-A resolvers
Resolver returned stale A record 10.20.30.40 for app.internal.corp despite recent change
root_cause: Stale DNS data for app.internal.corp was being served by internal resolvers, causing intermittent responses between NXDOMAIN and an outdated A record after a record change.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the internal DNS zone for app.internal.corp on DNS-AUTH-01 and corrected the A record to the current intended IP address 10.20.31.15 (previously pointing to deprecated 10.20.30.40, last modified by rgarcia on 2026-01-16).

Compared resolver responses from DNS-RES-01 (10.16.0.5, Newark) and DNS-RES-02 (10.18.0.5, Richmond) against the authoritative zone data on DNS-AUTH-01 to confirm that internal resolvers were serving stale or inconsistent results — NXDOMAIN from DNS-RES-01 and 10.20.30.40 from DNS-RES-02.

Flushed DNS caches on the primary (DNS-RES-01) and secondary (DNS-RES-02) internal resolvers and triggered a zone reload on DNS-AUTH-01 so current data would be served immediately across all internal segments.

Retested name resolution for app.internal.corp from previously affected network segments in Newark and Richmond — Maria Chen confirmed from WORKSTATION-PC-MCHEN (10.16.4.87) and David Okafor confirmed from 10.18.2.33 that the hostname consistently returned the correct address 10.20.31.15.

Lowered the TTL for the affected zone record from 3600s to 300s to reduce propagation delay for future DNS changes and documented the update in the DNS change log. Notified rgarcia of the TTL policy adjustment for the internal.corp zone.

title: BitLocker not enabling
description: I was trying to bring a company-managed Windows 11 Enterprise laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-DELL-MR, asset tag EMP-78234) into encryption compliance for user Marcus Reilly (mreilly@corplabs.com), but Company Portal showed the device as noncompliant for encryption. BitLocker reported that encryption was not enabled on the C: volume, Intune showed no escrowed recovery key for this device, and earlier provisioning attempts failed when creating the TPM-backed protector. The device is located at our Portland office and is assigned to the Corporate Laptops group. This blocked the device from meeting corporate endpoint security requirements until disk encryption and key escrow were successfully completed.
observed_errors: Intune: No recovery key found for device
TPM initialization error during protector creation (reported during enablement step)
root_cause: TPM protector was not initialized on the endpoint, preventing BitLocker from creating the required TPM-backed protector and blocking recovery key escrow to Intune/Device Compliance Service.
resolution_steps: Validated TPM state on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and initialized the TPM protector locally using Initialize-Tpm, clearing legacy TPM ownership where needed so BitLocker could use the hardware protector.

Enabled BitLocker again on the C: volume using the TPM protector (manage-bde -on C: -RecoveryPassword) and confirmed encryption started successfully instead of returning the earlier TPM initialization failure.
Forced an Intune device sync from WORKSTATION-DELL-MR (10.42.18.97) and verified the assigned disk encryption policy was present on the endpoint for user mreilly without assignment issues.
Rotated the BitLocker recovery key on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR and confirmed the current key escrowed successfully to Intune/Device Compliance Service under the device record for mreilly.

Monitored encryption and compliance status on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR until BitLocker showed enabled on C:, the recovery key was visible to support in Intune, and the device returned to compliant status in Intune and Company Portal for user Marcus Reilly (mreilly).
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm what you see in Company Portal and BitLocker status on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR. We need to verify whether encryption is off on the C: volume, whether a recovery key appears in Intune for this device, and whether provisioning showed any TPM-related failure. Could you also confirm the device's current IP address so we can cross-reference Intune enrollment records? You can reach me at ext. 4417 or dkhan@corplabs.com if you'd prefer to walk through this over the phone.

title: BitLocker not enabled and recovery key not escrowed on corporate device
description: A corporate Windows 10 21H2 laptop, WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH (asset tag PC-1234), assigned to Marco Hoffmann (emp ID EMP-90214) in the Frankfurt office, was flagged noncompliant in Intune because disk encryption was not fully compliant. I could not complete required corporate compliance checks because BitLocker protection showed as suspended and the management service did not have an escrowed recovery key available for support recovery. The device was enrolled under the user account mhoffmann and had IP 10.42.17.88 at the time of enrollment. Enrollment evidence indicated the issue started during initial device enrollment when recovery key backup failed with error 0x87D1FDE8.
root_cause: BitLocker recovery key escrow failed during initial MDM enrollment, leaving the device with a protector present but no recovery key recorded in the Device Compliance Service, while BitLocker protection remained suspended.
resolution_steps: Confirmed TPM 2.0 availability and existing BitLocker protector state on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH (PC-1234, user mhoffmann, EMP-90214), then verified the device was receiving the assigned encryption policy EMEA-Sales-Encryption-v3 in Intune.

Rotated the BitLocker recovery key on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH using manage-bde -protectors -delete C: followed by manage-bde -protectors -add C: -RecoveryPassword, and triggered a fresh recovery key backup to the Device Compliance Service to replace the missing escrow record for mhoffmann.

Forced an Intune/Windows MDM sync from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH (IP 10.42.17.88) via Company Portal so the updated protector and escrow status were reported to compliance services. Sync completed successfully at 2026-01-17T18:38Z.

Validated that the new recovery key was visible in the Device Compliance Service under Marco Hoffmann's device record (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH) and available for support recovery operations. Confirmed with agent Lukas Brandt (lbrandt@corplabs.com) that the key was accessible.

Re-enabled BitLocker protection on the OS drive C: using manage-bde -protectors -enable C:, verified encryption protection was active (AES-256, full volume), and confirmed the device returned to compliant status in Intune. Notified Marco Hoffmann at marco.hoffmann@corplabs.com that the issue was resolved.
agent_questions: We confirmed Intune shows device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MH (PC-1234), registered to mhoffmann, as noncompliant for encryption. The Intune device record lists the primary user as Marco Hoffmann (marco.hoffmann@corplabs.com). Can you confirm whether this is the same corporate laptop PC-1234 and whether any recent enrollment or reset activity occurred before the compliance failure appeared?

title: Device noncompliant for BitLocker — Intune shows conflicting state
description: I noticed that corporate Windows 11 Enterprise laptop WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (asset tag SLS-4821) assigned to Marcus Reeves (mreeves, employee ID E-50274) in the Dallas office is flagged as noncompliant for disk encryption in Intune Device Compliance. The BitLocker policy appeared assigned in Microsoft Endpoint Manager and the device intermittently reported encrypted in MDM, but local BitLocker status showed encryption was not properly enabled and no protector was present. The recovery key was not visible in the tenant, preventing reliable recovery-key-backed encrypted boot support and leaving the device out of compliance. Marcus reported the issue after receiving a compliance notification email at marcus.reeves@corplabs.com.
observed_errors: Device marked noncompliant for encryption in Device Compliance
root_cause: BitLocker policy was assigned, but the endpoint did not have a valid TPM/recovery protector in place and repeated recovery key escrow attempts to Intune failed, leaving MDM compliance state out of sync with the local BitLocker configuration.
resolution_steps: Verified the assigned BitLocker policy 'Corporate BitLocker Policy - Sales' in Microsoft Endpoint Manager for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (mreeves, E-50274) and triggered a fresh device sync via Company Portal to confirm the endpoint was receiving the current encryption configuration.

Checked local BitLocker and TPM state on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (IP 10.42.18.97), then reinitialized the TPM-based protector using Initialize-Tpm and manage-bde after confirming the device was TPM-ready (TPM 2.0, firmware 7.2.1.0) and that no valid protector was present. Performed by Priya Nair (pnair).

Added the required BitLocker TPM protector locally on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR via manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tpm and confirmed the protector was successfully created (protector ID visible in manage-bde output) before proceeding with key management actions.

Rotated and re-escrowed the recovery key to the tenant from Endpoint Manager using BackupToAAD-BitLockerKeyProtector for WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, then verified the recovery key became visible to support in the management service under Marcus Reeves's device record.

Ran a follow-up sync on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and validated that local BitLocker status (manage-bde -status C: showing FullyEncrypted with TPM protector), escrowed recovery key presence in the tenant, and Intune Device Compliance status all reflected an encrypted and compliant state. Notified mreeves at marcus.reeves@corplabs.com that the device is now compliant.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus — please confirm whether BitLocker shows any protectors locally on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (IP 10.42.18.97) and whether a recovery key is visible in Endpoint Manager for this laptop. You can check locally by running manage-bde -protectors -get C: from an elevated prompt. Also, could you verify the device serial and confirm you're logged in as mreeves?

title: BitLocker not enabled
description: I was trying to get the Azure AD joined Windows 10 21H2 device (hostname WORKSTATION-SALES-MR, asset tag SLS-4821) assigned to Marcus Reeves (mreeves@corplabs.com, EMP-90274) into encryption compliance through Intune, but the endpoint showed BitLocker EncryptionState as Off, no recovery key was visible in Azure AD for this device, and the user never received a BitLocker PIN prompt. TPM management (tpm.msc) showed the TPM was not initialized, which prevented the device from enabling disk encryption and left it noncompliant in the Device Compliance Service. The device is located at our Phoenix office and connects from IP 10.42.17.88.
observed_errors: Device compliance state: Noncompliant for Encryption
root_cause: The device TPM was not initialized, so BitLocker could not create and use the required TPM protector to start encryption. In addition, the Intune BitLocker policy had not fully applied before remediation, so recovery key escrow to Azure AD had not occurred while the device remained noncompliant.
resolution_steps: Validated the endpoint state on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR (assigned to Marcus Reeves, mreeves, EMP-90274) in TPM management and BitLocker tooling, confirming TPM status was Not initialized, BitLocker was Off on C:, and no recovery key was escrowed to Azure AD for this device.

Initialized the TPM on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR using Initialize-Tpm and enabled the required TPM-based BitLocker protector on the device so the encryption prerequisites were satisfied. Verified tpm.msc now showed 'The TPM is ready for use.'

Started BitLocker encryption on the C: system volume of WORKSTATION-SALES-MR using the TPM protector (Enable-BitLocker -MountPoint C: -TpmProtector) and confirmed encryption began successfully — manage-bde reported Conversion Status: Encryption in Progress.

Forced an Intune device sync on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR via Company Portal so the assigned BitLocker configuration policy (Corp-Encryption-Win10) and compliance evaluation were reapplied to the endpoint. Device compliance state for mreeves updated to Compliant.

Backed up and rotated the BitLocker recovery key on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR using BackupToAAD-BitLockerKeyProtector and verified the current key (ID 7A3F2B) was escrowed to Azure AD under mreeves's device record, then confirmed the device compliance state changed to compliant in the Device Compliance Service. Sent confirmation to Marcus Reeves at mreeves@corplabs.com.

title: BitLocker not enabled and recovery key not escrowed
description: A managed Windows 10 21H2 corporate laptop (hostname: WORKSTATION-DELL-MR, asset tag ENG-4821) assigned to Marcus Reeves (emp ID E-20487) in the Portland office was reported as noncompliant for disk encryption in Intune. The device, with IP 10.42.17.93, could not meet endpoint compliance requirements because BitLocker was not enabled locally and no recovery key was visible in Azure AD/Intune for the user mreeves. Local checks via manage-bde showed the TPM protector was not initialized, which prevented BitLocker from starting, and later MDM sync attempts intermittently failed to escrow the generated recovery key, causing compliance status to lag and temporarily toggle between noncompliant and pending.
observed_errors: Intune key escrow failed: intermittent timeout on key escrow API
Device compliance: encryption not enabled (portal flag)
root_cause: BitLocker could not start because the device TPM protector was not initialized, and recovery key escrow to Intune/Azure AD was intermittently failing during MDM sync, delaying compliant status after local remediation.
resolution_steps: Confirmed TPM was present on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR but no usable BitLocker TPM protector had been initialized — Get-Tpm showed TPMReady: False. Ran Initialize-Tpm to prepare the TPM module, then added a TPM protector locally via manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tpm so the device could support BitLocker protectors.

Enabled BitLocker on the C: system drive of WORKSTATION-DELL-MR using manage-bde -on C: and generated a new 48-digit recovery key after the TPM protector was successfully added. Encryption began immediately and progressed without errors.

No BitLocker recovery key is visible in Azure AD, and the initial report did not include the device name, TPM state, or last Intune sync details. The user reached out from the Portland office and the issue affects BitLocker compliance and blocks the device from meeting endpoint security requirements for normal corporate use. The ticket was submitted on behalf of the user by mdelgado@corplabs.com.
observed_errors: No BitLocker recovery key found in Azure AD
Device Compliance Service shows noncompliant for encryption
root_cause: BitLocker was not fully enabled on the endpoint, so no valid recovery key had been escrowed to Azure AD. Based on the ticket evidence, the most likely contributing conditions were missing or unapplied Intune BitLocker policy and unverified TPM/protector readiness, which left the device reporting encryption as disabled and therefore noncompliant.
resolution_steps: Identify the affected device in Intune (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD, user mdelgado, EMP-40291) and confirm the assigned BitLocker or Endpoint Security disk encryption policy is targeted to the device without assignment conflicts. Verify the device object in Intune matches the expected hostname and user principal name mdelgado@corplabs.com.

Validate TPM readiness on the Windows endpoint WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD and initialize the TPM or BitLocker protector if it is present but not ready for use by encryption policy. Run tpm.msc or Get-Tpm via PowerShell to confirm TPM 2.0 is enabled and owned, and coordinate with Marcus Delgado (phone: 503-447-8126) if on-device action is needed.

Force an Intune device sync on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD so the active encryption policy is reapplied and the endpoint can begin BitLocker enablement. This can be triggered from the Intune portal under the device record for mdelgado or via the Company Portal app on the device.

Enable BitLocker on the system drive (C:) using the managed policy path and verify the device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD reports encryption in progress or protection on. Confirm via manage-bde -status that the volume is fully encrypted with a TPM protector.

Escrow or rotate the BitLocker recovery key to Azure AD after protection is enabled on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD, then confirm the recovery key is visible in the device record under Azure AD > Devices > mdelgado's device > BitLocker keys.

Recheck Intune compliance after policy refresh and key escrow to confirm the device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD no longer reports 'Encryption not enabled' and returns to compliant status. Notify Marcus Delgado at mdelgado@corplabs.com and close the ticket once compliance is verified.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, please provide the device name (hostname), confirm whether TPM is ready on the laptop, and share the last Intune sync time so we can verify BitLocker policy application and recovery key escrow status. You can find the TPM status by running tpm.msc on the device. Also, please confirm if the device hostname is something like WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD or similar so we can look it up in Intune.

title: BitLocker not enabled
description: A corporate Surface Pro 7 laptop assigned to Marcus Delgado (employee ID EMP-40291) showed "Encryption not enabled" in Intune. The device, hostname WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MD, was marked noncompliant for BitLocker, and no recovery key was visible in Azure AD. The issue affected BitLocker enforcement on a Windows 10 21H2 Azure AD joined endpoint used by the Sales team in the Dallas office and blocked the device from meeting corporate encryption compliance requirements. The user reported the issue after receiving a compliance notification at mdelgado@corplabs.com.
observed_errors: Intune shows 'Encryption not enabled' for device
Recovery keys not found in Azure AD for device
BitLocker failed to start due to TPM protector not initialized
root_cause: The device TPM protector had not been initialized, which prevented BitLocker from starting and completing encryption. In addition, an earlier recovery key escrow attempt failed during enrollment, leaving no recovery key stored in Azure AD for support and compliance validation.
resolution_steps: Validated TPM status on the affected device WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MD (mdelgado, EMP-40291) using `Get-Tpm` and initialized the TPM protector via `Initialize-Tpm` so BitLocker could create a valid hardware-backed protector.
Enabled BitLocker encryption locally on the endpoint WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MD after TPM readiness was confirmed, using `Enable-BitLocker -MountPoint C: -TpmProtector -EncryptionMethod XtsAes256`.

Forced an Intune device sync from Company Portal on WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MD and re-applied the assigned BitLocker encryption policy "Corp-BitLocker-Enforce" so the device could receive current compliance settings.

Rotated and generated a current recovery key using `manage-bde -protectors -add C: -RecoveryPassword` and escrowed it to Azure AD via `BackupToAAD-BitLockerKeyProtector -MountPoint C:`, then verified that the key was visible for WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MD under mdelgado's device objects.

Confirmed the device encryption state on WORKSTATION-SURFACE-MD (C: volume 100% encrypted, XTS-AES 256) and monitored Intune and Device Compliance Service until the endpoint reported compliant for BitLocker. Notified Marcus Delgado at mdelgado@corplabs.com that the issue was resolved.

title: BitLocker not enabling
description: My corporate Windows 10 laptop (hostname WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, asset tag SLS-4821) remained noncompliant for disk encryption in Intune. The device, assigned to my account mreeves (employee ID E-50274), showed encryption not enabled, no BitLocker recovery key was visible in escrow, and I was blocked from meeting endpoint compliance requirements on a managed UEFI/TPM 2.0 laptop. A prior policy push appeared to apply, but the endpoint at IP 10.22.47.115 still reported conflicting encryption state and missing key escrow. I need this resolved before my client meetings in Charlotte next week.
root_cause: BitLocker enablement was initiated before TPM protection was fully initialized, so the device entered a partial or conflicting encryption state and the recovery key escrow operation to the management service timed out. Intune policy assignment was present, but compliance remained noncompliant until TPM protector initialization, encryption start, and recovery key escrow were completed and verified.
resolution_steps: Validated TPM readiness on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and initialized the TPM-based BitLocker protector so the device had a valid hardware-backed protector before retrying encryption. Confirmed via manage-bde -protectors -get C: that the TPM protector was active.

Started BitLocker encryption again on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR after TPM initialization to move the endpoint out of the prior conflicting state where policy had applied but encryption and escrow were incomplete. manage-bde -on C: completed without error.

Forced an Intune device sync for mreeves (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR, IP 10.22.47.115) and re-applied the assigned disk encryption policy 'Corp-BitLocker-Encrypt-v3' so the endpoint could process the current BitLocker configuration and compliance evaluation.

Rotated the BitLocker recovery key on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR and retried escrow to the management service, then verified that the recovery key record became visible to support under the mreeves device object in Azure AD.

Confirmed the endpoint WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR reported encrypted status and allowed time for compliance evaluation to refresh until Intune no longer showed EncryptionNotEnabled or missing escrow for user mreeves. Notified Marcus Reeves at mreeves@corplabs.com that the device is now compliant.

title: Corporate laptop not showing BitLocker enabled
description: User Marcus Delgado (EMP-40291) reported that his recently Autopilot-provisioned corporate Windows 10 Enterprise 21H2 laptop (hostname LAPTOP-MDELGADO-7) showed BitLocker as Off and was marked noncompliant in Microsoft Intune for device encryption. The device (IP 10.42.17.83) had no recovery key escrowed in Azure AD, so the endpoint could not reach required encryption compliance after provisioning. A manual Intune sync had already been attempted by Marcus without creating a recovery key or changing compliance state. The user is based in the Charlotte office and needs the laptop compliant for an upcoming client engagement.
observed_errors: No recovery key found in Azure AD for device
root_cause: BitLocker could not complete enablement because the TPM protector was not initialized on the device after provisioning, which prevented creation of a valid protector and blocked recovery key escrow to Azure AD.
resolution_steps: Validated that the TPM was present and available on LAPTOP-MDELGADO-7 (IP 10.42.17.83) via tpm.msc and Get-Tpm, then reviewed BitLocker state with manage-bde -status C: to confirm encryption was still off and no usable protector had been established for user mdelgado's device.

Cleared residual or incomplete protector state using manage-bde -protectors -delete C: and initialized the TPM-based BitLocker protector locally on LAPTOP-MDELGADO-7 by running Initialize-Tpm followed by manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tpm. Desktop support engineer Diana Kwan (dkwan) performed this step remotely.

Re-applied the corporate BitLocker configuration (Corp-Encryption-Win10-Standard) from Intune so LAPTOP-MDELGADO-7 received the expected TPM protector and encryption settings, including the recovery key escrow directive targeting Azure AD.

Forced an Intune device sync on LAPTOP-MDELGADO-7 via Company Portal and verified that BitLocker started properly on the C: drive and generated a recovery key for the endpoint. manage-bde -status C: confirmed 'Encryption in Progress' with TPM protector active.

Confirmed the recovery key was escrowed to Azure AD under the device record for LAPTOP-MDELGADO-7 and then verified Intune compliance updated from 'Encryption not enabled' to Compliant. Notified Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) at the Charlotte office that the device was now fully compliant and the ticket could be closed.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, please confirm whether BitLocker shows Off locally on LAPTOP-MDELGADO-7 and whether this device was recently Autopilot-provisioned. You can reach me at x4418 or dkwan@corplabs.com if you need to follow up offline.

title: BitLocker not enabled

observed_errors: No recovery key found in Azure AD / Intune escrow
Device compliance: Noncompliant for Disk Encryption
root_cause: The device was not receiving the required Intune BitLocker encryption policy, and the TPM protector was in a NotInitialized state. Together these conditions prevented BitLocker from starting and blocked recovery key escrow to Azure AD/Intune.
resolution_steps: Assigned the correct Intune BitLocker encryption policy 'BL-Sales-Mobile-West' to device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR (W10-123, user mreeves) by adding the device to the 'Sales - Mobile Devices' Intune group so the endpoint could receive the required disk encryption settings.

Forced an Intune device sync on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR via Sync-IntuneDevice to refresh policy application and update the endpoint with the current encryption configuration. Sync completed successfully within 90 seconds.

Initiated BitLocker encryption on the device using Enable-BitLocker -MountPoint C: -EncryptionMethod XtsAes256 -RecoveryPasswordProtector and verified the status changed from not enabled to encryption pending and then enabled. Full volume encryption completed in approximately 18 minutes.

Rotated the BitLocker recovery key via BackupToAAD-BitLockerKeyProtector, confirmed escrow to Azure AD/Intune (recovery key ID 7F2A91xx visible under mreeves's device record), and verified the device WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MR returned to a compliant encryption state in the Device Compliance Service. title: BitLocker encryption failed: TPM protector not initialized and recovery key not escrowed
description: Windows BitLocker was not enabled on a managed Windows 10 21H2 device (hostname WORKSTATION-SALES-MR, asset tag WS-4417) assigned to Marcus Reeves (emp ID EMP-90234) in the Portland office. Control Panel showed the C: drive as not protected, and Intune marked the device noncompliant for the required disk encryption policy ('EP-Win10-Encryption-v3'). This prevented the device from meeting encryption compliance requirements and indicated the initial BitLocker encryption workflow did not complete successfully during provisioning.
observed_errors: Intune: No recovery key on record
Device Compliance: Noncompliant for 'Require disk encryption'
root_cause: BitLocker encryption could not complete because the TPM was in an unowned or cleared state and no TPM protector was initialized. Without a valid protector, BitLocker did not generate a usable recovery key, so Intune had no key to escrow and the device remained noncompliant for disk encryption.
resolution_steps: Initialize and verify TPM readiness on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR by running 'Initialize-Tpm' in an elevated PowerShell session, then confirm Get-Tpm returns TpmReady: True so the device can support a TPM-based BitLocker protector.

Add the BitLocker TPM protector for the C: system drive after TPM initialization is complete by running 'Add-BitLockerKeyProtector -MountPoint C: -TpmProtector' and verify the protector is listed via 'manage-bde -protectors -get C:'.

Enable BitLocker encryption on the C: volume using 'Enable-BitLocker -MountPoint C: -RecoveryPasswordProtector' and confirm that a 48-digit numerical recovery key is generated locally as part of the protection setup. Verify encryption progress with 'manage-bde -status C:'.

Force an Intune device sync on WORKSTATION-SALES-MR via Company Portal or 'Start-IntuneSync' so updated BitLocker state and the recovery key can be reported to the management service. Confirm sync completes successfully in the Intune portal.

Validate that the recovery key is escrowed in Intune (Devices > WORKSTATION-SALES-MR > Recovery keys) and confirm the device changes from noncompliant to compliant for the 'Require disk encryption' policy. Notify Marcus Reeves (mreeves, marcus.reeves@corplabs.com) that encryption is active and the device is now compliant.

Retested affected client connections for kwhitfield (WORKSTATION-MBP-KW), jmorales (10.22.48.117), and other impacted Sales users — confirmed successful EAP-TLS handshakes and normal network access on CorpWiFi for the majority of impacted devices. Retested representative affected clients on the Corporate SSID, including Elena Richter's and Markus Hahn's devices, and confirmed they received normal network access (correct VLAN, full connectivity) without repeated disconnects or quarantine placement.
