observed_errors: certificate expired presented by load balancer
root_cause: The F5 load balancer served a certificate bundle containing an expired intermediate certificate even though the endpoint certificate itself had been renewed successfully. Monitoring and deployment evidence were insufficient to confirm when the active LB chain diverged from the intended full bundle.
resolution_steps: Rebuild the full certificate bundle with the renewed server certificate (CN=svc-internal.corplabs.internal, serial 0A:3F:7B:22) and the correct current intermediate chain (DigiCert SHA2 Secure Server CA, valid through 2031-11-09) from the issuing CA. Bundle assembled by nwong and verified with openssl verify -CAfile.

Explicitly bind the corrected chain bundle (intermediate-digicert-2026.crt) to the F5 virtual server vs-svc-internal-443 via SSL profile ssl-svc-internal and remove the stale intermediate object intermediate-digicert-2024.crt and any legacy chain references from lb-prod-east-01.corplabs.internal. Configuration change approved by Robert Fielding (rfielding).

Validate trust from multiple client paths (tested from 10.42.18.97 in Arlington and 10.55.6.203 in Denver) and directly from the F5 configuration (tmsh show sys crypto cert-chain) to confirm no expired intermediate is presented. Maria Chen (mchen) and jparker confirmed HTTPS access restored without warnings from WORKSTATION-MC-4082 and WORKSTATION-DT-7761.

Add chain-level monitoring for the LB-served path on lb-prod-east-01 in the cert-monitor dashboard, covering both leaf and intermediate expiry for svc-internal, and require post-deployment evidence capture (automated openssl chain validation) for the active certificate bundle after every renewal job. Monitoring rule created by dtran (E-60215) and assigned to the Arlington infrastructure team.
agent_questions: Please confirm whether clients are failing on certificate expiry only or also reporting chain trust issues from the load balancer endpoint for svc-internal.corplabs.internal. Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) reported both browser warnings and API integration failures from host 10.42.18.97. Can the network team (cc: Robert Fielding, rfielding@corplabs.com) verify the full chain presented by lb-prod-east-01 on the svc-internal virtual server?

title: Expired TLS certificate caused internal service TLS outage
description: Internal users and service integrations reported TLS warnings and failed connections when accessing the Internal Web Service (https://internal-web.corplabs.internal) through the F5 load balancer from the Arlington office. The issue was initially reported by Maria Delgado (mdelgado, emp ID E-40291) on the Platform Engineers Slack channel. The application remained unavailable to some internal consumers after certificate-related alerts, but the available troubleshooting data did not consistently show an expired certificate at the time of review and the team could not confirm whether the issue was isolated to one client path or load balancer partition. Affected workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD (IP 10.22.47.88) was used to reproduce the browser warning.
observed_errors: automation job error: access denied when writing LB config
root_cause: Insufficient evidence to confirm a certificate expiration outage. The incident may have involved a transient or path-specific load balancer certificate presentation issue, but diagnostic access gaps and incomplete monitoring history prevented confirmation.
resolution_steps: Capture fresh certificate and chain checks from each affected client path at the time symptoms recur, including the exact VIP (10.22.1.50) and hostname (internal-web.corplabs.internal) used. Ensure checks are run from both the Arlington and Denver office subnets to cover the paths reported by mdelgado and rpatel.

Obtain access to the relevant F5 configuration partition (partition-internal-web on LB-EAST-01) or engage the load balancer team to export the active certificate and chain bindings for the impacted virtual server serving VIP 10.22.1.50. Contact Kevin Ostrowski (kostrowski@corplabs.com) to coordinate access restoration.

Increase retention and coverage for certificate renewal and LB deployment logs (minimum 90-day retention) so future incidents can confirm whether the served chain changed during the event. Ensure CertMonitor alerts for internal-web.corplabs.internal are routed to the Platform Engineers distribution list.

If symptoms recur, escalate immediately to the load balancer team for live path comparison before the condition clears. Assign to kostrowski or the on-call platform engineer and include diagnostic captures from both Arlington and Denver office client paths.
agent_questions: Hi Maria — please confirm whether users are seeing certificate date warnings at the service URL https://internal-web.corplabs.internal and whether dependent internal API calls through internal-api-gateway are failing with TLS handshake errors. Also, can you verify from your workstation WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD whether the issue persists? — Kevin Ostrowski (kostrowski@corplabs.com)

title: Internal DNS names failing to resolve from corporate resolver
description: Internal users and dependent services were unable to reliably reach several corp.local resources, including internal-portal.corp.local and inventory-api.corp.local, because hostname lookups through the corporate DNS resolver (dns-resolver-01.corp.local, 10.20.1.10) were returning different answers than expected. Reports originated from the Austin office, initially filed by Marcus Delgado (EMP-40821) after multiple teams noticed intermittent failures reaching internal endpoints by name following a recent infrastructure migration on 2026-05-09. The issue affected service connectivity across multiple internal applications including service-discovery. Workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD belonging to Marcus was among the first clients to surface NXDOMAIN responses. Initial reports suggested a resolver problem, but the current incident required validation of the internal DNS data and resolver path before proceeding.
root_cause: Outdated A records remained published in the authoritative internal DNS zone for the impacted corp.local hostnames, causing all resolvers to return retired internal addresses.
resolution_steps: Update the affected authoritative corp.local zone records on ns1-internal.corp.local and ns2-internal.corp.local so each hostname points to the current internal service address: internal-portal.corp.local → 10.20.50.20, inventory-api.corp.local → 10.20.50.22. Changes applied by Raj Okonkwo (rokonkwo).

Increment the zone serial from 2026050801 to 2026051001 and reload the internal DNS zone via rndc reload corp.local on both authoritative servers ns1-internal.corp.local and ns2-internal.corp.local to republish the corrected records.

Re-test lookups through the corporate resolver dns-resolver-01.corp.local (10.20.1.10) and directly against the authoritative servers to confirm both now return the current addresses (10.20.50.20 for internal-portal.corp.local, 10.20.50.22 for inventory-api.corp.local). Validated from WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.20.44.112) and the Austin monitoring probe. Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) confirmed application connectivity by hostname for internal-portal and inventory-api is fully restored.
agent_questions: Comparing affected corp.local lookups between the corporate resolver (dns-resolver-01.corp.local / 10.20.1.10) and authoritative DNS servers (ns1-internal.corp.local, ns2-internal.corp.local) now. Need to confirm whether failures are stale answers at the resolver or missing records in the internal zone. Running nslookup and dig queries from WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.20.44.112) as reported by Marcus Delgado, and cross-referencing with queries from the monitoring host. — Priya Nair, Network Engineering

title: Intermittent NXDOMAIN for internal host 'app-db.internal' from one client subnet
description: Users on the 10.20.30.0/24 internal subnet at the Denver office reported intermittent inability to reach the internal application database host app-db.internal under corp.local, while teams on other networks (e.g., 10.20.40.0/24) reported mixed results. The initial report came from Maria Castillo (emp ID E-20487) who noticed that her workstation WORKSTATION-MC-7741 could not connect to internal services that depend on name resolution. The failure affected access to internal services used by the Internal Apps group, but the reporting context was limited and did not confirm whether the issue was caused by missing DNS data, stale resolver answers, or client path differences. Diagnostics focused on comparing resolver behavior with the authoritative internal DNS service and checking whether cache handling changed the outcome.
root_cause: Suspected misconfiguration or instability in the corporate resolver path for the internal zone caused intermittent SERVFAIL responses even though the authoritative corp.local records were healthy.
resolution_steps: Escalate to the DNS or network infrastructure team (contact: Raj Patel, rpatel, phone 512-555-0173) to review conditional forwarding, recursion behavior, and resolver health for the affected internal zone path on resolver 10.20.30.2 serving the Denver 10.20.30.0/24 subnet.

Capture resolver logs on 10.20.30.2 and compare behavior on the impacted resolver against a known-good corporate resolver (e.g., 10.20.40.2) during repeated test queries for app-db.internal and other corp.local hostnames, documenting SERVFAIL frequency and forwarding latency.

As an interim workaround, direct affected clients or dependent services to a known-good internal resolver (10.20.40.2) where permitted — Maria Castillo (mccastillo) on WORKSTATION-MC-7741 and other impacted users on 10.20.30.0/24 should update their DNS settings accordingly — then retest hostname resolution and application connectivity to app-db.internal (expected A record 10.50.10.22).
agent_questions: Please confirm the DNS resolver IP used by a client on 10.20.30.0/24 (e.g., Maria Castillo's workstation at 10.20.30.114) and whether dig for app-db.internal returns NXDOMAIN consistently from that subnet while succeeding from a known-good subnet such as 10.20.40.0/24. If possible, run the test from WORKSTATION-MC-7741 and share the output. You can reach me at dns-ops@corplabs.com or contact Raj Patel (rpatel) on the network team for assistance.

title: Internal hostname fails to resolve — stale A record in internal DNS
description: Internal users in the Portland office were trying to reach corp.local services by hostname, but some systems continued to fail name resolution even though others reported successful lookups. The issue was initially reported by Maria Chen (emp ID EMP-40218) via the monitoring-dashboard, noting that her workstation could not resolve app.example.internal or svc-registry.corp.local. The problem affected access to internal endpoints such as service-discovery and application dependencies, with symptoms most visible on clients that had recently changed networks or resumed from long-running sessions. Additional reports came in from developer Raj Patel (raj.patel@corplabs.com) whose machine WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RP also failed lookups intermittently. The incident needed DNS validation to determine whether the problem was in the central DNS infrastructure or limited to local resolver behavior on affected systems.
observed_errors: Application error: unable to resolve host
root_cause: No fault was found in the central internal DNS service; suspected client-side DNS caching, local network settings, or an already-cleared transient issue caused the earlier hostname resolution failures.
resolution_steps: Have affected users flush local DNS cache and renew network configuration on impacted endpoints or application hosts. Maria Chen (WORKSTATION-PC-MC, 10.22.47.113) ran ipconfig /flushdns and ipconfig /renew; Raj Patel (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RP, 10.22.48.86) reconnected to the Portland office VPN, which refreshed his DNS settings.

Verify the affected systems are using the expected corporate DNS servers (10.20.1.5 and 10.20.1.6) and not stale or alternate resolver settings. Both Maria Chen's and Raj Patel's endpoints were confirmed pointing to the correct resolvers after remediation. Agent dmorales validated via ipconfig /all output collected from each user.

Retest hostname resolution and application access from affected endpoints; if the issue persists, collect client-side DNS diagnostics for endpoint-focused follow-up. Post-fix nslookup app.example.internal from both WORKSTATION-PC-MC and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RP returned 10.50.12.40 successfully. Internal-app-service and monitoring-dashboard confirmed accessible by hostname from both endpoints. No further failures reported; ticket closed.

title: Cannot connect to Corporate Wi-Fi
description: Several managed laptops on the 4th floor of the Birmingham office could see and join the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-5G), but users including Rachel Whitfield (r.whitfield@corplabs.com) and Marcus Okonkwo were either denied access during EAP-TLS sign-in or left without usable network connectivity after attempting to connect. The issue appeared on a subset of corporate devices (approximately 6 endpoints) rather than across the whole wireless environment and prevented affected users from working normally on office Wi-Fi. Ticket raised by network liaison Priya Nair (EMP-40821).
observed_errors: RADIUS: Access-Reject due to certificate validation failure
root_cause: A subset of managed endpoints had stale or missing corporate Wi-Fi profile and trust settings, causing NAC policy rejection during 802.1X authentication.
resolution_steps: Re-enroll the current corporate Wi-Fi profile on all six affected devices (including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RW and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MO) via Intune forced sync to restore the expected CorpNet-5G SSID, trust chain, and renewed EAP-TLS client certificate configuration.

Force device compliance check-in for each endpoint and confirm the endpoints meet the NAC posture requirements for corporate wireless access; verify updated status in the Intune compliance dashboard and clear any 'Non-Compliant' flags for the Birmingham 4th-floor device group.

Validate successful 802.1X authentication and correct VLAN 120 network policy assignment by reconnecting test devices (WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-RW — user r.whitfield, and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MO — user m.okonkwo) to Corporate Wi-Fi and confirming full network connectivity with Priya Nair and affected users.
agent_questions: Hi Priya — please confirm whether the Wi-Fi failure is affecting multiple users on the Birmingham 4th-floor area and whether devices connect to the CorpNet-5G SSID but fail during 802.1X/EAP-TLS authentication rather than showing no signal. Could you also share the hostnames or MAC addresses of two or three affected machines so we can cross-reference RADIUS logs?

title: Intermittent disconnects from Corporate Wi-Fi
description: Users in the Portland office (Building C, 3rd floor) reported that managed Windows 10 laptops could join the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (CorpNet-5G) but were repeatedly dropped shortly after connecting, interrupting access to internal applications such as Salesforce and the corporate intranet. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (EMP-40291) around 19:15 UTC on 2026-05-11 and quickly confirmed by several other Sales team members on the same floor. Reports were concentrated to that single location and a narrow time window rather than all wireless users globally. Some users, including Derek Holloway, could reconnect briefly before being disconnected again within 2–5 minutes.
observed_errors: No IP address assigned after join
root_cause: Wireless access point or controller radio instability in the affected area caused repeated client deauthentication and session drops after otherwise successful Wi-Fi authentication.
resolution_steps: Escalate to the wireless infrastructure team (network engineer Raj Kapoor, rkapoor@corplabs.com) to remediate the unstable APs AP-PDX-3F-04 and AP-PDX-3F-06 or controller radio conditions affecting the Portland Building C 3rd floor.

Remove or restart the affected APs (AP-PDX-3F-04 and AP-PDX-3F-06) from service as needed and correct the underlying controller or RF issue on WLC-PDX-01.corp.internal causing repeated deauth events. Raj Kapoor disabled both APs and rebalanced 3rd-floor clients to adjacent healthy APs while scheduling hardware replacement.

Verify clients in the affected Portland 3rd-floor location can stay associated and maintain normal network access without repeated disconnects. Confirmed with Maria Chen (mchen), Derek Holloway (dholloway), and Priya Nair (pnair) that their laptops maintained stable Wi-Fi connectivity for over 30 minutes after the AP remediation, with no further deauth events observed in controller logs.
agent_questions: We confirmed the controller certificate on WLC-PDX-01.corp.internal was renewed last week, but some devices are still failing 802.1X. I checked with Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) and Derek Holloway (dholloway) who are both affected. Please confirm whether the affected Sales laptops — for example WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (10.42.18.77) and WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-DH (10.42.18.83) — can join the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID and whether they show no internet or no IP after connecting.

title: Multiple users cannot connect to Corporate Wi-Fi
description: A small number of employees in the Charlotte office reported they could not use the Corporate Wi-Fi SSID (corp-employee) on managed devices. Users including Maria Delgado (mdelgado, EMP-40821) and Kevin Tran (ktran, EMP-40956) saw connection prompts fail, while others reported they connected briefly but still had no reliable network access or IP assignment. The issue was intermittent and limited in scope — affecting roughly 4–5 users on the 3rd floor — making it difficult to determine whether the problem was with the endpoint configuration, wireless authentication via 802.1X/RADIUS, or local wireless infrastructure on the Cisco WLC.
root_cause: Insufficient evidence to confirm whether the primary cause was endpoint Wi-Fi profile inconsistency, intermittent NAC rejection, or short-lived wireless infrastructure instability.
resolution_steps: Capture fresh logs from an actively failing device (prioritize WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-KT or pnair's endpoint), including Wi-Fi profile state, EAP certificate validity, and exact connection timestamps, if the issue recurs. Contact Kevin Tran (ktran@corplabs.com, ext. 4-7823) or Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) to coordinate log collection.

Monitor NAC/RADIUS and controller events on the Charlotte 3rd-floor east-wing APs (AP-CLT-3E-01, AP-CLT-3E-02) during the next reported failure window to correlate authentication results with local AP behavior. Network team lead Rachel Owens (rowens) to set up enhanced logging on the WLC for the affected AP group.

Provide interim user guidance to affected employees (mdelgado, ktran, pnair) to retry after forgetting and rejoining the corp-employee SSID, or move to a nearby coverage area on the 3rd floor west wing while additional evidence is gathered. For mdelgado's device, the expired certificate was renewed and the Wi-Fi profile was re-pushed to v2.4 — confirm stable connectivity at next check-in.
agent_questions: Please confirm whether affected users such as Maria Delgado (mdelgado) and Kevin Tran (ktran) are all failing on the corp-employee SSID and whether their devices show an authentication failure immediately after joining or only after they briefly connect. If possible, capture the exact hostname (e.g. WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD or WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-KT) and client IP of a failing device so we can trace the RADIUS session.

title: BitLocker not enabling
description: I was trying to bring a company-managed Windows 11 laptop (hostname: WORKSTATION-DELL-MR) into encryption compliance, but Company Portal continued to show the device as noncompliant for disk encryption. The device is assigned to me (Marcus Reeves, emp ID EMP-40821) and is located at our Portland office. Local BitLocker status indicated encryption prerequisites were available — TPM 2.0 was present and initialized — yet the device was not reporting a usable recovery key to support. I contacted our desktop team at endpoint-support@corplabs.com but the device remained blocked from meeting corporate security requirements because the encryption policy appeared targeted but was not applying successfully to complete compliant BitLocker protection.
observed_errors: Intune: No recovery key found for device
TPM initialization error during protector creation (reported during enablement step)
root_cause: Intune disk encryption policy assignment/applicability failure prevented the endpoint from receiving and enforcing the required BitLocker configuration, leaving recovery key escrow unavailable and the device noncompliant.
resolution_steps: Reviewed the device's Intune policy targeting and applicability details for WORKSTATION-DELL-MR (enrolled user: mreeves). Identified that the assignment filter on the 'Corp-BitLocker-Win11' encryption profile excluded the device's enrollment category. Corrected the assignment filter to include the 'Corporate Laptops - Portland' device group, resolving the conflict preventing the encryption profile from applying.

Triggered a fresh device sync on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR after the policy assignment change (initiated via Intune portal at 2026-05-12T07:28:00Z) and confirmed the endpoint received the active disk encryption configuration 'Corp-BitLocker-Win11' without assignment errors. Profile status for mreeves updated to 'Succeeded'.

Forced BitLocker policy evaluation on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR using Invoke-GPUpdate and a manual Intune sync cycle, verified recovery key escrow became visible to support in the Intune BitLocker recovery keys blade under mreeves, and confirmed the device returned to compliant status in both Company Portal and the Intune Device Compliance dashboard. Marcus Reeves (EMP-40821) was notified at mreeves@corplabs.com that the device is now fully compliant.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, thanks for reporting this. Please confirm what you see in Company Portal and BitLocker status on WORKSTATION-DELL-MR. We need to verify whether encryption is off, whether a recovery key appears in Intune for your device (enrolled under username mreeves), and whether provisioning showed any TPM-related failure. Also, can you confirm the device IP address so we can cross-reference Intune enrollment logs?

title: BitLocker not enabled and recovery key not escrowed on corporate device
description: A corporate Windows laptop assigned to Marco Pellegrini (employee ID EMP-40291) was still showing as noncompliant for disk encryption in Intune, even though the device appeared to have BitLocker components present locally. The main support concern was that no recovery key was available in the management service for recovery operations. The device hostname is WORKSTATION-SALES-MP and it connects from the Milan office. Marco needed the endpoint to meet corporate encryption compliance, but the current state could not be validated end to end from the available diagnostics.
root_cause: Recovery key escrow or recovery key visibility in the management service could not be confirmed despite healthy TPM state and successful policy delivery; exact failure point remains unresolved.
resolution_steps: Collected BitLocker and MDM logs from WORKSTATION-SALES-MP (hostname confirmed with Marco Pellegrini, EMP-40291) to determine whether recovery key backup attempts were being generated successfully. Logs were exported from C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\IntuneManagementExtension\Logs and the BitLocker-API event channel.

Opened escalation (ESC-20260512-0047) to the endpoint management service team — assigned to Lena Richter (lrichter@corplabs.com) — to review escrow ingestion and key visibility for WORKSTATION-SALES-MP in the EMEA tenant. Included MDM log excerpts showing KeyBackupError 0x87D1FDE8 and the pending BackupRecoveryPasswordToAAD task entries.

Maintained WORKSTATION-SALES-MP under monitoring and rechecked for recovery key appearance in the Intune console after additional sync cycles (three cycles over 90 minutes) before closing or pursuing further remediation. Marco Pellegrini was advised via marco.pellegrini@corplabs.com to keep the device connected to the corporate network in Milan and not to restart until escrow confirmation was received.
agent_questions: We confirmed Intune shows device WORKSTATION-SALES-MP (serial enrolled under mpellegrini) as noncompliant for encryption. Can you confirm whether this is the same corporate laptop and whether any recent enrollment or reset activity occurred before the compliance failure appeared? The device last checked in from IP 10.42.17.88 and is associated with user Marco Pellegrini in the Sales group.

title: Device noncompliant for BitLocker — Intune shows conflicting state
description: User Marcus Delgado (EMP-40291) from the Arlington sales office brought his company-managed Windows 11 Enterprise endpoint (hostname: WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD) forward for encryption compliance review because Company Portal listed disk encryption as noncompliant. During troubleshooting, local checks on the device (IP 10.42.17.88) showed BitLocker prerequisites were in place and Intune policy delivery looked normal, but support still could not locate an escrowed recovery key for the machine in Microsoft Endpoint Manager. The lack of escrowed key visibility prevented standard recovery support and kept the device from satisfying corporate compliance requirements under the Sales user group encryption baseline.
observed_errors: Device marked noncompliant for encryption in Device Compliance
root_cause: BitLocker recovery key escrow failed or never completed for the existing protector even though TPM readiness and Intune policy delivery were functioning normally.
resolution_steps: Verified that WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD (user: Marcus Delgado, mdelgado, EMP-40291) was receiving the correct disk encryption policy (Sales-Encryption-Baseline) via Intune and confirmed the existing TPM 2.0-backed protector was healthy before changing any key material.

Rotated the BitLocker recovery key on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD using 'manage-bde -protectors -delete C: -type RecoveryPassword' followed by 'Add-BitLockerKeyProtector -MountPoint C: -RecoveryPasswordProtector', then initiated a fresh backup of the new key to the Azure AD management service via 'BackupToAAD-BitLockerKeyProtector'.

Ran a follow-up Intune device sync on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD, confirmed the new recovery key was visible to support in the Endpoint Manager recovery key blade, and validated that Device Compliance Service updated the encryption compliance status to compliant for mdelgado's device. Notified Marcus Delgado at mdelgado@corplabs.com that the issue was resolved.
agent_questions: Hi Marcus, this is Priya Nair from desktop support. Could you please confirm whether BitLocker shows any protectors locally on WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD by running 'manage-bde -protectors -get C:' in an elevated prompt? Also, can you check whether a recovery key is visible in Endpoint Manager for this laptop under your device listing (mdelgado@corplabs.com)?

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership
title: Access denied to Finance shared drive for user jane.doe
description: I'm Jane Doe (employee ID FIN-20481) and I was trying to open the Finance shared drive from my usual mapped network drive (F:) on my workstation WORKSTATION-PC-JD as well as directly through \\fs01\Finance, but both returned Access Denied (0x5) with intermittent credential prompts. The issue was affecting access to Finance files needed for daily reconciliation work on the SMB file server. I contacted my colleague Mark Chen (ext. 4127) who confirmed he could still access the share without issues, so initial checks suggested the problem was limited to my access path or session rather than a broader department-wide outage. My IP address is 10.42.17.89 and I'm based in the Arlington office.
root_cause: User was connecting through a stale or retired Finance share path, so the mapped drive was targeting the wrong UNC location and producing Access Denied behavior despite valid access membership.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the approved current UNC path for the Finance shared drive (\\fs01\Finance) with the file services configuration and validated that \\fs01-old\Finance was officially retired during the Q1 2026 server consolidation managed by Kevin Ostrowski.

Removed the stale mapped drive (F: → \\fs01-old\Finance) on WORKSTATION-PC-JD using 'net use F: /delete', cleared cached credentials via Credential Manager for user jdoe, and remapped the drive to the current Finance share path with 'net use F: \\fs01\Finance /persistent:yes'.

Retested direct UNC access (\\fs01\Finance) and mapped-drive access (F:) with Jane Doe on WORKSTATION-PC-JD (10.42.17.89) and verified the Finance folder — including subfolders Reconciliation and Reports — opened without further Access Denied prompts or credential challenges.
agent_questions: Hi Jane, thanks for reporting this. I'm Kevin Ostrowski from the file services team. Could you please try opening \\fs01\Finance directly from Windows Explorer on WORKSTATION-PC-JD instead of using the mapped F: drive, and confirm whether you still receive Access Denied or a credential prompt? Also, please verify you're logged in as jdoe@corplabs.internal and not using any cached or alternate credentials. You can reach me at kostrowski@corplabs.com if you need to follow up offline.

category_name: Shared Drive Access Denied & Group Membership

Also, can you confirm you're logged in as rnguyen on your workstation?

Advise the user Rosa Garcia (rgarcia, ext 4-7823) of the escalation to Tier 2 and provide ticket reference INC-SDA-V0030. title: Integration Gateway API timeouts causing delayed data sync
description: During the overnight CustomerSync batch window (02:00–04:30 UTC), the Integration Gateway at gw-prod-west-02.integrations.corplabs.internal began timing out on calls to the downstream customer API endpoint /api/v2/customers/sync, causing delayed customer data updates and failed sync jobs for dependent reporting workflows used by the Portland operations team. The issue was reported by Marcus Delgado (Application Support lead) and was concentrated during the scheduled batch period rather than throughout the day. Operations confirmed the external service was reachable from WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MD (10.42.18.77) but responses were too slow for the integration to complete within its configured 30-second timeout.
root_cause: Elevated downstream API latency during the overnight processing window caused authenticated requests to exceed the Integration Gateway timeout threshold, resulting in timeout errors and failed batch synchronization jobs.
resolution_steps: Correlated batch-job failures with Integration Gateway latency metrics on gw-prod-west-02.integrations.corplabs.internal and downstream API traces (e.g., trx-8a3f19c7) to confirm the slowdown was external to gateway authentication and scheduling; p95 latency spiked from 4.2s to 52.1s during the 02:00–04:30 UTC window.

Escalated the incident to the downstream API provider (ticket ref EXT-CUS-20260513) with timestamps, trace samples (trx-8a3f19c7), and timeout evidence from the affected processing window. Escalation handled by Reiko Nakamura and acknowledged by downstream support contact Priya Venkatesh at priya.venkatesh@customerapi.io.

Applied a temporary timeout increase from 30s to 90s and tuned retry/backoff settings (exponential backoff with jitter, max 5 retries) on the Integration Gateway configuration for the CustomerSync Service endpoint to reduce failed overnight jobs until downstream performance stabilized. Change approved by team lead Marcus Delgado.

Re-ran the 47 affected synchronization jobs via the CustomerSync Service admin console and verified customer data updates completed successfully (all 312 records synced, 0 failures) after downstream API latency returned to normal baseline (~4s p95) at approximately 06:15 UTC on 2026-05-13.
agent_questions: We found repeated 504 timeouts during the overnight CustomerSync batch (02:00–04:30 UTC on 2026-05-13) on gw-prod-west-02.integrations.corplabs.internal and a failed token refresh event in the same window. Reviewing the Integration Gateway audit trail under service account svc-custsync, we see 47 consecutive timeout entries. Can you confirm whether any token rotation or downstream API credential change occurred before the sync delays started? Please reach out to me at r.nakamura@corplabs.com or ext. 4-7831 if you need to discuss offline. — Reiko Nakamura, Integration Support

title: Integration Gateway API timeouts
description: Scheduled CustomerDataSync jobs through the Integration Gateway began failing during the overnight processing window on 2026-05-13, preventing timely customer record updates for the backend-syncers team and creating a backlog in the gateway worker queue. The issue was initially reported by Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) from the Austin office, who noticed that sync jobs for the CustomerDataSyncApp were timing out. root_cause: The overnight sync workload exceeded the downstream API's rate or quota limits, leading to 429 throttling responses and retry exhaustion that appeared as integration timeout failures.
resolution_steps: Confirmed the throttling pattern in gateway and downstream logs (batch-20260514-0115) and reduced request concurrency for the affected overnight batch jobs from 50 to 10 concurrent workers on the Integration Gateway EKS deployment in us-east-1.

Implemented stronger pacing, exponential backoff (initial delay 2s, max 60s, jitter enabled), and batch spreading on the Integration Gateway to stay within the downstream API rate limits of 100 requests/minute. Configuration was updated by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) and reviewed by Priya Nair.

Requested a quota review or temporary limit increase from the downstream API owner (contacted via api-support@partnerservices.net) where supported, referencing the CustomerDataSyncApp integration and projected batch volumes.

Monitored the next batch cycle (2026-05-15T01:15:00Z) via the Monitoring System and verified sync jobs completed without retry exhaustion or timeout symptoms. Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) confirmed all customer records were synced successfully and the backlog was fully cleared.
agent_questions: We are seeing 401 Unauthorized and 504 timeout errors during the scheduled sync window for the CustomerDataSyncApp running on pod cluster us-east-1.
